catalog.name: Accounts Payable calculations
catalog.description: Every formula, algorithm, rounding rule and worked example of the accounts payable domain, in a structured form a rebuild can test against: the sign conventions and the document totals, the three dates and the accounting date algorithm, the choice of the supplier bank account, duplicate bill detection, the payment term distribution with its instalments, its balance line and its early payment discount, the account selection rules, the amount in words and the cheque fill rule, cash rounding, the defaulting of a bill line, partial deductibility and its private-share entries, quick encoding, the abnormal amount and date detection, cheque numbering, the cheque stub with its allocation and its paging, the invoice analysis figures, the intercompany clearing amounts, the precision reference, the purchase journal dashboard numbers, the numbering starting pattern and the arithmetic that groups incoming files into bills.
catalog.authored_from: docs/domains/accounts-payable/calculations.md, with the ledger effects of docs/domains/accounts-payable/accounting-effects.md and the rule identifiers of docs/domains/accounts-payable/business-rules.md

records.name: The direction sign of a purchase document
records.purpose: Bridges the positive commercial quantities written on a document and the signed balances the ledger needs, by giving every document type a sign that multiplies every amount derived from it.

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the stored type of the document, one of the miscellaneous-entry type, `in_invoice` (vendor bill), `in_refund` (vendor credit note), `in_receipt` (purchase receipt), `out_invoice` (customer invoice), `out_refund` (customer credit note) and `out_receipt` (sales receipt)
operands.constraints: always set; a document always has exactly one type

preconditions.condition: The document has a type.
preconditions.otherwise: No amount of the document can be signed and no line balance can be derived.

procedure: Read the document type.
Answer plus one when the type is the miscellaneous-entry type or one of the outbound types, that is `in_invoice`, `out_refund` or `in_receipt`.
Answer minus one for every other type, that is `out_invoice`, `in_refund` or `out_receipt`.
records.formula:
direction_sign = +1   when the document type is a miscellaneous entry, or an outbound type (in_invoice, out_refund, in_receipt)
direction_sign = −1   otherwise (out_invoice, in_refund, out_receipt)

rounding.what: Nothing; the direction sign is an exact whole number.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: direction sign
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a bare sign of value plus one or minus one
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; recomputed wherever a signed amount is derived, and never shown to the user.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is plus one, so an expense line is a debit and the payable term line is a credit.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is minus one, so the expense line is a credit and the payable term line is a debit.

edge_cases.case: The document is a purchase receipt.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is plus one, exactly as for a vendor bill.

edge_cases.case: The document is a miscellaneous entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is plus one, and the signed total is taken as an absolute value when the totals are derived.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill
worked_examples.narrative: The vendor bill is an outbound type, so the direction sign is plus one and every expense line carries a positive balance.

worked_examples.description: A vendor credit note
worked_examples.narrative: The vendor credit note is not in the outbound list, so the direction sign is minus one and the expense line becomes a credit.

records.name: The balance of a document line from its amount in document currency
records.purpose: Turns the amount a line carries in the document currency into the signed company-currency balance that the ledger stores, which is what makes an expense line of a bill a debit and the payable term line a credit.

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the document type, by the direction-sign rule
operands.constraints: plus one or minus one

operands.name: line amount in document currency
operands.source: the amount in currency of the line, itself the unit price multiplied by the quantity less the discount
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: document rate
operands.unit_or_currency: a ratio of document-currency units per company-currency unit
operands.source: the currency rate stored on the document, named `invoice_currency_rate`
operands.constraints: strictly positive; one when the document currency equals the company currency

preconditions.condition: The document rate is known and not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The balance cannot be derived and the amount is treated as zero by the routines that divide by the rate.

preconditions.condition: The line is not a presentation line, that is not a section, a subsection or a note.
preconditions.otherwise: The line carries no amount in currency and no balance at all.

procedure: Take the direction sign of the document.
Multiply the direction sign by the amount the line carries in the document currency.
Divide the product by the document rate to express it in the company currency.
Round the quotient to the company currency and store it as the line balance, a positive value being a debit and a negative value a credit.
records.formula: line_balance = direction_sign × line_amount_in_document_currency ÷ document_rate

rounding.what: The resulting balance.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency, which is 0.01 for a currency with two decimal places.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the direction sign and the division by the document rate, before the balance is stored.

result.name: line balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the journal item as its balance, and shown split into a debit column and a credit column.

edge_cases.case: The document currency equals the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The document rate is one and the balance equals the signed amount in currency.

edge_cases.case: The line amount in document currency is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance is zero and the line is neither a debit nor a credit.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is minus one, so an expense line of positive amount produces a negative balance, that is a credit.

edge_cases.case: The line is a payable term line.
edge_cases.outcome: Its amount in currency is the counterpart of the other lines, so on a vendor bill it is negative and the balance is a credit.

worked_examples.description: An expense line of a vendor bill in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: One unit at one hundred euros on a bill: plus one multiplied by 100.00 divided by one is a balance of 100.00, a debit on the expense account.

worked_examples.description: The payable term line of the same bill, taxes included
worked_examples.narrative: The counterpart carries the negated total, so its balance is −120.00, a credit of one hundred and twenty euros on the payable account.

records.name: The untaxed total of a purchase document in the document currency
records.purpose: Produces the figure shown as the untaxed amount of the document, which is the base on which taxes are computed and the amount an early payment discount reduces in the two modes that spare the tax.

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the document type
operands.constraints: plus one on a vendor bill

operands.name: amount in currency of each product line
operands.source: the lines whose display type is `product`
operands.constraints: signed as stored on the line

operands.name: amount in currency of each rounding line
operands.source: the cash-rounding line, when a cash rounding rule with the add-a-rounding-line strategy applies
operands.constraints: may be positive or negative

operands.name: amount in currency of each non-deductible product line
operands.source: the lines whose display type is `non_deductible_product`
operands.constraints: negative on a vendor bill

preconditions.condition: The document is invoice-like, that is one of the six invoice and receipt types.
preconditions.otherwise: The untaxed total is not meaningful and is left at zero.

procedure: Select the lines whose display type is a product line, a rounding line or a non-deductible product line.
Sum their amounts in the document currency.
Multiply the sum by the direction sign.
Round the product to the document currency and store it as the untaxed amount.
records.formula: amount_untaxed = direction_sign × Σ amount_in_currency over product, rounding and non-deductible-product lines

rounding.what: The untaxed total.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.step: Once, on the signed sum, after every line amount has itself been rounded to the document currency.

result.name: untaxed amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document as its untaxed amount and displayed in the totals block above the taxes.

edge_cases.case: A rounding line carries a tax distribution.
edge_cases.outcome: That rounding line is counted in the tax total instead of the untaxed total.

edge_cases.case: A private share reduces the deductible expense.
edge_cases.outcome: The non-deductible product line is negative and lowers the untaxed total accordingly, while the aggregate private-share line restores it on the private share account.

edge_cases.case: The document has only presentation lines.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is empty and the untaxed amount is zero; posting is refused for a document with no accountable line.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is minus one, so the untaxed amount is still shown as a positive figure while every underlying balance is a credit.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill of three thousand euros before tax
worked_examples.narrative: One product line of 3 000.00 on a bill: the direction sign is plus one, so the untaxed amount is 3 000.00.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill carrying a private share of one quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The non-deductible product line of −25.00 is part of the untaxed base, so the untaxed amount reads 75.00 while the aggregate private-share line of +25.00 sits in the tax-free part of the document.

records.name: The tax total of a purchase document in the document currency
records.purpose: Produces the tax figure of the totals block, which is what the company may reclaim as input tax once the non-deductible share has been carved out.

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the document type
operands.constraints: plus one on a vendor bill

operands.name: amount in currency of each tax line
operands.source: the lines whose display type is `tax`
operands.constraints: produced by the tax engine from the base lines

operands.name: amount in currency of each non-deductible tax line
operands.source: the lines whose display type is `non_deductible_tax`
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill, since it moves tax to the private share account

operands.name: amount in currency of each tax-bearing rounding line
operands.source: a cash-rounding line that carries a tax distribution
operands.constraints: may be positive or negative

preconditions.condition: The tax engine has recomputed the tax lines from the current base lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax total is stale and the balance check refuses the write.

procedure: Select the lines whose display type is a tax line, a non-deductible tax line or a rounding line that carries a tax distribution.
Sum their amounts in the document currency.
Multiply the sum by the direction sign.
Round the product to the document currency and store it as the tax amount.
records.formula: amount_tax = direction_sign × Σ amount_in_currency over tax, non-deductible-tax and tax-bearing rounding lines

rounding.what: The tax total.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.step: Once, on the signed sum of the already rounded tax lines.

result.name: tax amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document as its tax amount and displayed as the tax line of the totals block.

edge_cases.case: The document carries no tax at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is empty and the tax amount is zero, so the total equals the untaxed amount.

edge_cases.case: A private share is present.
edge_cases.outcome: The deductible tax line falls by the tax on the negative base and the non-deductible tax line carries the same figure on the private share account, so the tax total of the document is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A cash-rounding line carries a tax distribution.
edge_cases.outcome: Its amount is counted here rather than in the untaxed total.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is minus one and the displayed tax amount is again a positive figure.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill with one purchase tax at twenty per cent
worked_examples.narrative: A base of 100.00 with a purchase tax of twenty per cent gives a tax line of 20.00, and the tax amount of the bill is 20.00.

worked_examples.description: The same bill with a deductibility of seventy-five per cent
worked_examples.narrative: The deductible tax falls to 15.00 and the non-deductible tax line carries 5.00; both are counted, so the tax amount of the bill stays 20.00 and the supplier is still owed the full tax.

records.name: The grand total of a purchase document in the document currency
records.purpose: Produces the amount the company owes the supplier, which is the figure the payment term distributes, the figure duplicate detection compares and the figure the quick encoding total must match.

operands.name: untaxed amount
operands.source: the untaxed total rule
operands.constraints: already signed by the direction sign

operands.name: tax amount
operands.source: the tax total rule
operands.constraints: already signed by the direction sign

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the document type
operands.constraints: plus one on a vendor bill

preconditions.condition: Every line amount has been recomputed in the document currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The total is stale; on an unsaved draft the totals are recomputed from the base lines rather than read from storage.

procedure: Select every product line, rounding line, non-deductible product line, tax line and non-deductible tax line of the document.
Sum their amounts in the document currency.
Multiply the sum by the direction sign.
Round the product to the document currency and store it as the total.
records.formula: amount_total = direction_sign × Σ amount_in_currency over all of the above

rounding.what: The grand total.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.step: Once, on the signed sum of the already rounded line amounts, so that the total always equals the untaxed amount plus the tax amount.

result.name: total amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document as its total and displayed as the last line of the totals block; positive on a vendor bill, because it is what the company owes.

edge_cases.case: The total is strictly negative in the document currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Posting is refused with the message that an invoice with a negative total amount cannot be validated and that a credit note should be created instead.

edge_cases.case: The total is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The document may still be posted, but duplicate detection ignores it, because the second matching case requires a non-zero total.

edge_cases.case: A cash rounding rule applies.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounding line is part of the sum, so the total is already the cash-rounded figure that the payment term distributes.

worked_examples.description: The bill of the payment-term example
worked_examples.narrative: Three thousand euros of goods and six hundred euros of tax give a total of 3 600.00, which is the amount the payment term distributes over its instalments.

worked_examples.description: The bill of the early discount example
worked_examples.narrative: A net of 1 000.00 with a tax of twenty-one per cent gives 210.00 of tax and a total of 1 210.00.

records.name: The residual amount of a purchase document in the document currency
records.purpose: Gives the amount still owed on the document after the payments reconciled against its payable term lines, which drives the payment status, the dashboard figures and the amount proposed when a payment is registered.

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the document type
operands.constraints: plus one on a vendor bill

operands.name: residual in currency of each payment-term line
operands.source: the unreconciled part of each payable term line
operands.constraints: between zero and the line amount in absolute value

preconditions.condition: The document is posted, so that its term lines exist and can be reconciled.
preconditions.otherwise: The residual equals the total and no payment can be registered, since payment registration refuses a document that is not posted.

procedure: Select the lines whose display type is `payment_term`.
Sum the residual amounts they carry in the document currency.
Multiply the sum by the negated direction sign.
Round the product to the document currency and store it as the residual amount.
records.formula: amount_residual = − direction_sign × Σ residual_in_currency over payment-term lines

rounding.what: The residual amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.step: On the signed sum, after each partial reconciliation has been rounded.

result.name: residual amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document and displayed as the amount due; zero when the document is fully paid.

edge_cases.case: The document is fully reconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: Every term line has a residual of zero, so the residual amount is zero and the payment status becomes paid.

edge_cases.case: The document is partly paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The residual amount is the unpaid part and the payment status is partial, which is one of the two statuses the waiting group of the dashboard counts.

edge_cases.case: The document has several instalments and only the first is paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The residual is the sum of the remaining instalments, and the late group counts the document when the earliest unpaid maturity date has passed.

edge_cases.case: The negation makes the residual positive on a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: The term lines are credits, so their residuals are negative and the negated direction sign turns the figure into the positive amount owed.

worked_examples.description: A bill of one hundred and twenty euros on which nothing has been paid
worked_examples.narrative: The single term line still carries its whole credit of −120.00; the negated direction sign gives a residual of 120.00.

worked_examples.description: The same bill after a payment of fifty euros
worked_examples.narrative: Fifty euros have been reconciled, so the residual of the term line is −70.00 and the document shows 70.00 still due.

records.name: The signed untaxed amount of a purchase document in the company currency
records.purpose: Gives the untaxed figure in the ledger's own signing, which is what the analysis report and the reporting layers aggregate across documents of different types.

operands.name: balance of each product line
operands.source: the journal items whose display type is `product`
operands.constraints: a debit is positive on a vendor bill

operands.name: balance of each rounding line
operands.source: the cash-rounding line, when one exists
operands.constraints: may be positive or negative

operands.name: balance of each non-deductible product line
operands.source: the journal items whose display type is `non_deductible_product`
operands.constraints: a credit on a vendor bill

preconditions.condition: The document is stored, so that its journal items carry balances.
preconditions.otherwise: The signed figures are recomputed from the base lines of the draft in memory.

procedure: Select the product lines, the rounding lines and the non-deductible product lines.
Sum their balances in the company currency.
Negate the sum, without applying the direction sign, because the ledger signing is already carried by the balances themselves.
records.formula: amount_untaxed_signed = − Σ balance over product, rounding and non-deductible-product lines

rounding.what: The signed untaxed amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency.
rounding.step: On the negated sum of the already rounded balances.

result.name: signed untaxed amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document and used by the analysis report and the dashboard rather than by the totals block.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: The expense balances are debits, so the negated sum is negative.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The expense balances are credits, so the negated sum is positive.

edge_cases.case: The document currency differs from the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is expressed in the company currency, since it sums balances rather than amounts in currency.

worked_examples.description: A bill of three thousand euros before tax in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The expense line is a debit of 3 000.00, and the negation gives a signed untaxed amount of −3 000.00.

worked_examples.description: A vendor credit note of the same size
worked_examples.narrative: The expense line is a credit of 3 000.00, so the signed untaxed amount is +3 000.00.

records.name: The signed tax amount of a purchase document in the company currency
records.purpose: Gives the tax figure in the ledger's own signing, for the reporting layers that add documents of several types together.

operands.name: balance of each tax line
operands.source: the journal items whose display type is `tax`
operands.constraints: a debit on a vendor bill, because input tax is recoverable

preconditions.condition: The tax lines have been produced by the tax engine.
preconditions.otherwise: The signed tax amount is zero.

procedure: Select the lines whose display type is a tax line, and only those, so that the non-deductible tax line is excluded from this figure.
Sum their balances in the company currency.
Negate the sum.
records.formula: amount_tax_signed = − Σ balance over tax lines

rounding.what: The signed tax amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency.
rounding.step: On the negated sum of the already rounded balances.

result.name: signed tax amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document and used by the reporting layers.

edge_cases.case: The document carries a private share.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the deductible tax lines are summed here, so the signed tax amount reflects the reduced deductible tax and not the tax moved to the private share account.

edge_cases.case: The document carries no tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax balances are credits and the negated sum is positive.

worked_examples.description: A bill with six hundred euros of purchase tax
worked_examples.narrative: The tax line is a debit of 600.00, so the signed tax amount is −600.00.

worked_examples.description: A bill whose deductibility is seventy-five per cent
worked_examples.narrative: The deductible tax line has fallen to 15.00, so the signed tax amount is −15.00; the five euros of non-deductible tax are not counted here.

records.name: The signed grand total of a purchase document in the company currency
records.purpose: Gives the total in the ledger's own signing, negative on a vendor bill because the ledger sees a credit on the payable side; it is the figure the dashboard and the analysis report aggregate.

operands.name: balance of every non-term line
operands.source: every journal item of the document except the payable term lines
operands.constraints: signed as the ledger stores them

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the stored type
operands.constraints: a miscellaneous entry takes the absolute value

preconditions.condition: The document balances, that is the rounded sum of every balance is zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused with the message that the entry is not balanced.

procedure: Select every line of the document whose display type is not `payment_term`.
Sum their balances in the company currency.
Negate the sum.
For a miscellaneous entry, take the absolute value of the negated sum instead of its signed value.
records.formula: amount_total_signed = − Σ balance over all non-term lines      (for a miscellaneous entry: the absolute value)

rounding.what: The signed grand total.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency.
rounding.step: On the negated sum of the already rounded balances.

result.name: signed total amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document; negative on a vendor bill while the displayed total is positive.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: The displayed total is positive, being what the company owes, while the signed total is negative, the ledger seeing a credit on the payable side.

edge_cases.case: The document is a miscellaneous entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute value is taken, so the figure is never negative for that type.

edge_cases.case: The document is in a foreign currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is in the company currency, and the dashboard uses it directly whenever the row's company currency is the target currency.

worked_examples.description: A bill of one hundred and twenty euros including tax
worked_examples.narrative: The expense debit of 100.00 and the tax debit of 20.00 sum to 120.00; the negation gives −120.00, while the displayed total is 120.00.

worked_examples.description: A miscellaneous entry of the same shape
worked_examples.narrative: The absolute value is taken, so the figure is 120.00 rather than −120.00.

records.name: The signed residual amount of a purchase document in the company currency
records.purpose: Gives the outstanding amount in the ledger's own signing, which is what the purchase journal dashboard sums for the waiting and the late groups before negating it for display.

operands.name: residual of each payment-term line
operands.source: the unreconciled part of each payable term line, expressed as a balance
operands.constraints: negative on an unpaid vendor bill

preconditions.condition: The document is posted and carries payable term lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure is zero.

procedure: Select the lines whose display type is `payment_term`.
Sum the residual balances they carry in the company currency, without negating the sum.
records.formula: amount_residual_signed =   Σ residual over payment-term lines

rounding.what: The signed residual amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency.
rounding.step: On the sum of the already rounded partial reconciliations.

result.name: signed residual amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document; summed as-is by the dashboard queries and negated only at display time for a purchase journal.

edge_cases.case: The document is fully paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero and the document leaves the waiting group of the dashboard.

edge_cases.case: The document is an unpaid vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is negative, which is why the purchase card negates the sum so that the amount owed reads as a positive figure.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The term line is a debit, so the figure is positive and reduces the negated dashboard sum.

worked_examples.description: An unpaid bill of one hundred and twenty euros
worked_examples.narrative: The dashboard sums −120.00 and the purchase card negates it, so the card reads one hundred and twenty euros to pay.

worked_examples.description: An unpaid credit note of thirty euros against the same vendor
worked_examples.narrative: The credit note's term line is a debit, so its signed residual is +30.00 and it lowers the negated total on the card to ninety euros.

records.name: Deriving the accounting date of a document from its bill date
records.purpose: Chooses which date the entry hits the ledger on, so that a bill captured late still lands in the period it belongs to while the numbering of the series stays monotonically increasing.

operands.name: bill date
operands.source: the date the supplier issued the document, stored as `invoice_date`
operands.constraints: may be empty on a draft

operands.name: current accounting date
operands.source: the accounting date already on the document, stored as `date`
operands.constraints: may be empty on a brand-new draft

operands.name: today
operands.source: the current date in the reading user's time zone
operands.constraints: always available

preconditions.condition: The accounting date source is not empty, that is the document has a bill date or already has an accounting date.
preconditions.otherwise: If the accounting date is empty it is set to today, and the derivation stops there.

preconditions.condition: The document is invoice-like.
preconditions.otherwise: The same fallback applies: an empty accounting date becomes today and nothing further is computed.

procedure: Take the accounting date source: the bill date when there is one, and the current accounting date otherwise.
If the source is empty, or the document is not invoice-like, set the accounting date to today when it is empty and stop.
If the document is a sale document, answer the source unchanged, the shifting rules applying to sale documents only when a lock date is violated.
Otherwise, and every purchase document takes this path, run the accounting date algorithm over the candidate date.
If the answer differs from the current accounting date, write it, and schedule the recomputation of the line dates and of the document number.
records.formula:
accounting_date_source = bill_date when set, otherwise current accounting date
accounting_date = accounting_date_algorithm( accounting_date_source )   for every purchase document

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the result is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: accounting date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document as `date` and shown as the accounting date; it determines the period, the numbering series and the lock-date checks.

edge_cases.case: The document has neither a bill date nor an accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: The accounting date becomes today.

edge_cases.case: The document is a sale document and no lock date is violated.
edge_cases.outcome: The accounting date is the source unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The derived date equals the current accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is written and no recomputation is scheduled.

edge_cases.case: The derived date differs.
edge_cases.outcome: The line dates and the document number are both scheduled for recomputation, because the number depends on the period.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill captured in the month after its date
worked_examples.narrative: The source is the bill date of 20 August 2026; the purchase branch of the algorithm applies and returns the last day of August, so the bill is numbered in the August series.

worked_examples.description: A brand-new draft with no date at all
worked_examples.narrative: The source is empty, so the accounting date is set to today and no shifting occurs.

records.name: The accounting date of a purchase document in a monthly-resetting numbering series
records.purpose: Keeps a late-captured bill inside the month it belongs to when the journal numbers reset every month, so that the series stays ordered and the tax period is the right one.

operands.name: candidate date
operands.source: the accounting date source, after the lock-date shift has been applied
operands.constraints: never empty at this point

operands.name: today
operands.source: the current date in the user's time zone
operands.constraints: always available

operands.name: number reset period
operands.source: deduced from the highest number already used in the series, or from the last number of the series computed with the relaxed rule when the highest is unknown; one of `month`, `year`, `year_range_month`, `year_range` and `never`
operands.constraints: this record covers the case where the series has no name yet, resets monthly, or resets monthly within a year range

preconditions.condition: The document is a purchase document, that is not a sale document.
preconditions.otherwise: The sale branch of the algorithm applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The numbering series has no name yet, or its reset period is monthly, or it is monthly within a year range.
preconditions.otherwise: The yearly branch or the unchanged-date branch applies.

procedure: Take today in the user's time zone.

Take the highest number already used in this numbering series, or the last number of the series computed with the relaxed rule when the highest is unknown, and deduce the reset period from its grammar.
Apply the lock-date shift first: when a lock date is violated, replace the candidate date by the latest violated lock date plus one day.
Compare the month of today with the month of the candidate date.
When today is in a later month than the candidate date, answer the last day of the month of the candidate date.
Otherwise answer the later of the candidate date and today.
records.formula:
accounting_date = last_day_of_month( d )      when today is in a later month than d
accounting_date = max( d , today )            otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: accounting date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document; determines the numbering period and the lock-date verdict.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date is in the future relative to today.
edge_cases.outcome: Today is not in a later month, so the later of the two is the candidate date itself, which is answered unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date is earlier in the same month as today.
edge_cases.outcome: The later of the two is today, so the entry is dated today.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date is in a month before today's month.
edge_cases.outcome: The last day of that earlier month is answered, so the entry falls in its own period.

edge_cases.case: The series has no number yet.
edge_cases.outcome: The same monthly branch is used, because an unnamed series is treated as monthly.

worked_examples.description: A bill of the previous month captured today
worked_examples.narrative: September is later than August, so the accounting date becomes 31 August 2026 and the bill is numbered in the August series.

worked_examples.description: A bill of the current month captured a few days later
worked_examples.narrative: Today's month equals the bill's month, so the answer is the later of 2 September and 11 September, that is 11 September 2026.

records.name: The accounting date of a purchase document in a yearly-resetting numbering series
records.purpose: Keeps a late-captured bill inside the year it belongs to when the journal numbers reset once a year.

operands.name: candidate date
operands.source: the accounting date source, after the lock-date shift
operands.constraints: never empty at this point

operands.name: today
operands.source: the current date in the user's time zone
operands.constraints: always available

operands.name: number reset period
operands.source: deduced from the highest number of the series
operands.constraints: this record covers the reset period `year`

preconditions.condition: The document is a purchase document.
preconditions.otherwise: The sale branch applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The numbering series resets yearly.
preconditions.otherwise: The monthly branch or the unchanged-date branch applies.

procedure: Take today in the user's time zone.
Deduce the reset period from the highest number of the series and confirm that it is yearly.
Apply the lock-date shift first when a lock date is violated.
Compare the year of today with the year of the candidate date.
When today is in a later year, answer the thirty-first of December of the year of the candidate date.
Otherwise answer the later of the candidate date and today.
records.formula:
accounting_date = 31 December of the year of d      when today is in a later year than d
accounting_date = max( d , today )                 otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: accounting date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date is in the previous year.
edge_cases.outcome: The answer is the thirty-first of December of that previous year.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date is earlier in the current year.
edge_cases.outcome: The answer is today.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date is in the future.
edge_cases.outcome: The answer is the candidate date itself.

worked_examples.description: A bill of the previous year captured in the new year
worked_examples.narrative: 2027 is later than 2026, so the entry is dated the last day of 2026 and keeps its place in the yearly series.

worked_examples.description: A bill of the current year captured a month later
worked_examples.narrative: The years are equal, so the answer is the later of the two dates, that is today.

records.name: The accounting date of a purchase document in a series that never resets or resets over a year range
records.purpose: Leaves the candidate date untouched when the numbering grammar carries no monthly or yearly period that a late capture could disturb.

operands.name: candidate date
operands.source: the accounting date source, after the lock-date shift
operands.constraints: never empty at this point

operands.name: number reset period
operands.source: deduced from the highest number of the series
operands.constraints: this record covers the reset periods `year_range` and `never`

preconditions.condition: The document is a purchase document.
preconditions.otherwise: The sale branch applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The reset period is neither monthly, nor monthly within a year range, nor yearly.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the two shifting branches applies.

procedure: Deduce the reset period from the highest number already used in the series.
Apply the lock-date shift when a lock date is violated.
Answer the candidate date unchanged, since no period boundary has to be respected.
records.formula: accounting_date = d

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: accounting date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document.

edge_cases.case: A lock date was violated.
edge_cases.outcome: The candidate date has already been replaced by the latest violated lock date plus one day, and that shifted date is what is answered.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date is far in the past.
edge_cases.outcome: It is answered unchanged, because a series that never resets has no period to protect.

worked_examples.description: A bill in a journal whose numbers never reset
worked_examples.narrative: No period boundary applies, so the bill keeps its own date of 20 August 2026.

records.name: The accounting date of a sale document
records.purpose: States the branch the same routine takes for a sale document, where the date is only shifted when a lock date has been violated; it is recorded here because the payable side shares the routine with the receivable side.

operands.name: candidate date
operands.source: the accounting date source
operands.constraints: never empty at this point

operands.name: today
operands.source: the current date in the user's time zone
operands.constraints: always available

operands.name: violated lock dates
operands.source: the lock dates of the company and the journal that the candidate date falls before, ordered chronologically
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: number reset period
operands.source: deduced from the highest number of the series
operands.constraints: one of the five grammars

preconditions.condition: The document is a sale document.
preconditions.otherwise: The purchase branches apply.

procedure: When no lock date is violated, answer the candidate date unchanged.
Otherwise replace the candidate date by the latest violated lock date plus one day.
When the series has no name yet or resets monthly, answer the earlier of today and the last day of the month of the shifted date.
When it resets yearly, answer the earlier of today and the last day of the year of the shifted date.
Otherwise answer the shifted date.
records.formula:
accounting_date = d                                              when no lock date is violated
accounting_date = min( today , last day of the month of d )      when a lock date is violated and the series has no name yet or resets monthly
accounting_date = min( today , last day of the year of d )       when a lock date is violated and the series resets yearly
accounting_date = d                                              otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: accounting date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document.

edge_cases.case: No lock date is violated.
edge_cases.outcome: The sale document keeps its own date, unlike a purchase document, which is shifted whenever it was captured in a later period.

edge_cases.case: A lock date is violated and the shifted date is later than today.
edge_cases.outcome: The smaller of the two is today, so the entry is dated today.

worked_examples.description: A sale document with no lock date violation
worked_examples.narrative: The sale branch leaves the date alone; only a violated lock date would move it.

worked_examples.description: A sale document dated before a lock date of 31 August 2026, monthly series
worked_examples.narrative: The candidate becomes 1 September 2026; the smaller of today and the last day of September is today, so the entry is dated 11 September 2026.

records.name: The lock-date shift of a candidate accounting date
records.purpose: Moves a candidate accounting date out of a locked period before the period rules are applied, and supplies the date the warning banner announces to the user.

operands.name: candidate date
operands.source: the accounting date source of the document
operands.constraints: never empty at this point

operands.name: violated lock dates
operands.source: the lock dates of the company and of the journal that the candidate date falls on or before, taking the tax report flag of the document into account, ordered chronologically
operands.constraints: may be empty

preconditions.condition: At least one lock date is violated by the candidate date.
preconditions.otherwise: The candidate date is left unchanged and no banner is shown.

preconditions.condition: The reading user holds the read-only accounting group or the invoicing group.
preconditions.otherwise: The banner is not displayed, although the shift itself still happens.

procedure: Collect the lock dates that the candidate date violates, for that candidate, that journal and that company, taking into account whether the document affects the tax report.
Order them chronologically and take the latest.
Add one day to that latest violated lock date and use the result as the new candidate date.
Show the warning banner naming the formatted list of lock dates and the resulting accounting date.
Continue with the period rules of the numbering grammar, which may move the date further.
records.formula: shifted_candidate = latest_violated_lock_date + 1 day

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the shift is one whole day.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Before the period rules of the numbering grammar are applied.

result.name: shifted candidate date
result.stored_or_displayed: Fed into the period rules; the final accounting date is stored on the document and announced in the banner, which reads "The date is being set prior to: «the formatted list of lock dates». The Journal Entry will be accounted on «the resulting accounting date» upon posting." at warning level.

edge_cases.case: Several lock dates are violated at once.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the latest of them matters; the banner nonetheless lists all of them.

edge_cases.case: The shifted date now falls in a later month than the candidate.
edge_cases.outcome: The period rules of the numbering grammar are applied to the shifted date, which may move it again to the last day of that month.

edge_cases.case: The user holds neither accounting group.
edge_cases.outcome: The shift happens silently, without a banner.

worked_examples.description: A bill dated inside a locked period
worked_examples.narrative: The candidate is moved to the day after the lock date, 1 September 2026; the purchase branch then compares months, finds them equal, and answers the later of 1 September and today, that is 11 September 2026.

records.name: Ordering the candidate supplier bank accounts
records.purpose: Chooses the bank account the payment will be sent to, preferring an account held in the currency of the document and, among equals, an account trusted for outgoing payments.

operands.name: candidate bank accounts
operands.unit_or_currency: a list of bank account records
operands.source: the bank accounts of the bank partner, which is the company partner for an inbound document and the commercial partner, that is the vendor, for an outbound document
operands.constraints: kept only when they belong to the document's company or to no company and when they are active, the active filter being applied explicitly because some contexts disable it implicitly

operands.name: currency priority of an account
operands.source: a comparison between the account currency and the document currency
operands.constraints: zero when the account has no currency or its currency equals the document currency, one otherwise

operands.name: outgoing payment trust of an account
operands.source: the flag saying the account is allowed for outgoing payments
operands.constraints: a trusted account sorts first

preconditions.condition: The document is not an inbound document served by a payment method line that carries a journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The recipient bank account is that journal's bank account and the ordering below is not run at all.

preconditions.condition: At least one candidate account survives the company and active filters.
preconditions.otherwise: No recipient bank account is set.

procedure: Recompute whenever the bank partner, the currency or the preferred payment method line changes.

For an inbound document, which on the payable side means a vendor credit note, and when a payment method line is available, either the document's preferred one or the bank partner's inbound payment method line property, and when that method line has a journal, take that journal's bank account and stop.
Otherwise take the bank accounts of the bank partner: the company partner for an inbound document, the vendor for an outbound one.
Keep only the accounts that belong to the document's company or to no company and that are active.
Sort the survivors by the pair made of the currency priority and the negation of the outgoing payment trust.
Take the first account of that ordering, or none when the list is empty.
records.formula:
sort_key(account) = ( currency_priority , not allowed_out_payment )
currency_priority = 0 when the account has no currency or its currency equals the document currency, 1 otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the result is a chosen record.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: recipient bank account
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a bank account reference
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document as its recipient bank account and printed on the payment instruction.

edge_cases.case: Two accounts are in the document currency, one trusted and one not.
edge_cases.outcome: The trusted account wins, because the second component of the key sorts a trusted account first.

edge_cases.case: One account is in the document currency but untrusted and another is in a different currency but trusted.
edge_cases.outcome: The account in the document currency wins, because the currency component is compared first.

edge_cases.case: An account has no currency at all.
edge_cases.outcome: It is treated as matching the document currency and receives priority zero.

edge_cases.case: The chosen account is archived at posting time.
edge_cases.outcome: Posting is refused with the message that the recipient bank account linked to this invoice is archived and that the document cannot be confirmed.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has no bank account.
edge_cases.outcome: The document carries no recipient bank account, and posting an outgoing payment whose method requires one is refused.

worked_examples.description: A vendor with three accounts and a bill in euros
worked_examples.narrative: The two euro accounts share the currency priority of zero; the trusted one sorts first, so the third account is chosen, and the dollar account comes last.

worked_examples.description: A vendor with a single untrusted account
worked_examples.narrative: An account with no currency counts as matching; it is the only candidate and is chosen even though it is untrusted, the trust being checked again when the payment is posted.

records.name: The duplicate candidate predicate for a purchase document
records.purpose: Decides whether a stored document is a probable duplicate of the purchase document being examined, so that the same supplier document is not captured, posted or paid twice.

operands.name: examined document
operands.source: the document being typed, whose in-memory values are injected into the comparison: company, partner, commercial partner, vendor reference, type, bill date, status, total and currency, plus the identifier, which is the stored identifier for an existing document and zero for a brand-new one
operands.constraints: its total is read from the live tax totals structure rather than from the stored total, which is only computed at save time

operands.name: stored document
operands.source: any other document of the same company
operands.constraints: must be of type `in_invoice`, `in_refund` or `in_receipt` when the examined document is one of those three

operands.name: matching states
operands.source: the fixed pair `draft` and `posted`
operands.constraints: a cancelled document is never a candidate

operands.name: total
operands.source: the grand total of each document
operands.constraints: the second matching case requires the examined total to be non-zero

preconditions.condition: The examined document is a sale document or a purchase document, receipts included.
preconditions.otherwise: The set of probable duplicates is empty.

preconditions.condition: The reading user is allowed to read the candidate.
preconditions.otherwise: The candidate is filtered out of the grouped result.

procedure: Recompute the set whenever the vendor reference, the document type, the partner, the bill date, the tax totals or the currency changes.
Require the same company on both documents.
Require different identifiers, a brand-new document carrying the identifier zero.
Require the stored document's status to be one of the matching states, that is draft or posted.
Require compatible types: equal types, or both in the pair vendor bill and purchase receipt, or both in the pair customer invoice and sales receipt.
Require the same currency.
Require the same commercial partner, or that the examined document has no commercial partner and the stored one is a draft.
Then accept the candidate under the first case when the two vendor references are equal and either document has no bill date or the two bill dates fall in the same calendar year.
Or accept it under the second case when the commercial partners are equal, the totals are equal, the examined total is not zero and the two bill dates are equal.
Group the accepted candidates per examined document and filter them down to the records the reading user may read.
records.formula:
duplicate( D , M ) = same company × different identifiers × D.status ∈ { draft , posted } × compatible types × same currency × matching partners × ( case_1 + case_2 )
case_1 = ( D.reference = M.reference ) × ( M has no bill date + D has no bill date + same calendar year )
case_2 = ( D.commercial_partner = M.commercial_partner ) × ( D.total = M.total ) × ( M.total ≠ 0 ) × ( D.bill_date = M.bill_date )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the totals are compared as stored, each already rounded to its currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the shared currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each total was computed.
rounding.step: Before the comparison, never during it.

result.name: set of probable duplicates
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a set of document references
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the examined document as its set of duplicated documents, displayed as a banner with a button naming the first duplicate and its total.

edge_cases.case: The same reference is used by the supplier in two different calendar years.
edge_cases.outcome: The first case fails on the year test and the second fails on the bill date, so no duplicate is reported; this is deliberate, because suppliers restart their own numbering every year.

edge_cases.case: The reference was typed differently, for instance with spaces instead of hyphens.
edge_cases.outcome: The first case fails but the second succeeds when the commercial partner, the non-zero total and the bill date all match.

edge_cases.case: The examined total is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The second case cannot fire, so only an identical reference can raise a duplicate.

edge_cases.case: The examined document has no commercial partner yet.
edge_cases.outcome: Only draft documents can match, through the alternative partner condition.

edge_cases.case: The candidate is in another currency.
edge_cases.outcome: It is rejected, whatever its reference or total.

worked_examples.description: The same reference captured twice in the same year
worked_examples.narrative: Same company, different identifiers, the stored document is posted and therefore in the matching states, both types are vendor bills, same currency, same commercial partner, and the references are equal with both bill dates in 2026, so the stored bill is a duplicate candidate.

worked_examples.description: The reference typed with spaces instead of hyphens
worked_examples.narrative: The references differ so the first case fails, but the commercial partner, the non-zero total of 1 452.00 and the bill date all match, so the second case succeeds.

worked_examples.description: The same reference one year apart
worked_examples.narrative: The calendar years differ, so the first case fails, and the bill dates differ, so the second fails; the document posts normally.

records.name: The duplicate candidate predicate for a sale document
records.purpose: States the branch the same routine takes for a sale document, recorded here because the payable side shares the detection routine with the receivable side and the common conditions are identical.

operands.name: examined document
operands.source: the sale document being typed, with the same in-memory values injected
operands.constraints: of type `out_invoice`, `out_refund` or `out_receipt`

operands.name: stored document
operands.source: any other document of the same company
operands.constraints: must satisfy the common conditions

operands.name: total
operands.source: the grand total of each document
operands.constraints: compared exactly

operands.name: bill date
operands.source: the document date of each document
operands.constraints: compared exactly

preconditions.condition: The examined document is a sale document.
preconditions.otherwise: The purchase-specific condition applies instead.

procedure: Apply the six common conditions: same company, different identifiers, the stored status among draft and posted, compatible types, same currency and matching partners.
Then require the totals to be equal and the two bill dates to be equal.
Group and filter the result exactly as for a purchase document.
records.formula: duplicate( D , M ) = common conditions × ( D.total = M.total ) × ( D.bill_date = M.bill_date )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the totals are compared as stored.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the shared currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each total was computed.

result.name: set of probable duplicates
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a set of document references
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the examined document and shown as a banner.

edge_cases.case: The reference differs but the total and the date match.
edge_cases.outcome: The candidate is still detected, because the sale branch does not look at the reference at all.

edge_cases.case: The total is zero on both documents.
edge_cases.outcome: The candidate is detected, the non-zero condition being specific to the purchase branch.

worked_examples.description: Two customer invoices of the same amount on the same day
worked_examples.narrative: The common conditions hold and both the total of 500.00 and the date of 2 March 2026 are equal, so the stored invoice is reported as a probable duplicate.

records.name: The exact-duplicate predicate
records.purpose: Distinguishes a duplicate that is certainly the same supplier document, which raises the red banner, from a merely probable one, which raises the amber banner.

operands.name: vendor reference of the examined document
operands.source: the reference the supplier printed on the document
operands.constraints: must be non-empty for the predicate to hold

operands.name: vendor reference of the detected duplicate
operands.source: the same field on the candidate
operands.constraints: must be equal to the examined one

operands.name: partner
operands.source: the partner of each document, not the commercial partner
operands.constraints: compared exactly, so a different contact of the same company is not an exact duplicate

operands.name: bill date
operands.source: each document
operands.constraints: compared exactly

operands.name: total
operands.source: each document
operands.constraints: compared exactly

preconditions.condition: The candidate has already passed the duplicate candidate predicate.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to qualify.

preconditions.condition: The examined document is a purchase document, that is a vendor bill or a vendor credit note and not a purchase receipt.
preconditions.otherwise: The predicate cannot hold, because it excludes receipts.

procedure: Require the examined vendor reference to be non-empty and equal to the candidate's.
Require compatible types, that is equal types, or both in the pair vendor bill and purchase receipt, or both in the pair customer invoice and sales receipt.
Require the two partners to be equal, comparing the partner and not the commercial partner.
Require the two bill dates to be equal.
Require the two totals to be equal.
Require the examined document to be a bill or a vendor credit note.
Record separately whether any detected duplicate is still a draft, which is what enables the delete action.
records.formula: exact_duplicate = ( M.reference non-empty ) × ( D.reference = M.reference ) × compatible types × ( D.partner = M.partner ) × ( D.bill_date = M.bill_date ) × ( D.total = M.total ) × ( M is a bill or a vendor credit note )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the totals are compared as stored.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the shared currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each total was computed.

result.name: exact-duplicate flag
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a true or false value
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the examined document; it selects the red banner and shades the vendor reference cell red in the bill upload list.

edge_cases.case: The duplicate is on a different contact of the same commercial partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is false, because the comparison is on the partner and not on the commercial partner; the amber banner is shown instead.

edge_cases.case: The examined document is a purchase receipt.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is false by construction, since the predicate excludes receipts.

edge_cases.case: The examined vendor reference is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is false, and only the amber banner can appear.

edge_cases.case: Every detected duplicate is posted.
edge_cases.outcome: The draft-duplicate flag is false and the delete action is hidden.

worked_examples.description: The same reference, partner, date and total
worked_examples.narrative: Every component holds, so the flag is set; the only duplicate is posted, so the draft flag is false and the delete action stays hidden.

worked_examples.description: The reference typed with spaces instead of hyphens
worked_examples.narrative: The references differ, so the flag is false even though the candidate was detected through the second matching case.

records.name: Choosing the duplicate warning level and its consequence for automatic posting
records.purpose: Turns the two duplicate flags into the banner the user sees, the shading of the list cell and the suppression of automatic posting.

operands.name: exact-duplicate flag
operands.source: the exact-duplicate predicate
operands.constraints: true or false

operands.name: number of detected duplicates
operands.source: the set of probable duplicates
operands.constraints: zero or more

operands.name: draft-duplicate flag
operands.source: true when at least one detected duplicate is still a draft
operands.constraints: true or false

operands.name: status of the examined document
operands.source: the stored status
operands.constraints: the amber banner requires a draft

preconditions.condition: At least one duplicate was detected.
preconditions.otherwise: No banner is shown and automatic posting proceeds.

procedure: When the exact-duplicate flag is set, show the banner at danger level, coloured red.
When duplicates exist, the exact-duplicate flag is not set and the document is still a draft, show the same wording at warning level, coloured amber.
In both cases the wording is "This document might be a duplicate of" followed by a button naming the first duplicate and showing its total.

When the draft-duplicate flag is set, add the red action reading "Delete duplicate" when there is exactly one duplicate and "Delete all duplicates" when there are several; that action removes every detected duplicate of the current document.
Shade the vendor reference cell of the bill upload list red when the exact-duplicate flag is set and amber when duplicates exist and the document is a draft.
Suppress automatic posting and write to the chatter "Auto-post was disabled on this invoice because a potential duplicate was detected."
records.formula:
banner_level = danger      when exact_duplicate_flag
banner_level = warning     when duplicates exist and not exact_duplicate_flag and the document is a draft
banner_level = none        otherwise
delete_action_visible = draft_duplicate_flag
auto_post_allowed = ( number of detected duplicates = 0 )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the total shown on the button is formatted in the duplicate's own currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of that currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the total was computed.

result.name: duplicate banner and its actions
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the document form and in the bill upload list; it also blocks automatic posting.

edge_cases.case: The exact-duplicate flag is set on a posted document.
edge_cases.outcome: The red banner is still shown, since it does not require a draft, unlike the amber one.

edge_cases.case: Duplicates exist, the flag is not set and the document is posted.
edge_cases.outcome: No banner is shown.

edge_cases.case: Several duplicates exist and at least one is a draft.
edge_cases.outcome: The action reads "Delete all duplicates" and removes every detected duplicate.

edge_cases.case: The single duplicate is posted.
edge_cases.outcome: The delete action is hidden, because the draft-duplicate flag looks at the detected duplicates and not at the examined document.

worked_examples.description: A draft bill that exactly duplicates a posted one

expected_outputs.chatter_message: Auto-post was disabled on this invoice because a potential duplicate was detected.

worked_examples.narrative: The red banner names the posted bill and its total of 1 452.00; the delete action is hidden because the duplicate is posted, and automatic posting is suppressed.

worked_examples.description: A draft bill matched only through the second case
worked_examples.narrative: The amber banner is shown with the same wording, and automatic posting is still suppressed.

records.name: The due date of a term line of delay type a number of days after the reference date
records.purpose: Places one instalment of a payment term on the calendar by adding a plain number of days to the reference date of the document.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the bill date when set, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

operands.name: day count
operands.source: the day count of the term line
operands.constraints: a whole number, zero or more

preconditions.condition: The term line's delay type is the plain days-after type, stored as `days_after`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the four other delay rules applies.

procedure: Take the reference date of the document: the bill date when it is set, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise today.
Add the line's day count to it, counting whole calendar days.
Answer that date as the maturity date of the instalment.
records.formula: due_date = r + n days

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line as its maturity date and used as part of the key of the needed-terms map.

edge_cases.case: The day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The instalment falls on the reference date itself, that is immediate payment.

edge_cases.case: The addition crosses a month or a year boundary.
edge_cases.outcome: Plain calendar arithmetic applies; no clamping is needed because no month is being added.

edge_cases.case: The document has no bill date and no accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: Today is used as the reference date.

worked_examples.description: Thirty days from the bill date
worked_examples.narrative: June has thirty days, so adding thirty days to 1 June 2026 gives 1 July 2026, which is the maturity date of the single instalment in the early discount example.

worked_examples.description: Immediate payment
worked_examples.narrative: A day count of zero leaves the reference date unchanged.

records.name: The due date of a term line of delay type a number of days after the end of the month
records.purpose: Places an instalment a fixed number of days after the last day of the month of the reference date, the customary way of expressing sixty days end of month.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the bill date when set, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

operands.name: day count
operands.source: the day count of the term line
operands.constraints: a whole number, zero or more

preconditions.condition: The term line's delay type is the days-after-end-of-month type, stored as `days_after_end_of_month`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the four other delay rules applies.

procedure: Take the reference date.
Move to the last day of the month that contains it.
Add the line's day count to that last day, counting whole calendar days.
Answer that date as the maturity date of the instalment.
records.formula: due_date = last_day_of_month( r ) + n days

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line as its maturity date.

edge_cases.case: The day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The instalment falls on the last day of the month of the reference date.

edge_cases.case: The reference date is already the last day of its month.
edge_cases.outcome: The first step changes nothing and the day count is added to that date.

edge_cases.case: The month is February of a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The last day is the twenty-ninth, and the day count is added to it.

worked_examples.description: Sixty days end of month from a bill of 14 April 2026
worked_examples.narrative: April has thirty days, so the last day is 30 April 2026; thirty days later is 30 May and thirty more is 29 June, so the due date is 29 June 2026.

worked_examples.description: End of month with no extra days
worked_examples.narrative: The first instalment of the two-instalment variant falls on 30 April 2026.

records.name: The due date of a term line of delay type a number of days after the end of the next month
records.purpose: Places an instalment a fixed number of days after the last day of the month following the reference date, for terms that grant an extra month before the count starts.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the bill date when set, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

operands.name: day count
operands.source: the day count of the term line
operands.constraints: a whole number, zero or more

preconditions.condition: The term line's delay type is the days-after-end-of-next-month type, stored as `days_after_end_of_next_month`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the four other delay rules applies.

procedure: Take the reference date and add one month to it, clamping the day to the length of the target month.
Move to the last day of the month so reached.
Add the line's day count to that last day.
Answer that date as the maturity date of the instalment.
records.formula: due_date = last_day_of_month( r + 1 month ) + n days

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date. The month addition clamps the day to the length of the target month.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: The clamping happens at the month addition, before the last day of the month is taken.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line as its maturity date.

edge_cases.case: The reference date is 31 January.
edge_cases.outcome: Adding one month clamps to 28 or 29 February, and the last day of that month is the same date.

edge_cases.case: The day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The instalment falls on the last day of the month after the reference month.

edge_cases.case: The reference date is in December.
edge_cases.outcome: The month addition moves into January of the next year.

worked_examples.description: Sixty days after the end of the next month
worked_examples.narrative: One month after 14 April 2026 is 14 May 2026, whose month ends on 31 May 2026; thirty days later is 30 June and thirty more is 30 July 2026.

worked_examples.description: End of the next month with no extra days
worked_examples.narrative: The month addition clamps 31 January to 28 February 2026, which is already the last day of that month, and no days are added.

records.name: The due date of a term line of delay type end of month on a given day, when that day is zero or less
records.purpose: Places an instalment at the end of the month reached after adding a number of days, which is the behaviour of the fourth delay type when no day of the month has been named.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the bill date when set, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

operands.name: day count
operands.source: the day count of the term line
operands.constraints: a whole number, zero or more

operands.name: days on the next month
operands.source: the term line's days-on-the-next-month value
operands.constraints: this record covers the case where the value is zero or less; the value must be a number between zero and thirty-one

preconditions.condition: The term line's delay type is the end-of-month-on-a-given-day type, stored as `days_end_of_month_on_the`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the four other delay rules applies.

preconditions.condition: The days-on-the-next-month value is zero or less.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant that forces a day of the month applies.

procedure: Take the reference date and add the line's day count to it.
Move to the last day of the month that contains the date so reached.
Answer that date as the maturity date of the instalment.
records.formula: due_date = last_day_of_month( r + n days )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line as its maturity date.

edge_cases.case: The day count carries the date into the following month.
edge_cases.outcome: The end of that following month is used, not the end of the reference month.

edge_cases.case: The days-on-the-next-month value is exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: This branch applies, since the variant requires a strictly positive value.

worked_examples.description: Ten days, then the end of the month reached
worked_examples.narrative: Ten days after 25 April 2026 is 5 May 2026, whose month ends on 31 May 2026.

records.name: The due date of a term line of delay type end of month on a given day, when that day is strictly positive
records.purpose: Places an instalment on a named day of the month after the one reached by adding the day count, which is how a term such as ten days then the fifteenth of the following month is expressed.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the bill date when set, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

operands.name: day count
operands.source: the day count of the term line
operands.constraints: a whole number, zero or more

operands.name: days on the next month
operands.source: the term line's days-on-the-next-month value
operands.constraints: strictly positive for this variant, and refused unless it is a number between zero and thirty-one

preconditions.condition: The term line's delay type is the end-of-month-on-a-given-day type, stored as `days_end_of_month_on_the`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the four other delay rules applies.

preconditions.condition: The days-on-the-next-month value is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The end-of-month variant applies.

preconditions.condition: The days-on-the-next-month value is numeric and between zero and thirty-one.
preconditions.otherwise: The term line is refused, with the message that the days added must be a number and has to be between 0 and 31, or that the days added must be between 0 and 31.

procedure: Take the reference date and add the line's day count to it.
Advance the date so reached by one month, clamping the day to the length of the target month.
Force the day of the month to the days-on-the-next-month value.
Answer that date as the maturity date of the instalment.
records.formula: due_date = ( r + n days ) advanced by one month, then the day of month forced to d

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date. Adding a month clamps the day to the length of the target month, so 31 January plus one month is 28 or 29 February.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: The clamping happens at the month addition, before the day of the month is forced.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line as its maturity date.

edge_cases.case: The named day is thirty-one and the target month is shorter.
edge_cases.outcome: The day of the month is forced to a day the month does not have; the month addition has already clamped the intermediate date, and the forced day is applied within the length of that month.

edge_cases.case: The day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The month is added directly to the reference date.

edge_cases.case: The named day is earlier than the day reached.
edge_cases.outcome: The date still moves to the named day of the following month, which may be earlier in that month.

worked_examples.description: Ten days, then the fifteenth of the following month
worked_examples.narrative: Ten days after 25 April 2026 is 5 May 2026; one month later is 5 June 2026, and the day is then forced to the fifteenth, giving 15 June 2026.

records.name: The totals and the derived rate of the payment term distribution
records.purpose: Establishes the two amounts the instalments must add back up to and the conversion rate between them, derived from the totals themselves so that the instalments can never drift away from the document.

operands.name: signed tax amount in company currency
operands.source: the tax total of the document, already signed
operands.constraints: recomputed from the base lines while the document is an unsaved draft

operands.name: signed untaxed amount in company currency
operands.source: the untaxed total of the document, already signed
operands.constraints: recomputed from the base lines while the document is an unsaved draft

operands.name: signed tax amount in document currency
operands.source: the tax total of the document in the currency written on it
operands.constraints: same

operands.name: signed untaxed amount in document currency
operands.source: the untaxed total of the document in the currency written on it
operands.constraints: same

preconditions.condition: The two totals are available in both currencies.
preconditions.otherwise: While the document is an unsaved draft they are recomputed from the base lines rather than read from the stored totals.

preconditions.condition: The company-currency total is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is taken as zero, and every instalment computed by division by the rate is taken as zero.

procedure: Add the signed tax amount and the signed untaxed amount in the company currency to obtain the company-currency total.
Add the same two amounts in the document currency to obtain the document-currency total.
Divide the document-currency total by the company-currency total and take the absolute value; this is the rate used by the distribution.
Take the rate as zero when the company-currency total is zero.
Initialise the two residuals to the two totals, which the instalments will consume in order.
