records.formula:
total_amount          = tax_amount + untaxed_amount                    (company currency)
total_amount_currency = tax_amount_currency + untaxed_amount_currency  (document currency)
rate                  = | total_amount_currency ÷ total_amount |       (0 when total_amount is 0)

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded at this step; the rate is kept at full precision so that the divisions of the individual instalments are not distorted.
rounding.precision: Full precision for the rate; the two totals are already rounded to their own currencies.
rounding.step: Rounding happens on each instalment, not on the rate.

result.name: company-currency total, document-currency total and derived rate
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency, the document currency and a pure ratio
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; held for the duration of the distribution and consumed by the instalment rules.

edge_cases.case: The document is in the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The two totals are equal and the rate is one.

edge_cases.case: The company-currency total is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is zero and every fixed instalment and every rate division yields zero.

edge_cases.case: The rate is derived rather than read from the document.
edge_cases.outcome: The instalments always add back up to exactly the two totals, whatever rate the document itself carries.

edge_cases.case: The document total is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute value makes the rate positive, the sign being carried by the totals themselves.

worked_examples.description: A bill in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: Both totals are 3 600.00 and the rate is one, so every instalment is the same figure in both currencies.

worked_examples.description: A bill in a foreign currency
worked_examples.narrative: The document-currency total of 1 464.10 divided by the company-currency total of 1 210.00 gives a rate of 1.21, which is used to restate each fixed instalment.

records.name: The instalment of a fixed term line
records.purpose: Computes the two amounts of an instalment whose term line names an absolute figure rather than a percentage.

operands.name: line value
operands.source: the amount named on the fixed term line
operands.constraints: expressed in the document currency, since it is an absolute figure the supplier agreed to

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the document type
operands.constraints: plus one on a vendor bill

operands.name: rate
operands.source: the rate derived from the two totals
operands.constraints: zero makes both amounts zero

preconditions.condition: The term line is not the last line of the term.
preconditions.otherwise: The balance rule applies instead, whatever the line's declared type.

preconditions.condition: The rate is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The company-currency amount is taken as zero.

procedure: Take the absolute figure named on the term line, which is expressed in the document currency.
Multiply it by the direction sign and round it to the document currency to obtain the foreign amount.
Divide the same figure by the rate, multiply by the direction sign and round to the company currency to obtain the company amount, taking zero when the rate is zero.
Subtract both amounts from the two residuals before moving to the next line.
records.formula:
company_amount = direction_sign × round_to( company_currency , line_value ÷ rate )   ( 0 when the rate is 0 )
foreign_amount = direction_sign × round_to( document_currency , line_value )

rounding.what: Each of the two amounts of the instalment.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency for the company amount, of the document currency for the foreign amount.
rounding.step: After the division by the rate and before the multiplication by the direction sign is stored, once per currency, and before the residuals are reduced.

result.name: instalment amounts of a fixed term line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Fed into the needed-terms map and finally stored on the payable term line as its balance and its amount in currency.

edge_cases.case: The fixed amount exceeds the document total.
edge_cases.outcome: The residual becomes negative and the balance line, being the last, absorbs the negative remainder, so the instalments still sum to the total.

edge_cases.case: The rate is zero because the company-currency total is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The company amount is zero while the foreign amount is still the named figure.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is minus one and both amounts are negated.

worked_examples.description: A fixed first instalment of one thousand euros on a bill in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The rate is one, so both amounts are 1 000.00, and the residuals fall to 2 600.00 for the following lines.

worked_examples.description: The same fixed instalment on a document whose derived rate is 1.21
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand units of the document currency divided by 1.21 is 826.4462…, which rounds half away from zero to 826.45 in the company currency.

records.name: The instalment of a percent term line
records.purpose: Computes the two amounts of an instalment whose term line names a share of the total rather than an absolute figure.

operands.name: line value
operands.source: the percentage named on the term line
operands.constraints: between zero and one hundred, and the percent lines of a term must sum to exactly one hundred at the payment-terms decimal precision

operands.name: company-currency total
operands.source: the totals of the distribution
operands.constraints: already signed

operands.name: document-currency total
operands.source: the totals of the distribution
operands.constraints: already signed

preconditions.condition: The term line is not the last line of the term.
preconditions.otherwise: The balance rule applies instead, whatever the line's declared type.

preconditions.condition: The percent lines of the term sum to exactly one hundred.
preconditions.otherwise: The term itself is refused, with the message that the payment term must have at least one percent line and that the sum of the percent lines must be one hundred.

procedure: Multiply the company-currency total by the percentage and divide by one hundred, then round to the company currency.
Multiply the document-currency total by the percentage and divide by one hundred, then round to the document currency.
Note that the direction sign is not applied again here, because it is already carried by the two totals.
Subtract both amounts from the two residuals before moving to the next line.
records.formula:
company_amount = round_to( company_currency , total_amount × line_value ÷ 100 )
foreign_amount = round_to( document_currency , total_amount_currency × line_value ÷ 100 )

rounding.what: Each of the two amounts of the instalment.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency for the company amount, of the document currency for the foreign amount.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the percentage and the division by one hundred, once per currency, and before the residuals are reduced.

result.name: instalment amounts of a percent term line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Fed into the needed-terms map and finally stored on the payable term line.

edge_cases.case: The percentages do not divide the total exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: Every rounding difference accumulates in the residual and is absorbed by the last line, which is always the balance line.

edge_cases.case: The percentage is one hundred on a single-line term.
edge_cases.outcome: That single line is also the last line, so the balance rule applies and it takes the whole residual.

edge_cases.case: A percentage below zero or above one hundred is entered.
edge_cases.outcome: The term line is refused with the message that percentages on the payment terms lines must be between 0 and 100.

worked_examples.description: Thirty per cent of a bill of three thousand six hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: Three thousand six hundred multiplied by thirty and divided by one hundred is 1 080.00 in both currencies, leaving a residual of 2 520.00 for the last line.

worked_examples.description: Two lines of 33.33 per cent on a total of one hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: Each of the two percent lines rounds to 33.33, and the residual left for the third and last line is 33.34.

records.name: The instalment of the balance line of a payment term
records.purpose: Guarantees that the instalments sum exactly to the document total in both currencies by giving the whole remaining residual to the last line, whatever that line declares itself to be.

operands.name: remaining residual in company currency
operands.source: the company-currency total less every instalment already produced
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: remaining residual in document currency
operands.source: the document-currency total less every instalment already produced
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: position of the line
operands.source: the term's own line order, that is the order of the line identifiers, which is the order in which they were created
operands.constraints: the balance rule applies to the last line only

preconditions.condition: The term line being computed is the last one in the term's own line order.
preconditions.otherwise: The fixed rule or the percent rule applies.

procedure: Determine that the line under computation is the last of the term, in the term's own line order.
Give it the whole remaining residual in the company currency as its company amount.
Give it the whole remaining residual in the document currency as its foreign amount.
Do not apply the cash-rounding step to this line, because only cash-rounded amounts have been subtracted from a cash-rounded total, so the balance line is already cash-rounded.
Reduce both residuals to zero.
records.formula:
company_amount = residual_amount
foreign_amount = residual_amount_currency

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded on the balance line itself; it absorbs the rounding differences of every earlier line.
rounding.precision: The residuals are already expressed at the rounding factor of their currencies.
rounding.step: The balance line is computed last, after every other instalment has been rounded and subtracted.

result.name: instalment amounts of the balance line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the last payable term line; it is what makes the sum of the term lines equal the document total exactly.

edge_cases.case: The term has a single line.
edge_cases.outcome: That line is the last one, so it takes the whole total whatever its declared type or percentage.

edge_cases.case: The earlier lines rounded upwards.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance line is correspondingly smaller, and the sum still equals the total exactly.

edge_cases.case: The earlier fixed lines exceed the total.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance line carries a negative amount, keeping the sum exact.

edge_cases.case: A cash rounding rule applies to the document.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance line is cash-rounded implicitly, since every amount subtracted from the cash-rounded total was itself cash-rounded.

worked_examples.description: A single-line term on a bill of three thousand six hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: The only line is the balance line and takes the whole total of 3 600.00.

worked_examples.description: The third line of a term of 33.33, 33.33 and 33.34 per cent on one hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: The two earlier lines took 33.33 each, so the balance line takes 33.34 and the three instalments sum to exactly 100.00.

worked_examples.description: The second line of a thirty and seventy per cent term on three thousand six hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: The figure happens to equal seventy per cent exactly, but the line would absorb any rounding drift if it did not.

records.name: The cash-rounding adjustment of an instalment
records.purpose: Keeps every instalment payable in the smallest coin available when the document carries a cash rounding rule, so that the sum of the instalments remains the cash-rounded total.

operands.name: foreign amount of the instalment
operands.source: the fixed rule or the percent rule, before adjustment
operands.constraints: already rounded to the document currency

operands.name: cash rounding difference
operands.source: the cash rounding rule of the document, applied to the foreign amount
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rate
operands.source: the rate derived from the two totals
operands.constraints: zero makes the recomputed company amount zero

preconditions.condition: The document carries a cash rounding rule.
preconditions.otherwise: No adjustment is made.

preconditions.condition: The instalment is not the balance line.
preconditions.otherwise: No adjustment is made, the balance line being cash-rounded implicitly.

preconditions.condition: The cash rounding difference is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The instalment is left as computed.

procedure: Compute the cash rounding difference of the foreign amount under the document's cash rounding rule.
When that difference is not zero, add it to the foreign amount.
Recompute the company amount by dividing the adjusted foreign amount by the rate and rounding to the company currency, taking zero when the rate is zero.
Subtract the adjusted amounts from the two residuals, so that the balance line inherits a cash-rounded remainder.
records.formula:
foreign_amount = foreign_amount + difference( document_currency , foreign_amount )
company_amount = round_to( company_currency , foreign_amount ÷ rate )   ( 0 when the rate is 0 )

rounding.what: The foreign amount is moved to a multiple of the rule's rounding precision, and the company amount is then rounded to the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding precision of the cash rounding rule for the foreign amount, then the rounding factor of the company currency.
rounding.method: The rounding method of the rule, that is up, down or nearest, for the cash rounding; half away from zero for the currency rounding.
rounding.step: After the instalment has been computed and rounded to the document currency, and before the residuals are reduced.

result.name: cash-rounded instalment amounts
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Fed into the needed-terms map and stored on the payable term line.

edge_cases.case: The instalment is already a multiple of the rounding precision.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero and nothing changes.

edge_cases.case: The instalment is the last line.
edge_cases.outcome: No adjustment is applied; the line takes the residual, which is already cash-rounded.

edge_cases.case: The rate is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The company amount becomes zero while the foreign amount keeps its cash-rounded value.

worked_examples.description: An instalment of 23.91 under a rounding precision of five hundredths
worked_examples.narrative: The nearest multiple of five hundredths below 23.91 is 23.90, so the difference is −0.01; the instalment becomes 23.90 and the company amount follows at a rate of one.

records.name: The order of evaluation and the carry-forward of the residuals in the distribution
records.purpose: Fixes the order in which the instalments are computed and the way each one consumes the remaining total, which is what makes the distribution reproducible and free of drift.

operands.name: term lines
operands.source: the payment term of the document
operands.constraints: taken in the term's own line order, that is by identifier, which is creation order

operands.name: residual in company currency
operands.source: initialised to the company-currency total
operands.constraints: reduced by each instalment in turn

operands.name: residual in document currency
operands.source: initialised to the document-currency total
operands.constraints: reduced by each instalment in turn

preconditions.condition: The document has a payment term.
preconditions.otherwise: A single entry is produced instead, keyed on the document's own due date and valued at the signed totals.

preconditions.condition: The term has at least one line.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to distribute.

procedure: Initialise the company-currency residual to the company-currency total and the document-currency residual to the document-currency total.
Walk the term lines in the term's own line order, that is by identifier and therefore by creation order.
For each line compute its due date, then determine whether it is the last line of the term.
Apply the balance rule to the last line, the fixed rule to a fixed line and the percent rule to a percent line.
Apply the cash-rounding adjustment when a cash rounding rule exists and the line is not the balance line.
Subtract the two computed amounts from the two residuals, and move to the next line.
At the end of the walk both residuals are exactly zero, which is the invariant the balance line guarantees.
records.formula:
residual_amount ← residual_amount − company_amount
residual_amount_currency ← residual_amount_currency − foreign_amount
after the last line:  residual_amount = 0  and  residual_amount_currency = 0

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the carry-forward itself; it subtracts already rounded instalments.
rounding.precision: The rounding factors of the two currencies, carried by the instalments.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each instalment was rounded.
rounding.step: The subtraction happens after each instalment is computed and rounded, in line order.

result.name: the ordered list of instalments and the exhausted residuals
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the needed-terms map, which becomes the payable term lines of the document.

edge_cases.case: Two lines of the same term fall on the same maturity date and the same discount date.
edge_cases.outcome: Their amounts are merged into one entry of the needed-terms map, because the key is the pair of dates.

edge_cases.case: The term lines were created in an order different from their maturity dates.
edge_cases.outcome: The distribution still walks them by creation order; only the instalment index of the label is computed by maturity date.

edge_cases.case: The document has no payment term at all.
edge_cases.outcome: One entry is produced on the document's own due date, valued at the signed totals.

worked_examples.description: A term of thirty and seventy per cent on a bill of three thousand six hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: The first line takes thirty per cent, 1 080.00, leaving 2 520.00; the second line is the last and takes the whole residual, so the two instalments sum to exactly 3 600.00.

records.name: The early payment discount date and percentage of a distribution
records.purpose: Fixes the last day on which the reduced amount may be paid and the share by which the amount is reduced, which the payable term line carries alongside its ordinary maturity date.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the bill date when set, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

operands.name: discount days
operands.source: the day count of the early discount on the payment term
operands.constraints: strictly positive while the discount is enabled

operands.name: discount percentage
operands.source: the percentage of the early discount on the payment term
operands.constraints: strictly positive while the discount is enabled

preconditions.condition: The payment term enables the early payment discount.
preconditions.otherwise: No discount date and no discounted amount are produced, and the term line carries only its maturity date.

preconditions.condition: The payment term has exactly one line.
preconditions.otherwise: The term is refused, with the message that the early payment discount functionality can only be used with payment terms of a single line.

preconditions.condition: The discount percentage and the discount day count are both strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The term is refused, with the message that the early payment discount must be strictly positive, or that the early payment discount days must be strictly positive.

procedure: Take the percentage declared on the payment term as the discount percentage.
Add the discount day count to the reference date to obtain the discount date.
Attach both to the single entry the distribution produces, alongside the discounted balance and the discounted amount.
records.formula:
discount_percentage = the term's percentage
discount_date       = reference_date + discount_days

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the date is a whole calendar date and the percentage is stored as declared.
rounding.precision: One day for the date.

result.name: discount date and discount percentage
result.unit_or_currency: a calendar date and a percentage
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line, where they form part of the key of the needed-terms map and drive the reduced settlement.

edge_cases.case: The discount date falls after the maturity date.
edge_cases.outcome: The discount is meaningless in practice but is still recorded, since the two dates are independent.

edge_cases.case: The document has no bill date.
edge_cases.outcome: The accounting date, or today, serves as the reference date for the discount as well as for the maturity.

edge_cases.case: The discount is enabled on a term with several lines.
edge_cases.outcome: The term itself cannot be saved, so the case cannot reach the distribution.

worked_examples.description: Two per cent within ten days on a bill of 1 June 2026
worked_examples.narrative: Ten days after 1 June 2026 is 11 June 2026; paying on or before that date settles the bill at the discounted amount.

records.name: The discounted balance in the modes that never reduce the tax
records.purpose: Computes the reduced settlement amount when the discount is applied to the untaxed amount only, which is the behaviour of the mode that never reduces the tax and of the mode that books the reduction on the invoice itself.

operands.name: company-currency total
operands.source: the totals of the distribution
operands.constraints: already signed

operands.name: document-currency total
operands.source: the totals of the distribution
operands.constraints: already signed

operands.name: untaxed amount in company currency
operands.source: the untaxed total fed into the distribution
operands.constraints: already signed

operands.name: untaxed amount in document currency
operands.source: the untaxed total fed into the distribution
operands.constraints: already signed

operands.name: discount ratio
operands.source: the discount percentage divided by one hundred
operands.constraints: strictly between zero and one in practice

preconditions.condition: The tax-reduction mode of the payment term is the never-reduce mode, stored as `excluded`, or the always-upon-invoice mode, stored as `mixed`.
preconditions.otherwise: The mode that reduces the whole amount applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The early payment discount is enabled on the term.
preconditions.otherwise: No discounted balance is produced.

procedure: Divide the discount percentage by one hundred to obtain the discount ratio.
Multiply the untaxed amount by the discount ratio to obtain the reduction, in each currency separately.
Subtract the reduction from the total of the same currency.
Round each result to its own currency; the tax is left whole, because only the untaxed amount was reduced.
records.formula:
discounted_balance = round_to( company , total_amount − untaxed_amount × p )
discounted_amount  = round_to( document , total_amount_currency − untaxed_amount_currency × p )
where p = discount_percentage ÷ 100

rounding.what: The discounted balance and the discounted amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency and of the document currency respectively.
rounding.step: Once per currency, after the subtraction, and before the figure is stored on the term line.

result.name: discounted balance and discounted amount
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line as the amount that settles the document when it is paid on or before the discount date.

edge_cases.case: The document carries no tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The untaxed amount equals the total, so the two modes give the same figure as the mode that reduces the whole amount.

edge_cases.case: A cash rounding rule applies.
edge_cases.outcome: The discounted document-currency amount is cash-rounded and the discounted balance is recomputed from it.

edge_cases.case: The discount ratio is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The discounted amount equals the total, and no reduction is granted.

worked_examples.description: Two per cent on a bill of one thousand euros net and two hundred and ten euros of tax
worked_examples.narrative: The reduction of 20.00 applies to the net only, the 210.00 of tax being untouched, so the discounted amount is 1 190.00.

worked_examples.description: The same bill in the mode that books the reduction on the invoice
worked_examples.narrative: The arithmetic is identical to the never-reduce mode; the two modes differ in when the reduction is booked, not in the figure.

records.name: The discounted balance in the mode that reduces the tax on early payment
records.purpose: Computes the reduced settlement amount when the discount applies to the whole amount including the tax, which is the behaviour of the mode that reduces the tax only if the payment is actually anticipated.

operands.name: company-currency total
operands.source: the totals of the distribution
operands.constraints: already signed

operands.name: document-currency total
operands.source: the totals of the distribution
operands.constraints: already signed

operands.name: discount ratio
operands.source: the discount percentage divided by one hundred
operands.constraints: strictly between zero and one in practice

preconditions.condition: The tax-reduction mode of the payment term is the on-early-payment mode, stored as `included`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the two modes that spare the tax applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The early payment discount is enabled on the term.
preconditions.otherwise: No discounted balance is produced.

procedure: Divide the discount percentage by one hundred to obtain the discount ratio.
Subtract the discount ratio from one.
Multiply the total of each currency by that factor.
Round each result to its own currency; the tax is reduced in the same proportion as the net.
records.formula:
discounted_balance = round_to( company , total_amount × ( 1 − p ) )
discounted_amount  = round_to( document , total_amount_currency × ( 1 − p ) )
where p = discount_percentage ÷ 100

rounding.what: The discounted balance and the discounted amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency and of the document currency respectively.
rounding.step: Once per currency, after the multiplication, and before the figure is stored on the term line.

result.name: discounted balance and discounted amount
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line as the amount that settles the document when it is paid on or before the discount date.

edge_cases.case: The document carries no tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure coincides with the one the two other modes produce.

edge_cases.case: A cash rounding rule applies.
edge_cases.outcome: The discounted document-currency amount is cash-rounded and the discounted balance is recomputed from it.

edge_cases.case: The discount ratio is one.
edge_cases.outcome: The discounted amount is zero, which the strictly-positive constraints on the term make unreachable in practice.

worked_examples.description: Two per cent on a bill of one thousand two hundred and ten euros including tax
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand two hundred and ten multiplied by 0.98 is 1 185.80 exactly, so the payable term line of 1 210.00 due 1 July 2026 carries a discount date of 11 June 2026 and a discounted amount of 1 185.80.

records.name: The cash rounding of a discounted amount
records.purpose: Keeps the reduced settlement amount payable in the smallest coin available when the document carries a cash rounding rule.

operands.name: discounted amount in document currency
operands.source: one of the two discounted-balance rules
operands.constraints: already rounded to the document currency

operands.name: cash rounding difference
operands.source: the cash rounding rule of the document, applied to the discounted amount
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rate
operands.source: the rate derived from the two totals
operands.constraints: zero makes the recomputed balance zero

preconditions.condition: The document carries a cash rounding rule.
preconditions.otherwise: The discounted amount and the discounted balance stay as computed.

preconditions.condition: The early payment discount is enabled.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no discounted amount to round.

procedure: Apply the document's cash rounding rule to the discounted document-currency amount.
Recompute the discounted balance by dividing the cash-rounded amount by the rate and rounding to the company currency.
records.formula:
discounted_amount_currency = cash-rounded discounted amount
discounted_balance         = round_to( company , discounted_amount_currency ÷ rate )

rounding.what: The discounted amount, to the rule's rounding precision, then the discounted balance to the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding precision of the cash rounding rule, then the rounding factor of the company currency.
rounding.method: The rounding method of the rule for the cash rounding, half away from zero for the currency rounding.
rounding.step: After the discounted amount has been computed and before it is stored, the balance being derived from the rounded amount and not the other way round.

result.name: cash-rounded discounted amount and its balance
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line.

edge_cases.case: The discounted amount is already a multiple of the rounding precision.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing changes.

edge_cases.case: The rate is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The discounted balance is taken as zero.

worked_examples.description: A discounted amount of 1 185.80 under a rounding precision of five hundredths
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand one hundred and eighty-five euros and eighty cents is already a multiple of five hundredths, so the cash rounding changes nothing and the balance follows at a rate of one.

worked_examples.description: A discounted amount of 1 185.82 under the same rule
worked_examples.narrative: The two nearest multiples of five hundredths are 1 185.80 below and 1 185.85 above; 1 185.82 is two hundredths from the lower one and three from the upper one, so the difference is −0.02 and the settlement amount becomes 1 185.80.

records.name: The amount due after discount in the modes that never reduce the tax
records.purpose: Gives the simpler figure used for display and by the payment register, when the discount is applied to the untaxed amount only.

operands.name: total
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency the figure is asked in
operands.source: the total of the document
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill

operands.name: untaxed amount
operands.source: the untaxed total of the document
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill

operands.name: discount ratio
operands.source: the discount percentage divided by one hundred
operands.constraints: strictly between zero and one in practice

operands.name: cash rounding rule
operands.source: the rule carried by the document named by the calling context, when there is one
operands.constraints: optional

preconditions.condition: The tax-reduction mode is the never-reduce mode or the always-upon-invoice mode.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant for the on-early-payment mode applies.

preconditions.condition: The payment term grants an early payment discount.
preconditions.otherwise: The amount due is the total itself.

procedure: Subtract the untaxed amount from the total and multiply the difference by the discount ratio to obtain the discount amount.
Subtract the discount amount from the total.
Round the difference to the currency.
When the calling context names a document that carries a cash rounding rule, add that rule's difference and round again.
records.formula:
discount_amount = ( total − untaxed ) × p
amount_due      = round_to( currency , total − discount_amount )

rounding.what: The amount due.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency the figure is asked in, then the rounding precision of the cash rounding rule when one applies.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, then the method of the cash rounding rule.
rounding.step: After the subtraction, and again after the cash rounding difference has been added.

result.name: amount due after discount
result.unit_or_currency: the currency the figure is asked in
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the document and proposed by the payment register as the amount to pay when the payment date is within the discount period.

edge_cases.case: The document carries no tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference between the total and the untaxed amount is zero, so the discount amount is zero and the amount due is the total; this differs from the discounted balance of the distribution, which reduces the untaxed amount rather than the tax.

edge_cases.case: A cash rounding rule applies.
edge_cases.outcome: Its difference is added and the figure is rounded again.

edge_cases.case: No early payment discount exists.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount due is the residual of the document.

worked_examples.description: A bill of one thousand two hundred and ten euros with two hundred and ten euros of tax
worked_examples.narrative: The difference between the total and the untaxed amount is the tax of 210.00; two per cent of it is 4.20, so this display routine answers 1 205.80, which is the reduction applied to the tax part alone.

records.name: The amount due after discount in the mode that reduces the tax on early payment
records.purpose: Gives the simpler figure used for display and by the payment register, when the discount applies to the whole amount including the tax.

operands.name: total
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency the figure is asked in
operands.source: the total of the document
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill

operands.name: discount ratio
operands.source: the discount percentage divided by one hundred
operands.constraints: strictly between zero and one in practice

operands.name: cash rounding rule
operands.source: the rule carried by the document named by the calling context, when there is one
operands.constraints: optional

preconditions.condition: The tax-reduction mode is the on-early-payment mode, stored as `included`.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant for the two other modes applies.

preconditions.condition: The payment term grants an early payment discount.
preconditions.otherwise: The amount due is the total itself.

procedure: Multiply the total by the discount ratio to obtain the discount amount.
Subtract the discount amount from the total.
Round the difference to the currency.
When the calling context names a document that carries a cash rounding rule, add that rule's difference and round again.
records.formula:
discount_amount = total × p
amount_due      = round_to( currency , total − discount_amount )

rounding.what: The amount due.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency the figure is asked in, then the rounding precision of the cash rounding rule when one applies.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, then the method of the cash rounding rule.
rounding.step: After the subtraction, and again after the cash rounding difference has been added.

result.name: amount due after discount
result.unit_or_currency: the currency the figure is asked in
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the document and proposed by the payment register.

edge_cases.case: The document carries no tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure equals the discounted balance of the distribution.

edge_cases.case: A cash rounding rule applies.
edge_cases.outcome: Its difference is added and the figure is rounded again.

worked_examples.description: Two per cent of a bill of one thousand two hundred and ten euros
worked_examples.narrative: Two per cent of 1 210.00 is 24.20, so the amount due is 1 185.80, the same figure the distribution stores as the discounted amount.

records.name: The needed-terms map that becomes the payable term lines
records.purpose: Turns the instalments of the distribution into the exact set of payable term lines the document must carry, merging instalments that fall on the same dates and producing a single line when there is no payment term at all.

operands.name: instalments
operands.unit_or_currency: pairs of amounts in the company currency and the document currency
operands.source: the distribution over the term lines
operands.constraints: each carries a maturity date and, when a discount applies, a discount date, a discounted balance and a discounted amount

operands.name: document due date
operands.source: the due date of the document, used when there is no payment term
operands.constraints: may be empty, in which case the key carries no date

operands.name: signed totals
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
operands.source: the totals of the document, used when there is no payment term
operands.constraints: already signed

preconditions.condition: The document is invoice-like and carries at least one accountable line.
preconditions.otherwise: No payable term line is produced.

preconditions.condition: The document is still a draft when the amounts are recomputed from the base lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The stored totals are used instead.

procedure: Key each instalment by the triple made of the document, the maturity date and the discount date.
Value it by the company amount, the document amount, the discount date, the discounted balance and the discounted amount.
Merge two instalments that share a key by summing their amounts.
When the document has no payment term at all, produce a single entry keyed on the document's own due date and valued at the signed totals.
While the document is an unsaved draft, recompute the tax and untaxed amounts fed into the distribution from the base lines rather than reading the stored totals.

Create, update or delete payable term lines so that they match the map exactly, giving each line the payable account chosen by the payable account rule, the display type `payment_term`, the sequence 12000 so that term lines always sort last, the key's date as maturity date, and the label computed by the label rule.
records.formula:
needed_terms[ ( document , maturity_date , discount_date ) ] = ( company_amount , document_amount , discount_date , discounted_balance , discounted_amount )
merged value = the sum of the values of the instalments that share a key

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the map itself; it sums already rounded instalments.
rounding.precision: The rounding factors of the two currencies.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each instalment was rounded.
rounding.step: Before the merge, never after it.

result.name: the set of payable term lines of the document
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as journal items of display type `payment_term`, sorted last by their sequence of 12000, and reconciled against payments.

edge_cases.case: Two term lines fall on the same maturity date and the same discount date.
edge_cases.outcome: They are merged into a single payable term line whose amounts are the sums.

edge_cases.case: The document has no payment term.
edge_cases.outcome: One payable term line is produced on the document's own due date for the whole signed total.

edge_cases.case: A term line disappears because the total changed.
edge_cases.outcome: The synchronizer deletes the payable term line that no longer has a key in the map.

edge_cases.case: Two term lines share a maturity date but have different discount dates.
edge_cases.outcome: They are not merged, because the discount date is part of the key.

worked_examples.description: A single-line term on a bill of three thousand six hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: One key produces one payable term line, credited with 3 600.00 on the vendor's payable account and sorted last by its sequence of 12000.

worked_examples.description: Two term lines falling on the same date
worked_examples.narrative: The two instalments share the key, so they are merged into a single line of 1 500.00.

records.name: The label of a payable term line
records.purpose: Composes the text carried by each payable term line, which is what identifies the instalment on the payable ledger and on the payment allocation screens.

operands.name: payment reference
operands.source: the structured reference the payment must quote
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: vendor reference
operands.source: the reference the supplier printed on the document
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: number of term lines
operands.source: the payment term of the document
operands.constraints: one or more

operands.name: instalment index
operands.source: the one-based position of the line among the document's term lines sorted by maturity date, lines with no date sorting last
operands.constraints: counted from one

preconditions.condition: The payable term line exists in the needed-terms map.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no label to compose.

procedure: When the document has both a payment reference and a vendor reference and the two differ, take the vendor reference, a space, a hyphen, a space and the payment reference.
Otherwise, when it has a payment reference, take the payment reference.
Otherwise, when it is a bill or a vendor credit note and has a vendor reference, take the vendor reference.
Otherwise take the empty text.

When the payment term has more than one line, append a space, the word instalment, a space, a number sign and the one-based index of the line among the document's term lines sorted by maturity date, lines with no date sorting last.
Strip the leading space when the label was empty.
records.formula:
label = «vendor reference» - «payment reference»      when both exist and differ
label = «payment reference»                            when only that exists
label = «vendor reference»                             when the document is a bill or a vendor credit note and only that exists
label = empty                                          otherwise
label = «label» installment #«index»                   when the term has more than one line, the leading space being stripped when the label was empty

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the index is a whole count.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: label of the payable term line
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the journal item as its label and shown on the payable ledger and on the payment allocation screens.

edge_cases.case: The payment reference equals the vendor reference.
edge_cases.outcome: The first case does not apply, because it requires the two to differ, and the payment reference alone is used.

edge_cases.case: The document is a purchase receipt with only a vendor reference.
edge_cases.outcome: The third case requires a bill or a vendor credit note, so the label is empty for a receipt.

edge_cases.case: The term has several lines and the label would be empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The leading space is stripped, so the label is the instalment marker alone.

edge_cases.case: Two term lines have no maturity date.
edge_cases.outcome: They sort last among the term lines and are indexed in that position.

worked_examples.description: A bill with a vendor reference and a single-line term
worked_examples.narrative: There is no payment reference and the document is a bill, so the vendor reference alone is used and no instalment marker is appended.

worked_examples.description: The same bill under a two-instalment term
worked_examples.narrative: The term has more than one line, so each label carries its one-based index in maturity order.

worked_examples.description: A bill with both references
worked_examples.narrative: The two references differ, so both appear, joined by a space, a hyphen and a space.

records.name: The due date of the document
records.purpose: Gives the single date shown as the due date of the document, which is what the late group of the dashboard compares against today and what the ageing reports use.

operands.name: maturity dates of the payable term lines
operands.source: the payable term lines produced by the distribution
operands.constraints: at least one on a posted document

preconditions.condition: The document carries at least one payable term line with a maturity date.
preconditions.otherwise: The document has no due date and sorts last wherever documents are ordered by due date.

procedure: Collect the maturity dates of the payable term lines of the document.
Take the greatest of them as the due date of the document.
records.formula: invoice_date_due = max( maturity dates of the payment-term lines )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: due date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document as `invoice_date_due`, displayed as its due date, and compared with today by the late group of the purchase journal dashboard.

edge_cases.case: The document has several instalments.
edge_cases.outcome: The last maturity date is the due date, even though earlier instalments may already be overdue.

edge_cases.case: The document has no payment term.
edge_cases.outcome: The single payable term line carries the document's own due date, which is therefore also the maximum.

edge_cases.case: A term line has no maturity date.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not contribute to the maximum, the dated lines alone determining the due date.

worked_examples.description: A single instalment sixty days from end of month
worked_examples.narrative: The only maturity date is 29 June 2026, so that is the due date of the bill.

worked_examples.description: Two instalments, thirty per cent and seventy per cent
worked_examples.narrative: The maximum of the two maturity dates is 29 June 2026.

records.name: The payable account of a term line
records.purpose: Selects the account on which the amount owed to the supplier is credited, by walking an ordered list of sources and stopping at the first that answers.

operands.name: accounts of the other payable term lines of the same document
operands.source: the payment-term lines of the document other than the ones currently being computed
operands.constraints: the first such line found wins

operands.name: vendor payable account property
operands.source: the property `property_account_payable_id`, the payable account of the document's commercial partner, read in the document's company
operands.constraints: read per company

operands.name: company partner payable account property
operands.source: the same property on the company's own partner, read in the same company
operands.constraints: read per company

operands.name: first active payable account of the company
operands.source: an arbitrary but deterministic pick: for each pairing of a company and an account type, one account is chosen among the active accounts of that type belonging to that company
operands.constraints: the account type is the payable type

operands.name: fiscal position account mapping
operands.source: the account mapping of the fiscal position of the document
operands.constraints: applied after the account has been chosen

preconditions.condition: The line being computed is a payable term line.
preconditions.otherwise: The expense account rule applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The document has a commercial partner.
preconditions.otherwise: The vendor property cannot answer and the walk falls through to the company partner property.

procedure: Take the account already used by another payable term line of the same document, that is the account of a payment-term line other than the ones currently being computed, the first such line found; stop if one is found.
Otherwise take the payable account property of the document's commercial partner, read in the document's company; stop if it answers.
Otherwise take the payable account property of the company's own partner, read in the same company; stop if it answers.
Otherwise take the first active payable account of the company, chosen deterministically for that pairing of company and account type.
Then, when the document has a fiscal position, pass the chosen account through the position's account mapping and replace it by the mapped account.
For a sale document run the same walk with the receivable property and the receivable account type.
records.formula: payable_account = first non-empty of ( account of another payable term line of the document , vendor payable property , company partner payable property , first active payable account of the company ) , then mapped through the fiscal position

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the result is a chosen account.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: payable account of the term line
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payable term line and shown in the journal items of the document.

edge_cases.case: The document already has one payable term line with an account.
edge_cases.outcome: Every further term line takes that same account, so a multi-instalment document is homogeneous.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal position maps the payable account to another one.
edge_cases.outcome: The mapped account replaces the chosen one, whichever step of the walk produced it.

edge_cases.case: The company has no active payable account at all.
edge_cases.outcome: No account is found, and posting is refused because every accountable journal item must have an account.

edge_cases.case: A line that is not a payable term line sits on a payable account.
edge_cases.outcome: The payable-and-receivable coherence check refuses the document, since exactly the payable term lines may sit on payable accounts.

worked_examples.description: A vendor with its own payable account property
worked_examples.narrative: The first step finds nothing because this is the only term line, so the vendor's own property answers and the walk stops there.

worked_examples.description: A second instalment on the same document
worked_examples.narrative: The account already used by the first instalment wins over the vendor property, so both instalments sit on the same account.

records.name: The expense account of a product line
records.purpose: Selects the account a purchase line is charged to, preferring the product's own configuration, then the vendor's habits, then the neighbouring lines, and finally the journal's default.

operands.name: product accounts
operands.source: the accounts of the product read in the line's company and resolved through the document's fiscal position; the expense account for a purchase document and the income account for a sale document
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: most frequently used account for the partner
operands.source: the statistical rule over the partner's journal items
operands.constraints: answers only when at least one journal item matches

operands.name: accounts of the last two lines of the same display type
operands.source: the document's own lines
operands.constraints: used only when those two lines resolve to exactly one distinct account and the document has more than two lines in total

operands.name: journal default account
operands.source: the default account of the document's journal
operands.constraints: the final fallback

preconditions.condition: The line's display type is `product` and the document is invoice-like.
preconditions.otherwise: No expense account is computed; a presentation line never carries one.

preconditions.condition: The line is not a presentation line.
preconditions.otherwise: The neighbour rule and the journal default are not applied either.

procedure: When the line has a product, read the product's accounts in the line's company, resolved through the document's fiscal position, and take the expense account for a purchase document or the income account for a sale document; when that account is empty, keep the account already on the line.
Otherwise, when the line has a partner, take the most frequently used account for that partner and use it when one is found.

Then, for any line still without an account and not a presentation line, look at the accounts of the last two lines of the same display type on the document; when those two lines resolve to exactly one distinct account and the document has more than two lines in total, use that account.
Otherwise use the journal's default account.
records.formula:
expense_account = product expense account resolved through the fiscal position
expense_account = most frequently used account of the partner            when the line has no product
expense_account = the single account of the last two lines of the same display type   when the document has more than two lines
expense_account = the journal's default account                          otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the result is a chosen account.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: expense account of the line
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the journal item and shown in the lines of the document.

edge_cases.case: The product has no expense account and the line already carries one.
edge_cases.outcome: The existing account is kept rather than cleared.

edge_cases.case: The last two lines of the same display type use two different accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: The neighbour rule does not apply and the journal default is used.

edge_cases.case: The document has exactly two lines.
edge_cases.outcome: The neighbour rule is not applied, because it requires more than two lines in total.

edge_cases.case: The chosen account is archived at posting time.
edge_cases.outcome: Posting is refused unless the line is marked imported or the deprecation check is skipped.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal position maps the product's expense account.
edge_cases.outcome: The mapped account is used, the resolution happening as the product accounts are read.

records.name: The most frequently used account for a partner
records.purpose: Answers which account this vendor's charges usually land on, by counting the partner's recent journal items, so that a line without a product is charged where the previous ones were.

operands.name: company
operands.source: the company of the document
operands.constraints: part of the cache key

operands.name: partner
operands.source: the partner of the line
operands.constraints: part of the cache key

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the type of the document
operands.constraints: part of the cache key; it decides which account types are eligible

operands.name: window of journal items
operands.source: the journal items of that company for that partner whose account is active and whose date is on or after two years, that is seven hundred and thirty days, before today
operands.constraints: may be empty

preconditions.condition: The partner is set on the line.
preconditions.otherwise: The rule is not consulted at all.

preconditions.condition: At least one journal item matches the filters.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no answer, and the caller falls through to the neighbour rule of the expense account walk.

procedure: Consider the journal items of that company whose partner is the given partner, whose account is active, and whose date is on or after two years, that is seven hundred and thirty days, before today.

Restrict by document type: for a type whose name begins with the outbound marker `out_` keep only accounts of the income type; for a type whose name begins with the inbound marker `in_` keep only accounts of the expense type, the fixed asset type or the direct cost of revenue type.
Group the survivors by account and count the matching journal items in each group.
Order the groups by that count descending and then by the account code ascending as a tie-break.
Take the first group's account as the answer.
Cache the answer for the triple of company, partner and document type for the duration of the request.
records.formula:
most_frequent_account = the account of the group that maximises ( count of matching journal items ) , ties broken by the smallest account code
window = journal items dated on or after today − 730 days

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the counts are whole numbers.
rounding.precision: One journal item.

result.name: most frequently used account
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; used as a default when a line without a product is created, and cached for the duration of the request.

edge_cases.case: Two accounts have the same count.
edge_cases.outcome: The account with the smaller code wins, so the answer is deterministic.

edge_cases.case: Every matching journal item is older than two years.
edge_cases.outcome: The window is empty and there is no answer.

edge_cases.case: The partner's items sit on archived accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: Those items are excluded, because only active accounts are considered.

edge_cases.case: The document is a purchase type.
edge_cases.outcome: Only expense, fixed asset and direct cost of revenue accounts are eligible, so an income account is never proposed on a bill.

worked_examples.narrative: Seven items against three, so the telephone account wins.

worked_examples.description: A tie between two accounts
worked_examples.narrative: The counts are equal, so the smaller code wins and the office supplies account is proposed.

records.name: The most frequent account and taxes used by quick encoding
records.purpose: Answers both an account and a set of taxes for a vendor, so that typing a single tax-inclusive total can generate a line that matches how this vendor's charges are usually booked.

operands.name: company
operands.source: the company of the document
operands.constraints: restricts the journal items considered

operands.name: partner
operands.source: the vendor of the document
operands.constraints: when it is empty the answer is a count of zero, no account and no taxes

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the type of the document
operands.constraints: decides the direction, an inbound type selecting income accounts and an outbound type, which covers every bill and purchase receipt, selecting expense accounts

operands.name: window of journal items
operands.source: the journal items of that company, for that partner, dated within the last two years
operands.constraints: may be empty

preconditions.condition: The partner is set.
preconditions.otherwise: The answer is the triple made of a count of zero, no account and no taxes.

preconditions.condition: The company's quick encoding setting covers purchase journals.
preconditions.otherwise: The routine is not consulted at all.

procedure: Consider the journal items of that company, for that partner, dated within the last two years.

Restrict by direction: for an inbound type keep accounts whose internal group is income; for an outbound type, which covers every bill and purchase receipt, keep accounts whose internal group is expense.
For each journal item collect its account, its account code and the list of taxes attached to it.
Group by the pair made of the account and the list of taxes.
Order the groups by the count of items descending, then by the tax list ascending with empty lists last.
Take the first group and answer the triple made of the count, the account and the tax identifiers.
records.formula:
answer = ( count , account , tax identifiers ) of the group that maximises the count of journal items , ties broken by the ascending tax list with empty lists last
answer = ( 0 , none , none )   when the partner is empty

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the count is a whole number.
rounding.precision: One journal item.

result.name: count, account and taxes
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the quick encoding routine, which uses the account and the taxes when the count is not zero.

edge_cases.case: The count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Quick encoding falls back to the journal's default account and to the purchase-typed taxes attached to it, then to the company's default purchase tax.

edge_cases.case: Two groups have the same count, one with taxes and one without.
edge_cases.outcome: The group with taxes wins, because empty tax lists sort last.

edge_cases.case: The same account was used with two different tax sets.
edge_cases.outcome: The two form distinct groups, so the most frequent combination wins rather than the most frequent account.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: The outbound direction applies and only accounts whose internal group is expense are considered.

worked_examples.narrative: With no partner the routine answers a count of zero, and quick encoding falls back to the journal default.

records.name: The amount in words when the amount has a fractional part
records.purpose: Produces the spelled-out amount printed on a cheque and on the document, in the two-part form that names both the currency unit and its subunit.

operands.name: amount
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the payment or of the document
operands.source: the amount to spell
operands.constraints: may be any amount the currency can represent

operands.name: number of decimal places of the currency
operands.source: the currency, being two for a currency whose rounding factor is one hundredth
operands.constraints: a whole number, zero or more

operands.name: currency unit label
operands.source: the per-currency translatable text naming the unit, for instance Dollars for the United States dollar and Euros for the euro
operands.constraints: translated into the user's language

operands.name: currency subunit label
operands.source: the per-currency translatable text naming the subunit, Cents for both of those currencies
operands.constraints: translated into the user's language

operands.name: language
operands.source: the user's language, reduced to its two-letter code
operands.constraints: an unsupported language falls back to English

preconditions.condition: A textual-number facility is available.
preconditions.otherwise: The answer is the empty text and a warning is logged.

preconditions.condition: The amount less its integral part is not zero for the currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The single-part form applies instead.

procedure: Format the amount with exactly as many digits after the point as the currency has decimal places.
Split the formatted text at the point into the integral part and the fractional part.
Read the integral part as a whole number.
Resolve the user's language and take its two-letter code.

Render each number in words in that language and apply title casing, that is upper-case the first letter of every maximal run of letters and lower-case the rest; render in English and title-case that when the language is unsupported.
Read the fractional digit string as a whole number, an empty string reading as zero.
Join the spelled integer, a space, the currency unit label, the word and, the spelled fractional part and the currency subunit label.
records.formula: words = spell( integer_value ) + " " + currency_unit_label + " and " + spell( fractional_part_as_integer ) + " " + currency_subunit_label

rounding.what: The amount is formatted, not rounded again: it is written with exactly the number of decimal places of the currency, which fixes the digits the fractional part is read from.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal places of the currency, two for a currency whose rounding factor is one hundredth.
rounding.method: The formatting follows the currency's own decimal places; the amount reaching this step has already been rounded half away from zero.
rounding.step: At the formatting step, before the text is split at the point.

result.name: amount in words
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown as the amount in words of a cheque, exactly as produced, and as the total in words of a document with every comma removed.

edge_cases.case: The language is not supported by the textual-number facility.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is rendered in English and title-cased.

edge_cases.case: The fractional digit string is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: It reads as zero.

edge_cases.case: A hyphen appears inside a spelled number.
edge_cases.outcome: Title casing capitalises after the hyphen as well, because a hyphen is not a letter, so fifty-six becomes Fifty-Six.

edge_cases.case: No textual-number facility is available.
edge_cases.outcome: The answer is the empty text and a warning is logged, and the fill rule then yields an empty line rather than two hundred asterisks.

records.name: The amount in words when the amount has no fractional part
records.purpose: Produces the spelled-out amount in the single-part form, used when the amount is whole in its currency so that no subunit needs naming.

operands.name: amount
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the payment or of the document
operands.source: the amount to spell
operands.constraints: whole in its currency

operands.name: number of decimal places of the currency
operands.source: the currency
operands.constraints: a whole number, zero or more

operands.name: currency unit label
operands.source: the per-currency translatable text naming the unit
operands.constraints: translated into the user's language

preconditions.condition: A textual-number facility is available.
preconditions.otherwise: The answer is the empty text and a warning is logged.

preconditions.condition: The amount less its integral part is zero for the currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The two-part form applies instead.

procedure: Format the amount with exactly as many digits after the point as the currency has decimal places and split it at the point.
Read the integral part as a whole number.
Test whether the amount less that whole number is zero for the currency.
When it is, render the whole number in words in the user's language, apply title casing, and join it to the currency unit label with a single space.
records.formula: words = spell( integer_value ) + " " + currency_unit_label

rounding.what: The comparison that selects this form: the difference between the amount and its integral part is rounded to the currency and compared with zero.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency.
rounding.step: After the split, before the form is chosen.

result.name: amount in words
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown as the amount in words of a cheque and, with commas removed, as the total in words of a document.

edge_cases.case: The fractional digits are present but all zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero for the currency, so the single-part form is used and the zero subunit is not named.

edge_cases.case: The currency has no decimal places at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The formatted text has no point, the fractional part is empty and the single-part form always applies.

edge_cases.case: The amount is zero.

result.name: total amount in words
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the printed document; the cheque uses the unmodified text instead.

edge_cases.outcome: The two texts are identical.

records.purpose: Pads the spelled amount to a fixed width with asterisks so that nobody can add words after it on a printed cheque.

operands.source: the amount-in-words rule applied to the payment amount
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: target width
operands.source: the fixed width of the printed line
operands.constraints: exactly two hundred characters

preconditions.otherwise: The filled line is empty as well, rather than two hundred asterisks.

result.name: filled amount-in-words line

result.stored_or_displayed: Printed on the cheque, and on the first page only when the stub spills over several pages, later pages carrying the literal text `VOID` instead.

records.name: The cash rounding difference with the nearest method
records.purpose: Computes by how much the total of a document has to move so that it becomes payable in the smallest coin in circulation, when the rule rounds to the nearest multiple.

operands.name: amount
operands.source: the amount to be made payable, usually the total of the document or one instalment of it
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding precision
operands.source: the rounding precision of the cash rounding rule, that is the smallest coin
operands.constraints: strictly positive, otherwise the rule is refused with the message that a strictly positive rounding value must be set

operands.name: currency rounding factor
operands.source: the smallest representable step of the currency
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The document carries a cash rounding rule.
preconditions.otherwise: No difference is computed and no rounding line is produced.

preconditions.condition: The rounding precision of the rule is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The rule cannot be saved; the message is "Please set a strictly positive rounding value."

procedure: Round the amount to the currency first, so that the comparison is made between two representable figures.
Round that figure to the nearest multiple of the rounding precision, halves going up.
Subtract the currency-rounded amount from the multiple so obtained.
Round the subtraction to the currency and answer it as the difference.
records.formula:
rounded( amount )            = round( amount , to a multiple of rounding_precision , using the nearest method )
difference( currency , amount ) = round_to( currency , rounded( round_to( currency , amount ) ) − round_to( currency , amount ) )

rounding.what: The amount, twice: first to the currency, then to a multiple of the rounding precision, and finally the difference itself back to the currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency, then the rounding precision of the rule, then the rounding factor of the currency again.
rounding.method: Half away from zero for the currency rounding; the nearest method, stored as `HALF-UP`, for the cash rounding.
rounding.step: The currency rounding comes first, the cash rounding second, and the difference is rounded last.

result.name: cash rounding difference
result.stored_or_displayed: Carried by the rounding line of the document, or applied to the biggest tax, depending on the strategy of the rule.

edge_cases.case: The amount is already a multiple of the rounding precision.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero and no rounding line is created.

edge_cases.case: The amount is exactly halfway between two multiples.
edge_cases.outcome: The nearest method sends it upwards.

edge_cases.case: The rounding precision is one.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is moved to a whole currency unit.

edge_cases.case: The amount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The same arithmetic applies, and the difference may be positive.

records.name: The cash rounding difference with the upwards method
records.purpose: Computes the movement of the total when the cash rounding rule always rounds to the next multiple upwards.

operands.name: amount
operands.source: the amount to be made payable
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding precision
operands.source: the rounding precision of the cash rounding rule
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The rounding method of the rule is the upwards method, stored as `UP`.
preconditions.otherwise: The nearest method or the downwards method applies.

procedure: Round the amount to the currency.
Move it up to the next multiple of the rounding precision, leaving it unchanged when it already is one.
Subtract the currency-rounded amount and round the difference to the currency.
records.formula:
rounded( amount )            = the smallest multiple of rounding_precision that is not smaller than amount
difference( currency , amount ) = round_to( currency , rounded( round_to( currency , amount ) ) − round_to( currency , amount ) )

rounding.what: The amount, to a multiple of the rounding precision, and the difference back to the currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency, then the rounding precision of the rule.
rounding.method: Always upwards for the cash rounding; half away from zero for the currency rounding.
rounding.step: The currency rounding first, the cash rounding second, the difference last.

result.name: cash rounding difference
result.stored_or_displayed: Carried by the rounding line or applied to the biggest tax.

edge_cases.case: The amount is already a multiple.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero.

edge_cases.case: The amount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: Rounding upwards moves it towards zero.

records.name: The cash rounding difference with the downwards method
records.purpose: Computes the movement of the total when the cash rounding rule always rounds to the previous multiple downwards.

operands.name: amount
operands.source: the amount to be made payable
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding precision
operands.source: the rounding precision of the cash rounding rule
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The rounding method of the rule is the downwards method, stored as `DOWN`.
preconditions.otherwise: The nearest method or the upwards method applies.

procedure: Round the amount to the currency.
Move it down to the previous multiple of the rounding precision, leaving it unchanged when it already is one.
Subtract the currency-rounded amount and round the difference to the currency.
records.formula:
rounded( amount )            = the largest multiple of rounding_precision that is not larger than amount
difference( currency , amount ) = round_to( currency , rounded( round_to( currency , amount ) ) − round_to( currency , amount ) )

rounding.what: The amount, to a multiple of the rounding precision, and the difference back to the currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency, then the rounding precision of the rule.
rounding.method: Always downwards for the cash rounding; half away from zero for the currency rounding.
rounding.step: The currency rounding first, the cash rounding second, the difference last.

result.name: cash rounding difference
result.stored_or_displayed: Carried by the rounding line or applied to the biggest tax.

edge_cases.case: The amount is already a multiple.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero.

edge_cases.case: The amount is smaller than one rounding precision.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounded figure is zero and the difference is the negated amount.

records.name: Booking the cash rounding difference on a purchase document
records.purpose: Places the cash rounding difference in the document, either as an added line or by modifying the largest tax, and selects the account that receives it.

operands.name: cash rounding difference
operands.source: one of the three rounding-method rules
operands.constraints: zero produces nothing

operands.name: strategy
operands.source: the strategy of the cash rounding rule, either adding a rounding line, stored as `add_invoice_line` and the default, or modifying the tax amount, stored as `biggest_tax`
operands.constraints: exactly one of the two

operands.name: profit account
operands.source: the profit account of the cash rounding rule
operands.constraints: used when the difference increases what is owed

operands.name: loss account
operands.source: the loss account of the cash rounding rule
operands.constraints: used when the difference reduces what is owed

preconditions.condition: The difference is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No rounding line is added and no tax is modified.

preconditions.condition: The document carries a cash rounding rule.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is booked.

procedure: Compute the difference under the rule's rounding method.
Under the strategy that adds a rounding line, create a line carrying the difference, booked to the loss account when it reduces what is owed and to the profit account otherwise.
Under the strategy that modifies the tax amount, apply the difference to the largest tax of the document rather than creating a line.
Let the rounding line participate in the untaxed total, or in the tax total when it carries a tax distribution line.
Compute the payable term line from the cash-rounded total, the distribution applying the cash rounding to every instalment except the balance line.
records.formula:
rounding_line_amount = difference( document_currency , amount_total )
account = the loss account   when the difference reduces what is owed
account = the profit account otherwise

rounding.what: The document total, moved to a multiple of the rule's rounding precision.
rounding.precision: The rounding precision of the rule, then the rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.method: The rounding method of the rule, that is upwards, downwards or nearest.
rounding.step: After the totals have been computed and before the payment term distributes them, so that the instalments are computed from the cash-rounded total.

result.name: rounding line or modified tax
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as a line of the document, counted in the untaxed total or in the tax total, and visible in the totals block.

edge_cases.case: The difference is zero.

operands.name: purchase unit of the matching supplier record

preconditions.condition: The document is not a hashed entry.

procedure: Read the product in the language of the document's partner when it has one, otherwise in the language of the line's partner.

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the result is a text.

result.name: label of the line
