records.name: The unit price of a bill line
records.purpose: Derives the price proposed on a purchase line from the product's stored cost, converting it between units, adapting it to a fiscal position and restating it in the document currency.

operands.name: base price
operands.source: the product's standard price read in the document's company
operands.constraints: read per company

operands.name: base currency
operands.source: the company of the document
operands.constraints: the currency the standard price is expressed in

operands.name: base taxes
operands.source: the product's supplier taxes, filtered to the company
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: line unit
operands.source: the unit chosen for the line
operands.constraints: may differ from the product's reference unit

operands.name: document date
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: used to read the conversion rate

preconditions.condition: The line is not marked as imported.
preconditions.otherwise: The line is skipped entirely, so a decoder's price is never overwritten.

preconditions.condition: The line carries a product.
preconditions.otherwise: No price is derived.

procedure: Read the product's standard price in the document's company, expressed in the company currency, together with the product's supplier taxes filtered to that company.
When the line's unit differs from the product's reference unit, convert the price between the two units.
When there are taxes and the document has a fiscal position, adapt the price so that the amount payable is preserved when the original taxes are replaced by the mapped ones.
When the document currency differs from the base currency, convert at the document's date, without rounding.
Write the result to the unit price, skipping the line entirely when it is marked as imported.
records.formula: unit_price = base_price , converted between the line unit and the product's reference unit , adapted for the fiscal position so that the amount payable is preserved , then converted from the company currency to the document currency at the document's date without rounding

rounding.what: The currency conversion of the price is performed without rounding; the value is rounded only when it is stored, at the decimal precision of the product price with a minimum display precision.
rounding.precision: The decimal precision named for product prices, with a minimum display precision; the currency conversion itself keeps full precision.
rounding.method: Half away from zero when the stored value is rounded.
rounding.step: The conversion happens without rounding; rounding occurs only at storage.

result.name: unit price of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency, per line unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the line and multiplied by the quantity to give the amount in currency.

edge_cases.case: The line is marked as imported.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is written, so a price decoded from the supplier's document survives.

edge_cases.case: The line unit is a multiple of the reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The price is converted accordingly, so a price per unit becomes a price per dozen.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal position maps a tax to another with a different rate.
edge_cases.outcome: The price is adapted so that the amount payable is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The document is in a foreign currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion uses the document's date and is not rounded before storage.

records.name: The taxes of a bill line
records.purpose: Chooses the taxes a purchase line carries, preferring the product's supplier taxes and falling back to the taxes attached to the account, then mapping them through the fiscal position.

operands.name: supplier taxes of the product
operands.source: the product, filtered to the document's company
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: purchase-typed taxes of the account
operands.source: the account on the line
operands.constraints: used only when the product has none

operands.name: fiscal position
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: maps the candidates when it exists

preconditions.condition: The line is not a presentation line, not a payable term line, not a cost-of-goods line and not marked as imported.
preconditions.otherwise: The recomputation is skipped entirely.

preconditions.condition: The line has a product, or is a discount line, or the account carries taxes, or the line already has taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: The recomputation is skipped, so that clearing the account never silently clears manually chosen taxes.

procedure: Take the product's supplier taxes, filtered to the document's company, as the candidates.
When the product has none, take instead the purchase-typed taxes attached to the line's account.
Filter the candidates to the line's company.
When the document has a fiscal position, map the candidates through it.

Skip the whole recomputation on presentation lines, on payable term lines, on cost-of-goods lines and on imported lines, and skip it as well when the line has no product, is not a discount line and there are neither account taxes nor existing taxes.
records.formula:
candidate_taxes = the product's supplier taxes, filtered to the document's company
candidate_taxes = the purchase-typed taxes attached to the line's account, when the product has none
taxes = candidate_taxes filtered to the line's company and mapped through the fiscal position

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the result is a set of taxes.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: taxes of the line
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a set of tax references
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the line; the tax engine derives the tax lines of the document from them.

edge_cases.case: The line is marked as imported.
edge_cases.outcome: The taxes are left as decoded from the supplier's document.

edge_cases.case: The account is cleared on a line with hand-chosen taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The guard skips the recomputation, so the taxes are not silently cleared.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal position maps a domestic tax to an intra-community one.
edge_cases.outcome: The mapped tax replaces the candidate.

edge_cases.case: A cash-basis tax and an ordinary tax would share a tax grid.
edge_cases.outcome: The document is refused by the rule that forbids mixing them.

records.name: The default quantity of a line
records.purpose: Fixes the quantity a newly created line carries, so that a product line multiplies its unit price by one and a line of any other kind carries no quantity at all.

operands.name: display type of the line
operands.source: the line
operands.constraints: a product line, a payable term line, a tax line, a rounding line, a private-share line or a presentation line

preconditions.condition: The line is being created or its display type changes.
preconditions.otherwise: The quantity is left as the user set it.

procedure: When the line's display type is a product line, set the quantity to one.
For every other kind of line, force the quantity to be empty.
Derive the account of the line by the expense account rule.
records.formula:
quantity = 1        on a product line
quantity = empty    on every other kind of line

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the default quantity is the whole number one, and quantities entered by the user are held at the decimal precision named for product units.
rounding.precision: The decimal precision named for product units.
rounding.method: Half away from zero when a computed quantity is stored.
rounding.step: Not applicable to the default itself.

result.name: quantity of the line

records.name: The non-deductible percentage and subtotal of a product line
records.purpose: Measures the private share of an expense line, that is the part of it that is not business use and whose input tax may not be reclaimed.

operands.name: deductibility
operands.source: the deductibility carried by the product line of a purchase document, one hundred by default
operands.constraints: compared at two decimal digits; a value below one hundred means part of the expense is private

operands.name: line subtotal
operands.source: the tax-excluded subtotal of the product line
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill

preconditions.condition: The document is a draft purchase document with at least one product line whose deductibility is below one hundred per cent.
preconditions.otherwise: No private-share line is generated at all.

preconditions.condition: The line's display type is a product line.
preconditions.otherwise: Deductibility does not apply to it.

procedure: Divide the deductibility by one hundred and subtract the quotient from one to obtain the private percentage.
Multiply the line subtotal by that percentage.
Round the product to the document currency to obtain the non-deductible subtotal.
Regenerate the private-share lines whenever the multiset of label, subtotal, taxes, deductibility and account over the document's product lines changes.
records.formula:
percentage              = 1 − deductibility ÷ 100
non_deductible_subtotal = round_to( document_currency , line_subtotal × percentage )

rounding.what: The non-deductible subtotal.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency; deductibility itself is compared at two decimal digits.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the private percentage, before the base amounts are derived.

result.name: non-deductible subtotal
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as such; it is the figure from which the private-share base amounts of both currencies are derived.

edge_cases.case: The deductibility is one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The private percentage is zero, the subtotal is zero and no private-share line is created for that line.

edge_cases.case: The deductibility is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole line is private and the non-deductible subtotal equals the line subtotal.

edge_cases.case: The document is posted.
edge_cases.outcome: The private-share lines are not regenerated, the regeneration being restricted to drafts.

edge_cases.case: Two product lines share a label, a subtotal, a tax set, a deductibility and an account.
edge_cases.outcome: Each still produces its own private-share line, the multiset only deciding when the regeneration runs.

records.name: The non-deductible base of a product line in both currencies
records.purpose: Turns the private share of a line into the signed amounts the private-share line carries, in the document currency and in the company currency.

operands.name: non-deductible subtotal
operands.source: the private percentage applied to the line subtotal
operands.constraints: zero or more

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the document type
operands.constraints: plus one on a vendor bill

operands.name: document rate
operands.source: the currency rate of the document
operands.constraints: a rate of zero makes the company-currency figure zero

preconditions.condition: The non-deductible subtotal is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No private-share line is produced for that product line.

preconditions.condition: The document rate is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The company-currency base is taken as zero.

procedure: Multiply the non-deductible subtotal by the direction sign and round to the document currency to obtain the base in the document currency.
Divide the same signed product by the document rate and round to the company currency to obtain the base in the company currency, taking zero when the rate is zero.
records.formula:
non_deductible_base         = round_to( document_currency , sign × non_deductible_subtotal )
non_deductible_base_company = round_to( company_currency , sign × non_deductible_subtotal ÷ rate )   ( 0 when the rate is 0 )

rounding.what: Each of the two base amounts.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency and of the company currency respectively.
rounding.step: Once per currency, after the multiplication by the direction sign and, for the company currency, after the division by the rate.

result.name: non-deductible base amounts
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Negated onto the private-share product line and summed onto the aggregate private-share line.

edge_cases.case: The document is in the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is one and the two figures are equal.

edge_cases.case: The rate is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The company-currency base is zero while the document-currency base keeps its value.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is minus one and both figures are negated.

records.name: The private-share product line
records.purpose: Removes the private fraction of an expense from the expense account by adding a negative line on the same account, carrying the same taxes so that the tax engine reduces the deductible tax accordingly.

operands.name: non-deductible base in document currency
operands.source: the base rule
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill before negation

operands.name: non-deductible base in company currency
operands.source: the base rule
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill before negation

operands.name: account of the product line
operands.source: the product line the private share belongs to
operands.constraints: the private-share line uses the same account

operands.name: taxes of the product line
operands.source: the product line, excluding fixed-amount taxes
operands.constraints: fixed-amount taxes are dropped, since a fixed amount cannot be apportioned

operands.name: sequence of the product line
operands.source: the product line
operands.constraints: the private-share line takes that sequence plus one

preconditions.condition: The document is a draft purchase document with at least one product line below one hundred per cent deductibility.
preconditions.otherwise: No private-share line exists.

preconditions.condition: The non-deductible base is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No line is created.

procedure: Create a line on the same account as the product line, with display type `non_deductible_product`.
Give it the product line's label.
Set its balance to the negated non-deductible base in the company currency and its amount in currency to the negated non-deductible base in the document currency.
Give it the product line's taxes, excluding fixed-amount taxes.
Give it the product line's sequence plus one, so that it sits immediately after the line it corrects.
records.formula:
balance            = − non_deductible_base_company
amount_in_currency = − non_deductible_base
sequence           = product line sequence + 1

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded; the two amounts were rounded when the bases were computed.
rounding.precision: The rounding factors of the two currencies.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied at the base computation.
rounding.step: Before the negation, never after it.

result.name: private-share product line
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as a journal item of display type `non_deductible_product`, counted in the untaxed total, and visible among the lines of the document.

edge_cases.outcome: That tax is excluded from the private-share line, so a fixed amount is never apportioned.

edge_cases.outcome: Each produces its own private-share line, immediately after itself in sequence.

edge_cases.case: The private-share line sits on the expense account.
edge_cases.outcome: It is a credit on a vendor bill, so the net charge on the expense account is the deductible part alone.

records.name: The aggregate private-share line
records.purpose: Gathers the private fractions of every partly deductible line onto a single account, so that the total private share of the document is visible as one figure.

operands.name: non-deductible bases in company currency
operands.source: every private-share product line of the document
operands.constraints: one per partly deductible product line

operands.name: non-deductible bases in document currency
operands.source: the same lines
operands.constraints: one per partly deductible product line

operands.name: private share account of the journal
operands.source: the journal of the document, falling back to the journal's default account
operands.constraints: must resolve, since every accountable journal item needs an account

operands.name: highest sequence on the document
operands.source: the lines of the document
operands.constraints: the aggregate line takes one more than that

preconditions.condition: At least one private-share product line exists.
preconditions.otherwise: No aggregate line is created.

preconditions.condition: The journal has a private share account, or failing that a default account.
preconditions.otherwise: No account can be found and the document cannot be posted.

procedure: Sum the non-deductible base amounts in the company currency over the private-share product lines to obtain the balance.
Sum the same amounts in the document currency to obtain the amount in currency.
Create one line on the journal's private share account, falling back to the journal's default account, with display type `non_deductible_product_total`.
Label it as the private part, that label being replaced at posting by the document number, a space, a hyphen, a space and the words private part.
Give it no taxes and a sequence of one more than the highest sequence on the document, so that it sits last among the accountable lines.
records.formula:
balance            = Σ non_deductible_base_company over the private-share product lines
amount_in_currency = Σ non_deductible_base over the private-share product lines
sequence           = highest sequence on the document + 1

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded; the sums are of already rounded amounts.
rounding.precision: The rounding factors of the two currencies.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied to each base before the sum.
rounding.step: The sum is taken after each base has been rounded.

result.name: aggregate private-share line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as a journal item of display type `non_deductible_product_total` on the private share account, labelled with the document number and the words private part once the document is posted.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no private share account.
edge_cases.outcome: The journal's default account is used.

edge_cases.case: Several partly deductible lines exist.
edge_cases.outcome: A single aggregate line carries the sum of all their private shares.

edge_cases.case: The document is posted.
edge_cases.outcome: The label becomes the document number followed by a hyphen and the words private part.

records.name: The non-deductible tax line
records.purpose: Moves the input tax on the private fraction out of the deductible tax account and onto the private share account, so that only the business share of the tax is reclaimed.

operands.name: tax-included total of each non-deductible base line
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
operands.source: the tax engine, evaluated over the negative base lines
operands.constraints: evaluated in both currencies

operands.name: tax-excluded total of each non-deductible base line
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
operands.source: the same
operands.constraints: evaluated in both currencies

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the document type
operands.constraints: plus one on a vendor bill

operands.name: account for the non-deductible tax
operands.source: the existing non-deductible tax line's account when one exists, otherwise the journal's private share account, otherwise the journal's default account
operands.constraints: must resolve

preconditions.condition: At least one private-share product line carries a tax.
preconditions.otherwise: No non-deductible tax line is produced.

preconditions.condition: The document is a draft purchase document.
preconditions.otherwise: The private-share lines are not regenerated.

procedure: Let the tax engine evaluate the negative base lines produced by the private-share rule.
For each of those base lines take the difference between the tax-included total and the tax-excluded total.
Multiply that difference by the negated direction sign and sum over the base lines, in both currencies.
Book the result to the existing non-deductible tax line's account when one exists, otherwise to the journal's private share account, otherwise to the journal's default account.
Give the line the display type `non_deductible_tax` and the label naming the private part and its taxes, replaced at posting by the document number, a hyphen and the same words.
records.formula: non_deductible_tax_amount = Σ over the non-deductible base lines of  − sign × ( total_included − total_excluded )

rounding.what: The tax amount, in each currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency and of the company currency respectively.
rounding.step: Once per currency, as the tax engine rounds each tax total, before the sum.

result.name: non-deductible tax amount
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as a journal item of display type `non_deductible_tax`, counted in the tax total of the document, and labelled with the document number and the words private part and taxes once the document is posted.

edge_cases.case: The private-share line carries no tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero and no non-deductible tax line is produced.

edge_cases.case: A non-deductible tax line already exists.
edge_cases.outcome: Its own account is reused rather than the journal's private share account.

edge_cases.case: The private share is one hundred per cent of the line.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole input tax of that line is moved to the private share account and none of it is reclaimed.

edge_cases.case: The payable term line.
edge_cases.outcome: It is unchanged, because the supplier is still owed the full amount including the whole tax.

records.name: The remaining amount to encode under quick encoding
records.purpose: Measures how much of the typed tax-inclusive total is not yet covered by the lines already on the document, which is the amount the generated line must carry.

operands.name: typed total
operands.source: the tax-inclusive total the user typed into the quick encoding field
operands.constraints: positive in the ordinary case

operands.name: current tax-inclusive total of the document
operands.source: the total of the lines already present
operands.constraints: zero on an empty document

preconditions.condition: The company's quick encoding setting covers purchase journals.
preconditions.otherwise: No total field is shown and no line is generated.

preconditions.condition: A total has been typed.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is generated.

procedure: Ask the most frequent account and taxes rule for this vendor and this document type.
When it answered a non-zero count, use that account and those taxes.

Otherwise use the journal's default account, and as taxes the purchase-typed taxes attached to that account, failing which the company's default purchase tax, then map the result through the fiscal position.
Subtract the current tax-inclusive total of the document from the typed total to obtain the remaining amount.
Propose a single line with that account, those taxes and the unit price derived from the remaining amount.
records.formula: remaining = quick_edit_total_amount − current tax-inclusive total of the document

rounding.what: The remaining amount, being a difference of two amounts already rounded to the document currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.

result.name: remaining amount to encode
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is the tax-inclusive amount from which the unit price of the proposed line is derived.

edge_cases.case: The document already carries lines.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the difference is proposed, so typing the total after adding a line completes it rather than duplicating it.

edge_cases.outcome: No line is needed, the typed total already matching the document.

edge_cases.case: The remaining amount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: A negative line is proposed, bringing the document down to the typed total.

records.name: The net amount of a quick-encoded line under the always-upon-invoice discount mode
records.purpose: Backs the tax-excluded amount out of a typed tax-inclusive total when the payment term books an early discount on the invoice itself, so that the tax is computed on the already-discounted base.

operands.name: remaining amount
operands.source: the typed total less the current total
operands.constraints: tax-inclusive

operands.name: discount percentage
operands.source: the early payment discount of the payment term
operands.constraints: strictly positive while the discount is enabled

operands.name: tax rate
operands.source: the single percentage tax chosen for the line
operands.constraints: the rule applies only when there is exactly one tax and it is a percentage tax

preconditions.condition: The payment term grants an early discount in the always-upon-invoice mode, stored as `mixed`.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary tax-included back-out applies.

preconditions.condition: There is exactly one tax on the line and it is a percentage tax.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary tax-included back-out applies.

procedure: Divide the discount percentage by one hundred and subtract the quotient from one.
Divide the tax rate by one hundred and multiply it by that factor.
Add one to the product to obtain the divisor.
Divide the remaining amount by the divisor and round to the document currency; the result is the net amount of the proposed line.
records.formula: price_untaxed = round_to( document_currency , remaining ÷ ( ( 1 − discount_percentage ÷ 100 ) × ( tax_rate ÷ 100 ) + 1 ) )

rounding.what: The net amount of the proposed line.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.step: After the division, before the unit price is written to the line.

result.name: tax-excluded unit price of the proposed line
result.stored_or_displayed: Written to the single line quick encoding proposes.

edge_cases.case: The discount percentage is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The divisor reduces to one plus the tax rate, that is the ordinary tax-included back-out.

edge_cases.case: There are two taxes on the line.
edge_cases.outcome: The rule does not apply and the ordinary back-out is used.

edge_cases.case: The tax is a fixed-amount tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The rule does not apply, since it requires a percentage tax.

edge_cases.case: The resulting document total differs from the typed total after rounding.
edge_cases.outcome: The reconciliation of rounding nudges the first tax group so that the printed total matches what was typed.

worked_examples.narrative: The tax is computed on ninety-eight per cent of the base, so the divisor is one plus 0.98 multiplied by 0.21, that is 1.2058; one hundred divided by 1.2058 is 82.9324…, which rounds half away from zero to 82.93.

records.name: The net amount of a quick-encoded line in the ordinary case
records.purpose: Backs the tax-excluded amount out of a typed tax-inclusive total in every case except the always-upon-invoice discount mode with a single percentage tax.

operands.name: remaining amount
operands.source: the typed total less the current total
operands.constraints: treated as a tax-included amount

operands.name: chosen taxes
operands.source: the most frequent taxes of the vendor, or the purchase-typed taxes of the journal's default account, or the company's default purchase tax, mapped through the fiscal position
operands.constraints: may be several, and may include fixed-amount taxes

preconditions.condition: The payment term does not grant an early discount in the always-upon-invoice mode with exactly one percentage tax.
preconditions.otherwise: The discount-aware division applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The taxes have been chosen.
preconditions.otherwise: The remaining amount is the net amount, there being no tax to back out.

procedure: Treat the remaining amount as a tax-included amount under the chosen taxes.
Ask the tax engine for the tax-excluded total of that amount under those taxes.
Propose a single line carrying that net amount, the chosen account and the chosen taxes.
records.formula: price_untaxed = the tax-excluded total obtained by treating remaining as a tax-included amount under the chosen taxes

rounding.what: The net amount and the tax amounts the engine derives from it.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.step: Inside the tax engine, once per tax, before the line is written.

result.name: tax-excluded unit price of the proposed line
result.stored_or_displayed: Written to the single line quick encoding proposes.

edge_cases.case: There is no tax at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The net amount equals the remaining amount.

edge_cases.case: Several taxes apply, one of them compounded.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax engine applies its own ordering, and the net amount is the tax-excluded total it returns.

edge_cases.case: The back-out does not reproduce the typed total exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: The reconciliation of rounding nudges the first tax group of the untaxed subtotal.

taxes: purchase tax at twenty-one per cent

records.name: The reconciliation of rounding after quick encoding
records.purpose: Makes the printed total match exactly what the user typed, by nudging the tax rather than the base when the back-out of the tax leaves a difference of a few hundredths.

operands.name: typed total
operands.source: the quick encoding field
operands.constraints: the figure the document must show

operands.name: resulting document total
operands.source: the total of the document after the proposed line has been added
operands.constraints: may differ from the typed total by a rounding step

operands.name: first tax group of the untaxed subtotal
operands.source: the tax groups of the totals block
operands.constraints: the difference is added to this group

preconditions.condition: The resulting document total differs from the typed total.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is adjusted.

preconditions.condition: The document carries at least one tax group.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nowhere to place the difference and the mismatch survives to posting.

procedure: Compare the resulting document total with the typed total.
Take the difference between them.
Add that difference to the first tax group of the untaxed subtotal, so that the base stays as computed and only the tax moves.

Refuse a mismatch that survives this at posting, with the message that the current total is a given figure but the expected total is another, and that the lines or the expected tax-inclusive total must be adjusted before the document can be posted.
records.formula:
adjustment = typed_total − resulting_document_total
first tax group ← first tax group + adjustment

rounding.what: The adjusted tax amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.step: After the line has been proposed and the totals recomputed, and before the document is shown.

result.name: adjusted tax amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown in the totals block, so that the printed total equals the typed total exactly.

edge_cases.case: The difference is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is adjusted.

edge_cases.case: The mismatch survives to posting.
edge_cases.outcome: Posting is refused with the message naming the current total and the expected total.

edge_cases.case: There are several tax groups.
edge_cases.outcome: The first group of the untaxed subtotal receives the whole adjustment.

worked_examples.narrative: The base of 82.64 and the tax of 17.35 give 99.99; the tax is nudged to 17.36 so that the printed total is exactly the 100.00 that was typed.

records.name: The default bill date under quick encoding
records.purpose: Fills the bill date of a new document when quick encoding is on and the user has typed none, reusing the date of the previous document of the same journal so that a batch of bills of the same period is captured quickly.

operands.name: today
operands.source: the current date
operands.constraints: the fallback when no previous document exists

operands.name: bill date of the previous posted document
operands.source: a previous posted document of the same journal and the same company that carries a bill date
operands.constraints: may not exist

preconditions.condition: Quick encoding is on for the journal.
preconditions.otherwise: No date is proposed.

preconditions.condition: No bill date has been typed.
preconditions.otherwise: The typed date is kept.

procedure: Take today as the default.
When a previous posted document of the same journal and the same company carries a bill date, take that date instead.
Pass the date so obtained through the accounting date algorithm, so that the accounting date follows the same period rules as any other capture.
records.formula:
bill_date = the previous posted document's bill date passed through the accounting date algorithm , when such a document exists
bill_date = today , otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.

result.name: proposed bill date
result.stored_or_displayed: Written to the bill date of the new document and shown in the form.

edge_cases.case: No previous posted document of that journal exists.
edge_cases.outcome: Today is used.

edge_cases.case: The previous document's bill date falls in an earlier month.
edge_cases.outcome: The accounting date algorithm moves the accounting date to the last day of that month, exactly as for a hand-captured bill.

edge_cases.case: A bill date has already been typed.
edge_cases.outcome: It is left untouched.

records.name: The statistical base of the abnormal amount and date detection
records.purpose: Builds the history against which a draft bill is judged unusual: the average interval between this vendor's documents, the average amount, and the dispersion of each.

operands.name: examined document
operands.source: the draft purchase document being judged
operands.constraints: must be stored, in the draft state, with a non-zero total, and its vendor must not have silenced both warnings

operands.name: comparable documents
operands.source: the other posted documents that share the examined document's partner, its type, its company and its currency, whose bill date is on or before the examined document's bill date, falling back to its accounting date and then to today
operands.constraints: ordered by bill date descending

operands.name: bill dates of the comparable documents
operands.source: those documents
operands.constraints: used to form the gaps between consecutive documents

operands.name: totals of the comparable documents
operands.source: those documents
operands.constraints: used to form the mean and the deviation of the amounts

preconditions.condition: The examined document is a stored purchase document in the draft state with a non-zero total.
preconditions.otherwise: Neither warning is computed.

preconditions.condition: The vendor has not silenced both warnings, and the context flag that disables the detection entirely is not set.
preconditions.otherwise: Neither warning is computed.

preconditions.condition: The window contains between ten and thirty rows.
preconditions.otherwise: The fallbacks apply: the last invoice date is the examined bill date, both means are zero and both deviations are ten thousand million, deliberately enormous so that no warning can fire.

procedure: Collect the other posted documents sharing the partner, the type, the company and the currency, whose bill date is on or before the examined document's reference date.
Order them by bill date descending.
For each row take the gap to the next more recent document, that is the bill date of the preceding row less the bill date of this one.
Take the most recent bill date as the last invoice date.
Take the mean of the gaps and their sample standard deviation.
Take the mean of the totals and their sample standard deviation.
Keep only the window rows numbered between ten and thirty, so that the statistics are used only when the vendor has at least ten and at most thirty prior documents in the series.
When no row qualifies, apply the fallbacks.
records.formula:
date_diff( row_i )  = bill_date( row_{i−1} ) − bill_date( row_i )
last_invoice_date   = the most recent bill date
date_diff_mean      = the mean of the gaps
date_diff_deviation = the sample standard deviation of the gaps
amount_mean         = the mean of the totals
amount_deviation    = the sample standard deviation of the totals

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded in the statistics themselves; the two figures quoted in the warning texts are rendered as integers.
rounding.precision: One day for the gaps, the rounding factor of the shared currency for the amounts.
rounding.method: Truncation to a whole number when the figures are rendered in the message.
rounding.step: At display time only, never during the computation.

result.name: the last invoice date, the two means and the two deviations
result.unit_or_currency: a calendar date, days and the shared currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; recomputed for each examined draft and consumed by the two warnings.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has fewer than ten prior documents.
edge_cases.outcome: No row qualifies, the deviations are ten thousand million and no warning can fire.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has more than thirty prior documents.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the window rows numbered between ten and thirty are kept.

edge_cases.case: The examined document has no bill date.
edge_cases.outcome: Its accounting date is used, and today when it has neither.

edge_cases.case: A prior document is in another currency.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, the currency being part of the selection.

edge_cases.case: The examined document is not stored yet.
edge_cases.outcome: The detection does not run.

worked_examples.description: A monthly supplier with twelve prior bills
worked_examples.narrative: Eleven gaps alternating between thirty and thirty-one days give a mean of 30.5 days; every total is the same, so the amount deviation is zero.

worked_examples.description: A vendor with only three prior bills
worked_examples.narrative: Fewer than ten rows qualify, so the fallbacks apply and the enormous deviations make both warnings unreachable.

records.name: The abnormal billing date warning
records.purpose: Warns that a bill has arrived sooner than this vendor's rhythm would suggest, which is the usual signature of a duplicate or of a misdated document.

operands.name: mean of the gaps
operands.source: the statistical base
operands.constraints: zero when the base fell back

operands.name: sample standard deviation of the gaps
operands.source: the statistical base
operands.constraints: one extra day is added when the mean exceeds twenty-five

operands.name: last invoice date
operands.source: the statistical base
operands.constraints: the most recent bill date of the series

operands.name: examined bill date
operands.source: the draft document being judged
operands.constraints: compared with the last invoice date

preconditions.condition: The vendor has not silenced date warnings.
preconditions.otherwise: No warning fires.

preconditions.condition: The statistical base has a usable window.
preconditions.otherwise: The enormous fallback deviation makes the threshold deeply negative and the warning unreachable.

procedure: When the mean of the gaps exceeds twenty-five, add one day to the deviation of the gaps; the extra day exists because months have different lengths, a strictly monthly supplier producing a mean around thirty and a half days with a deviation around one day, so that February would otherwise trip the alarm.
Multiply the deviation so adjusted by two to obtain the wiggle room in days.
Take the difference in days between the examined bill date and the last invoice date.
Take the whole part of the mean less the wiggle room.
Fire the warning when the difference is strictly smaller than that whole part.
records.formula:
if date_diff_mean > 25 then date_diff_deviation ← date_diff_deviation + 1
wiggle_room_date = 2 × date_diff_deviation
warning fires when ( examined_bill_date − last_invoice_date ) in days  <  integer_part( date_diff_mean − wiggle_room_date )

rounding.what: The threshold, reduced to its whole part, and the two figures quoted in the message.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.method: Truncation towards zero for the whole part; the figures in the message are rendered as integers.
rounding.step: The whole part is taken after the wiggle room has been subtracted from the mean, and immediately before the comparison.

result.name: abnormal date warning
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a warning-level banner reading "The billing frequency for «vendor display name» appears unusual. Based on your historical data, the expected next invoice date is not before «last invoice date plus the mean less the wiggle room, in days». (every «mean» (± «wiggle room») days). Please verify if this date is accurate."

edge_cases.case: The mean is twenty-five days or less.
edge_cases.outcome: No extra day is added to the deviation.

edge_cases.case: The gaps are perfectly regular.
edge_cases.outcome: The deviation is small, the wiggle room is small and even a modest anticipation fires the warning.

edge_cases.case: The examined bill date is later than expected.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is large and no warning fires; only an early document is flagged.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has silenced date warnings.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is shown, and the mass-posting wizard is what offers to silence a vendor permanently.

edge_cases.case: The statistical base fell back.
edge_cases.outcome: The wiggle room is twenty thousand million days and the threshold is deeply negative, so the warning cannot fire.

worked_examples.description: A monthly supplier billing after nine days
worked_examples.narrative: The mean exceeds twenty-five, so the deviation becomes 2.0 and the wiggle room 4.0 days; the whole part of 30.5 less 4.0 is 26, and the actual gap of nine days is smaller, so the banner appears.

worked_examples.description: The same supplier billing after twenty-nine days
worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-nine days is not smaller than twenty-six, so no warning is shown.

records.name: The abnormal amount warning
records.purpose: Warns that a bill is larger or smaller than this vendor's usual amount, and prevents the document from being posted automatically.

operands.name: mean of the totals
operands.source: the statistical base
operands.constraints: zero when the base fell back

operands.name: sample standard deviation of the totals
operands.source: the statistical base
operands.constraints: ten thousand million when the base fell back

operands.name: total of the examined document
operands.source: the draft document being judged
operands.constraints: must be non-zero for the detection to run at all

preconditions.condition: The vendor has not silenced amount warnings.
preconditions.otherwise: No warning fires.

preconditions.condition: The statistical base has a usable window.
preconditions.otherwise: The enormous fallback deviation makes the interval unbounded and the warning unreachable.

procedure: Multiply the deviation of the totals by two to obtain the wiggle room.
Form the closed interval from the mean less the wiggle room to the mean plus the wiggle room.
Fire the warning when the total of the examined document lies outside that interval.
records.formula:
wiggle_room_amount = 2 × amount_deviation
warning fires when amount_total is outside the closed interval [ amount_mean − wiggle_room_amount , amount_mean + wiggle_room_amount ]

rounding.what: The two amounts quoted in the message, formatted in the document currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero at formatting time.
rounding.step: At display time only; the comparison itself uses the unformatted figures.

result.name: abnormal amount warning
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a warning-level banner reading "The amount for «vendor display name» appears unusual. Based on your historical data, the expected amount is «mean» (± «wiggle room»). Please verify if this amount is accurate.", with both amounts formatted in the document currency; it also prevents automatic posting of the bill.

edge_cases.case: The total lies exactly on a bound of the interval.
edge_cases.outcome: No warning fires, the interval being closed.

edge_cases.case: Every prior total is identical.
edge_cases.outcome: The deviation is zero and any different total fires the warning.

edge_cases.case: The warning fires.
edge_cases.outcome: Automatic posting is prevented, and the mass-posting wizard lists the affected vendors and offers to silence the warning permanently for each of them.

edge_cases.case: The statistical base fell back.
edge_cases.outcome: The interval spans twenty thousand million on each side of zero and no warning can fire.

worked_examples.description: A supplier whose bills are around twelve hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: The interval runs from 1 100.00 to 1 300.00 and the examined total of 1 450.00 lies outside it, so the banner appears and the bill is not posted automatically.

worked_examples.description: The same supplier with a bill of twelve hundred and fifty euros
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand two hundred and fifty lies inside the interval, so nothing is shown.

records.name: The next cheque number of a journal
records.purpose: Exposes the number the next printed cheque of a bank journal will carry, drawn from the journal's own no-gap cheque sequence.

operands.name: cheque sequence of the journal
operands.source: the sequence the journal owns, implemented without gaps, with a padding of five and an increment of one
operands.constraints: a journal may have none

operands.name: next value of the sequence
operands.source: the sequence
operands.constraints: one or more

operands.name: padding of the sequence
operands.source: the sequence, five by default
operands.constraints: one or more

preconditions.condition: The journal owns a cheque sequence.
preconditions.otherwise: The next number is one.

procedure: Read the next value of the journal's cheque sequence.
Render it with the sequence's padding, that is with leading zeros to that many characters.
Answer one when the journal has no cheque sequence at all.

check_next_number = the sequence's next value, rendered with the sequence's padding
check_next_number = 1, when the journal has no cheque sequence

rounding.precision: One unit.

edge_cases.case: The padding has been changed by a previous write.

records.name: Writing the next cheque number of a journal
records.purpose: Lets an accountant align the sequence with the stationery in the printer, while refusing values that would produce a rejected cheque, and derives the padding from the text that was written.

operands.name: written value
operands.source: the value the user writes into the next cheque number of the journal
operands.constraints: must contain digits only

operands.name: current next value of the sequence
operands.source: the journal's cheque sequence
operands.constraints: the written value may not be lower than it

operands.name: upper bound
operands.source: the largest value the field accepts
operands.constraints: two thousand one hundred and forty-seven million four hundred and eighty-three thousand six hundred and forty-seven

preconditions.condition: The written value contains digits only.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused with the message "Next Check Number should only contains numbers."

preconditions.condition: The written value is not lower than the sequence's current next value.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused with the message "The last check number was «the current next value». In order to avoid a check being rejected by the bank, you can only use a greater number."

preconditions.condition: The written value does not exceed two thousand one hundred and forty-seven million four hundred and eighty-three thousand six hundred and forty-seven.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused with the message "The check number you entered («the value») exceeds the maximum allowed value of 2147483647. Please enter a smaller number."

procedure: Refuse a value containing anything but digits.
Refuse a value lower than the sequence's current next value.
Refuse a value above two thousand one hundred and forty-seven million four hundred and eighty-three thousand six hundred and forty-seven.
Otherwise set the sequence's next value to the number written.
Set the sequence's padding to the number of characters of the text that was written.
records.formula:
sequence next value ← the written value read as a whole number
sequence padding    ← the number of characters of the written text

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the value is a whole number and the padding a count of characters.
rounding.precision: One unit.

result.name: updated cheque sequence
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the journal's cheque sequence, changing every later cheque number's width.

edge_cases.case: The value is written with leading zeros.
edge_cases.outcome: The padding becomes the length of the whole text, so writing six characters sets a padding of six.

edge_cases.case: The value equals the current next value.
edge_cases.outcome: It is accepted, only a lower value being refused.

edge_cases.case: A non-numeric value is entered in the pre-numbered printing dialogue.
edge_cases.outcome: The same message about digits only is shown.

worked_examples.narrative: Six characters were written, so the padding becomes six and every later cheque number is six characters wide.

records.name: The cheque number carried by a payment
records.purpose: Shows the number a payment will bear while it is being drafted, and consumes the sequence for real when the payment is posted.

operands.name: cheque sequence next value of the journal
operands.source: the journal of the payment
operands.constraints: rendered with the sequence's padding

operands.name: manual numbering flag of the journal
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: the display and the consumption both require it

operands.name: payment method code
operands.source: the payment
operands.constraints: must be the cheque printing method, whose stored code is `check_printing`

preconditions.condition: The journal uses manual numbering and the payment method is the cheque printing method.
preconditions.otherwise: The displayed number is empty and no sequence is consumed.

procedure: While the payment is being drafted, show the journal's cheque sequence next value rendered with its padding.
Show nothing when the journal does not use manual numbering or the payment method is not the cheque printing method.
At posting, for every payment whose method is the cheque method and whose journal uses manual numbering, consume the sequence and write the drawn value to the payment.
When a number is written directly on a payment, set the journal cheque sequence's padding to the number of characters of the written text.
records.formula:
check_number = the journal's cheque sequence next value, rendered with its padding, when the journal uses manual numbering and the payment method code is check_printing
check_number = empty, otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the number is a whole number rendered with leading zeros.
rounding.precision: One unit.

result.name: cheque number of the payment
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed while drafting and stored on the payment at posting; printed as the sequence number of the cheque.

edge_cases.case: The payment is drafted but never posted.
edge_cases.outcome: No number is consumed, the sequence being implemented without gaps.

edge_cases.case: The journal does not use manual numbering.
edge_cases.outcome: The displayed number is empty and the numbers come from the stationery through the pre-printed path.

edge_cases.case: A number is typed directly on the payment.
edge_cases.outcome: The journal sequence's padding is set to the length of the typed text.

edge_cases.case: The payment is voided after being sent.
edge_cases.outcome: Its number remains visible in the audit trail, and because the uniqueness check only compares posted entries it does not block reuse from a database point of view.

worked_examples.description: A payment drafted in a journal whose sequence stands at one hundred
worked_examples.narrative: The number is shown while drafting; the sequence is only consumed when the payment is posted, at which point 00100 is written to it.

worked_examples.description: A payment by transfer in the same journal
worked_examples.narrative: The method is not the cheque method, so no number is shown.

records.name: The next number proposed by the pre-printed cheque path
records.purpose: Proposes the number to start from when the stationery carries the numbers itself, by continuing from the greatest number already used in the journal.

operands.name: existing cheque numbers of the journal
operands.source: the payments of the journal
operands.constraints: compared as whole numbers, so that a padded value and an unpadded one compare by value

operands.name: greatest existing number
operands.source: the maximum of those numbers read as whole numbers
operands.constraints: absent when the journal has none

preconditions.condition: The journal does not use manual numbering.
preconditions.otherwise: The numbers come from the journal's own sequence instead.

preconditions.condition: Printing has been requested.
preconditions.otherwise: No proposal is made.

procedure: Take the greatest existing cheque number of the journal, compared as a whole number.
Count the characters of that value, taking zero when the journal has none.
Add one to the greatest value.
Render the sum with leading zeros to exactly that many characters.
Pre-fill the printing dialogue with the value so rendered.
records.formula:
last  = the greatest existing check_number of the journal, compared as an integer
width = the number of characters of that value ( 0 when there is none )
next  = ( last + 1 ) rendered with leading zeros to exactly width characters

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the value is a whole number rendered to a fixed width.
rounding.precision: One unit.

result.name: proposed starting number
result.stored_or_displayed: Pre-fills the printing dialogue, where the user may change it.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no cheque number yet.
edge_cases.outcome: The width is zero, so the proposal is the plain number one with no leading zeros.

edge_cases.case: The greatest existing number is padded.
edge_cases.outcome: The width is the length of that padded text, so the proposal keeps the same width.

edge_cases.case: Adding one increases the number of digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The rendering to exactly that width cannot truncate the value, so the number grows by one character.

worked_examples.description: A journal whose greatest cheque number is 000123
worked_examples.narrative: The greatest value read as a whole number is one hundred and twenty-three, written on six characters, so the proposal is 000124.

worked_examples.description: A journal with no cheque printed yet
worked_examples.narrative: With no history the width is zero and the proposal is the plain number one.

records.name: Numbering a selection of payments when pre-printed cheques are printed
records.purpose: Assigns consecutive numbers to the selected payments in the order the printer will feed the stationery, and moves each payment to the state that printing implies.

operands.name: entered starting value
operands.source: the value the user confirms in the printing dialogue
operands.constraints: must contain digits only

operands.name: number of characters entered
operands.source: the same text
operands.constraints: fixes the width of every number assigned

operands.name: selected payments
operands.source: the selection
operands.constraints: they must all belong to the same bank journal, and at least one must use the cheque method and not yet have been sent

preconditions.condition: At least one selected payment uses the cheque method and has not yet been sent.
preconditions.otherwise: Printing is refused with the message that payments to print as checks must have the cheque method selected and must not have been sent.

preconditions.condition: The selection belongs to a single bank journal.
preconditions.otherwise: Printing is refused with the message that in order to print multiple checks at once they must belong to the same bank journal.

preconditions.condition: A cheque layout is configured on the journal or the company and still resolves to a printable document definition.
preconditions.otherwise: Printing is refused with the message asking the user to choose a check layout, or with the message that something went wrong with the check layout and that another layout should be selected.

procedure: Read the entered value as a whole number and count the characters entered.
Post every selected draft payment.
Mark as sent every selected payment that is in process and has not yet been sent.
Number the payments in recordset order: the first receives the entered value rendered with leading zeros to the entered width, the second that value plus one, and so on.
Produce the printable document and close the dialogue when the download completes.
records.formula: number of the i-th payment = ( k + i − 1 ) rendered with leading zeros to exactly w characters, where k is the entered value and w the number of characters entered, and i counts from one in recordset order

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the numbers are consecutive whole numbers.
rounding.precision: One unit.

result.name: cheque numbers of the selected payments
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on each payment and printed on each cheque.

edge_cases.case: A selected payment is still a draft.
edge_cases.outcome: It is posted first, so that every printed cheque corresponds to a posted entry.

edge_cases.case: A selected payment has already been sent.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not marked again; only payments in process that have not been sent are marked.

edge_cases.case: The entered value is not numeric.
edge_cases.outcome: The dialogue refuses it with the message that the next check number should only contain numbers.

edge_cases.case: Two of the numbers assigned collide with existing posted numbers of the journal.
edge_cases.outcome: The uniqueness check refuses them, listing each clashing number and its journal.

worked_examples.description: Three cheques printed from stationery starting at 000124
worked_examples.narrative: The three payments are numbered consecutively on six characters, in recordset order, after every draft among them has been posted.

records.name: The uniqueness of a cheque number within a journal
records.purpose: Prevents two posted payments of the same bank journal from carrying the same cheque number, comparing the numbers by value rather than by text so that padding cannot hide a collision.

operands.name: cheque numbers of the journal's payments
operands.source: the payments of the journal
operands.constraints: must consist of decimal digits only

operands.name: status of the journal entry of each payment
operands.source: the entry behind each payment
operands.constraints: only entries that are posted take part in the comparison

preconditions.condition: Every cheque number consists of decimal digits only.
preconditions.otherwise: The number is refused with the message "Check numbers can only consist of digits".

preconditions.condition: The two payments belong to the same journal and both their entries are posted.
preconditions.otherwise: No collision is raised.

procedure: Reject any number that contains a character other than a decimal digit.
Read each cheque number of the journal as a whole number.
Compare the numbers of the payments whose entries are posted, within one journal.
Refuse the write when two of them are equal as whole numbers, listing one line per clashing pair.
records.formula: collision when  integer( check_number of payment A ) = integer( check_number of payment B )  ,  same journal , both entries posted

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the comparison is between whole numbers.
rounding.precision: One unit.

result.name: uniqueness verdict
result.stored_or_displayed: Raised as a refusal reading "The following numbers are already used:" followed by one line per clashing pair, each naming the number and the journal display name.

edge_cases.case: One number is padded and the other is not.
edge_cases.outcome: They still clash, because the comparison is by value, so the digit string zero zero four two clashes with forty-two.

edge_cases.case: One of the two entries is cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: No collision is raised, because the comparison is restricted to posted entries; a voided cheque therefore does not block its own number from a database point of view, while the audit trail keeps it visible.

edge_cases.case: The two payments are in different journals.
edge_cases.outcome: No collision is raised, the constraint being per journal.

edge_cases.case: A number contains a letter.
edge_cases.outcome: It is refused outright.

worked_examples.description: A padded number colliding with an unpadded one

expected_outputs.message_first_line: The following numbers are already used:

worked_examples.narrative: Both read as forty-two, so the two posted payments clash and the write is refused with one line naming the number and the journal.

worked_examples.description: The same pair where one entry has been cancelled
worked_examples.narrative: Only posted entries are compared, so the cancelled cheque does not block the number.

records.name: Gathering the documents a cheque pays
records.purpose: Finds the documents that a payment settles, so that the detachable stub of the cheque can list what is being paid.

operands.name: counterpart lines of the payment
operands.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and the company currency
operands.source: the lines of the payment's own journal entry that sit on a receivable or a payable account
operands.constraints: present once the payment is posted

operands.name: partial reconciliations
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the currencies of the documents
operands.source: the reconciliations of those counterpart lines, followed in both directions
operands.constraints: grouped by the entry they touch

operands.name: documents linked to the payment
operands.source: the documents explicitly linked to the payment, used when the payment has no entry yet
operands.constraints: walked in order while the payment amount is consumed

preconditions.condition: The payment has a journal entry, which is the normal case after posting.
preconditions.otherwise: The documents explicitly linked to the payment are taken instead and are walked in order, consuming the payment amount.

procedure: Take the payment's own receivable and payable lines, that is its counterpart lines.
Follow their reconciliations in both directions to reach the counterpart entries.
Keep only the entries that are outbound documents, receipts included, that is vendor bills, purchase receipts and customer credit notes.
Group the partial reconciliations by the entry they touch, so that each document appears once with the amount allocated to it.
When the payment has no journal entry yet, take the documents explicitly linked to it, keep the outbound ones and walk them in order consuming the payment amount.
records.formula: paid_documents = the outbound counterpart entries reached by following the reconciliations of the payment's counterpart lines in both directions , grouped by entry

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the gathering itself; the allocated amounts come from the partial reconciliations, each already rounded to its currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factors of the currencies involved.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each reconciliation was recorded.

result.name: the documents paid and the amount allocated to each
result.unit_or_currency: the currencies of the documents and of the payment
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the stub-line rules and printed on the detachable stub of the cheque.

edge_cases.case: The payment settles a customer credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The credit note is an outbound document and is listed on the stub, in the refunds bucket.

edge_cases.case: The payment is reconciled against a document that is not outbound.
edge_cases.outcome: That document is dropped, the filter keeping only outbound documents and receipts.

edge_cases.case: The payment has not been posted.
edge_cases.outcome: The explicitly linked documents are used and the payment amount is allocated across them in order.

edge_cases.case: One document is settled by several partial reconciliations of the same payment.
edge_cases.outcome: They are grouped by entry, so the document appears once with the summed allocation.

worked_examples.description: A cheque settling two vendor bills
worked_examples.narrative: Both bills are outbound documents reached through the reconciliations of the payment's payable line, so each becomes one stub line.

records.name: The sign of a stub line
records.purpose: Gives each document listed on the stub the sign that makes a bill read as a positive amount paid and a credit note as a deduction.

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the document the stub line describes
operands.constraints: outbound documents and purchase receipts take plus one

preconditions.condition: The document has been gathered as one the payment settles.
preconditions.otherwise: No stub line exists for it.

procedure: Answer plus one when the document is an outbound document or a purchase receipt.
Answer minus one otherwise.
Multiply the total, the residual and the paid amount of the stub line by that sign.
records.formula:
invoice_sign = +1  when I is outbound or a purchase receipt
invoice_sign = −1  otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the sign is exact.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: stub line sign
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, plus one or minus one
result.stored_or_displayed: Applied to the three amount columns of the stub line.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is plus one and the amounts read as positive figures.

edge_cases.case: The document is a purchase receipt.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is plus one as well.

edge_cases.case: The document is a customer credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: It is an outbound document, so the sign is plus one and it appears in the refunds bucket.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill on the stub
worked_examples.narrative: A bill is an outbound document, so its total and its paid amount print as positive figures.

records.name: The total column of a stub line
records.purpose: Prints what the whole document amounts to, in the document's own currency, so that the payee can match the payment against the invoice.

operands.name: total of the document
operands.source: the document the stub line describes
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill

operands.name: stub line sign
operands.source: the sign rule
operands.constraints: plus one for an outbound document or a purchase receipt

preconditions.condition: The document has a total.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing can be printed in the column.

procedure: Multiply the total of the document by the stub line sign.
Format the product in the document's own currency.

Print beside it the due date of the document, formatted, and its number, or the single character that stands for an unnumbered document, joined to the vendor reference by a space, a hyphen and a space when the document carries one.
records.formula: total_column = invoice_sign × I.amount_total , formatted in I's currency

rounding.what: The formatted total.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document's own currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the total was computed.

result.name: total column of the stub line
result.stored_or_displayed: Printed on the stub beside the due date, the number and the vendor reference.

edge_cases.case: The document has no number.
edge_cases.outcome: The number column shows the single character that stands for an unnumbered document, that is `/`.

edge_cases.case: The document carries a vendor reference.
edge_cases.outcome: The number and the reference are joined by a space, a hyphen and a space.

edge_cases.case: The document is in another currency than the payment.
edge_cases.outcome: The total is nonetheless formatted in the document's own currency, only the paid column being expressed in the payment currency.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill of one thousand four hundred and fifty-two euros
worked_examples.narrative: The sign is plus one, so the column prints 1 452.00 in euros, and the number column carries both the document number and the supplier's own reference.

records.name: The residual column of a stub line
records.purpose: Prints what will still be owed on the document once this payment is applied, so that the payee can see whether the document is settled in full.

operands.name: residual of the document
operands.source: the document before this payment is applied
operands.constraints: positive on an unpaid vendor bill

operands.name: amount allocated by this payment
operands.source: the partial reconciliations of this payment against this document, or the allocation walk when the payment has no entry
operands.constraints: zero or more

operands.name: stub line sign
operands.source: the sign rule
operands.constraints: plus one for an outbound document or a purchase receipt

preconditions.condition: The document and the allocated amount are known.
preconditions.otherwise: No residual can be printed.

procedure: Subtract the amount allocated by this payment from the residual of the document.
Multiply the difference by the stub line sign.
Format the product in the document's own currency.
Print the single hyphen character instead when the value is zero in the document's currency.
records.formula: residual_column = invoice_sign × ( I.amount_residual − current_amount ) , formatted in I's currency ; the single character - when that value is zero in I's currency

rounding.what: The difference, compared with zero at the document's currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document's own currency.
rounding.step: After the subtraction, before the comparison with zero and before formatting.

result.name: residual column of the stub line
result.stored_or_displayed: Printed on the stub; a settled document shows a single hyphen rather than a zero.

edge_cases.case: The payment settles the document in full.
edge_cases.outcome: The value is zero in the document's currency and a single hyphen is printed.

edge_cases.case: The payment settles part of the document.
edge_cases.outcome: The remaining amount is printed.

edge_cases.case: The allocated amount exceeds the residual.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is negative and prints as such.

worked_examples.description: A bill of one thousand four hundred and fifty-two euros paid in full
worked_examples.narrative: Nothing remains, so the column prints a single hyphen.

worked_examples.description: The same bill paid to the extent of one thousand euros
worked_examples.narrative: Four hundred and fifty-two euros remain owed and are printed in the document's currency.

records.name: The paid column of a stub line
records.purpose: Prints how much of this payment is applied to this document, in the payment's own currency, which is the figure that adds up to the cheque amount.

operands.name: amount allocated by this payment
operands.source: the allocation given for this document, when one was given
operands.constraints: used directly when present

operands.name: debit amounts in currency of the reconciliations
operands.source: the partial reconciliations touching the document, used for an outbound document
operands.constraints: summed when no allocation was given

operands.name: credit amounts in currency of the reconciliations
operands.source: the same reconciliations, used for a document that is not outbound
operands.constraints: summed when no allocation was given

operands.name: stub line sign
operands.source: the sign rule
operands.constraints: plus one for an outbound document or a purchase receipt

preconditions.condition: An allocation was given for this document, or the document's reconciliations are available.
preconditions.otherwise: The column cannot be filled.

procedure: Take the allocated amount when one was given for this document.
Otherwise sum, over the reconciliations touching the document, the debit amount in currency for an outbound document and the credit amount in currency otherwise.
Multiply the figure by the stub line sign.
Format the product in the payment's currency, not in the document's.
records.formula:
paid_column = invoice_sign × amount_paid , formatted in the payment's currency
amount_paid = current_amount when one was given
amount_paid = Σ over the reconciliations of the debit amount in currency for an outbound document , of the credit amount in currency otherwise

rounding.what: The formatted amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the payment's currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each reconciliation was recorded.
rounding.step: At formatting time; the sum is of already rounded reconciliation amounts.

result.name: paid column of the stub line
result.stored_or_displayed: Printed on the stub; the paid columns of the page add up to the cheque amount.

edge_cases.case: The document is in another currency than the payment.
edge_cases.outcome: The paid column is still expressed in the payment currency, while the total and the residual columns use the document's currency.

edge_cases.case: Several reconciliations link the payment to the document.
edge_cases.outcome: Their amounts in currency are summed.

edge_cases.case: The document is not outbound.
edge_cases.outcome: The credit amounts in currency are summed instead of the debit amounts.

worked_examples.description: A cheque of eight hundred euros split across two bills
worked_examples.narrative: The two paid columns add up to the cheque amount of 800.00 euros.

records.name: Allocating a payment that has no journal entry across the documents it names
records.purpose: Spreads the amount of a payment that has not yet been posted over the documents it is linked to, oldest due first, so that a stub can be printed before the reconciliations exist.

operands.name: payment amount
operands.source: the payment
operands.constraints: consumed from the start of the walk

operands.name: documents linked to the payment
operands.source: the outbound documents explicitly linked to the payment
operands.constraints: ordered by due date and then by accounting date

operands.name: residual of each document
operands.source: each document
operands.constraints: converted into the payment currency before the comparison

preconditions.condition: The payment has no journal entry yet.
preconditions.otherwise: The reconciliations are followed instead.

preconditions.condition: At least one outbound document is linked to the payment.
preconditions.otherwise: The stub has no line.

procedure: Set the remaining amount to the payment amount.
Order the documents by due date and then by accounting date.
For each document take the smaller of the remaining amount and the document's residual converted from its own currency into the payment currency.
Emit a stub line for the document with that amount as the allocation.
Subtract the amount from the remaining amount.
Stop when the remaining amount reaches zero or the documents run out.
records.formula:
remaining ← payment amount
for each document I, ordered by due date and then by accounting date:
    current_amount = min( remaining , convert( I.amount_residual , from I.currency to the payment currency ) )
    emit a stub line for I with that current_amount
    remaining ← remaining − current_amount
stop when remaining reaches zero or documents run out

rounding.what: The converted residual of each document.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the payment currency.
rounding.step: At each conversion, before the comparison with the remaining amount.

result.name: the allocation of the payment across the documents
result.stored_or_displayed: Used to fill the paid column of each stub line.

edge_cases.case: The payment is larger than the sum of the residuals.
edge_cases.outcome: Every document receives its full residual and the walk ends when the documents run out, leaving a remainder unallocated.

edge_cases.case: The payment is smaller than the first document's residual.
edge_cases.outcome: That document receives the whole payment and the walk stops.

edge_cases.case: Two documents have the same due date.
edge_cases.outcome: The accounting date breaks the tie.

edge_cases.case: A document has no due date.
edge_cases.outcome: The accounting date is used in the ordering.

worked_examples.description: A payment of eight hundred euros against two bills
worked_examples.narrative: The oldest bill takes its whole residual of 500.00, leaving 300.00 for the second, whose residual column then shows the 300.00 still owed.

records.name: Grouping the stub lines into buckets and emitting their headers
records.purpose: Separates the bills a cheque pays from the customer credit notes it deducts, and labels each group when both are present.

operands.name: document types of the stub lines
operands.source: each document listed
operands.constraints: the bills bucket holds the types `in_invoice` and `in_receipt`; the refunds bucket holds the type `out_refund`

operands.name: due dates
operands.source: each document, falling back to its accounting date
operands.constraints: used to order the lines within each bucket

preconditions.condition: At least one document has been gathered.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no stub line to group.

preconditions.condition: Both buckets are non-empty.
preconditions.otherwise: No header line is emitted at all.

procedure: Place every vendor bill and every purchase receipt in the bills bucket.
Place every customer credit note in the refunds bucket.
Order the lines of each bucket by due date, falling back to the accounting date.
When both buckets are non-empty, emit a header line carrying the bucket name before each bucket.
records.formula:
bucket( I ) = bills    when the type of I is in_invoice or in_receipt
bucket( I ) = refunds  when the type of I is out_refund
headers are emitted only when both buckets are non-empty

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the grouping is a partition.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: the ordered stub lines with their header lines
