result.stored_or_displayed: Printed on the stub; the header lines count towards the nine lines a page holds.

edge_cases.case: Only bills are paid.
edge_cases.outcome: No header is emitted and the lines are printed directly.

edge_cases.case: Both bills and credit notes are present.
edge_cases.outcome: Two header lines are emitted, one before each bucket.

edge_cases.case: A document has no due date.
edge_cases.outcome: Its accounting date is used for the ordering.

edge_cases.case: A header would be the ninth line of a page in multi-page mode.
edge_cases.outcome: Only eight lines are placed on that page, so that a bucket never starts at the very bottom of a page.

worked_examples.description: A cheque paying two bills and deducting one credit note
worked_examples.narrative: Both buckets are non-empty, so each is preceded by a header, and the five lines fit on one page.

records.name: Paging the stub in single-page mode
records.purpose: Fits the stub on the single page of the cheque, keeping room for an ellipsis when there is more to show than the page can hold.

operands.name: stub lines
operands.source: the grouped and ordered stub lines, header lines included
operands.constraints: counted as printed lines

operands.name: lines per stub
operands.source: the fixed capacity of a page
operands.constraints: exactly nine

operands.name: number of documents reconciled by the payment's entry
operands.source: the reconciliations of the payment
operands.constraints: decides whether the page is flagged as cropped

preconditions.condition: The company's multi-page stub option is off.
preconditions.otherwise: The multi-page rule applies instead.

procedure: Count the stub lines.
When there are more than nine, keep only the first eight, leaving room for an ellipsis line.
Otherwise keep up to nine.
Produce exactly one page.
Flag the page as cropped when the payment's entry reconciles more than nine documents.
records.formula:
lines kept = the first 8 stub lines   when the number of stub lines is greater than 9
lines kept = up to 9 stub lines         otherwise
pages produced = 1
cropped = ( the payment's entry reconciles more than 9 documents )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the counts are whole numbers of lines.
rounding.precision: One line.

result.name: the single stub page and its cropped flag
result.stored_or_displayed: Printed on the cheque, with an ellipsis line when lines were dropped.

edge_cases.case: There are exactly nine stub lines.
edge_cases.outcome: All nine are kept and no ellipsis is needed.

edge_cases.case: There are ten stub lines.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the first eight are kept, the ninth slot carrying the ellipsis.

edge_cases.case: The payment reconciles exactly nine documents.
edge_cases.outcome: The page is not flagged as cropped, the flag requiring more than nine.

edge_cases.case: Header lines are present.
edge_cases.outcome: They count towards the nine, so two headers reduce the number of documents that fit.

worked_examples.description: A cheque paying twelve bills in single-page mode
worked_examples.narrative: Twelve lines exceed the capacity of nine, so eight are kept and the ninth slot is the ellipsis; the page is flagged as cropped because more than nine documents are reconciled.

worked_examples.description: A cheque paying five bills
worked_examples.narrative: Five lines fit, so all are kept and nothing is cropped.

records.name: Paging the stub in multi-page mode
records.purpose: Spreads a long stub over several pages without ever letting a bucket start at the very bottom of a page.

operands.name: stub lines
operands.source: the grouped and ordered stub lines, header lines included
operands.constraints: walked from the start

operands.name: lines per stub
operands.source: the fixed capacity of a page
operands.constraints: exactly nine

preconditions.condition: The company's multi-page stub option is on.
preconditions.otherwise: The single-page rule applies instead.

procedure: Walk the stub lines from the start.
At each step take nine lines for the page.
Take only eight instead when the ninth line of the prospective page would be a bucket header, so that a bucket never starts at the very bottom of a page.
Repeat until every line has been placed.
records.formula:
lines on the next page = 9 , or 8 when the ninth line of the prospective page is a bucket header
repeat until every stub line is placed

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the counts are whole numbers of lines.
rounding.precision: One line.

result.name: the sequence of stub pages
result.stored_or_displayed: Printed as several pages, of which only the first carries a negotiable cheque.

edge_cases.case: The ninth line of a page would be a header.
edge_cases.outcome: Only eight lines are placed on that page and the header opens the next one.

edge_cases.case: Exactly nine lines remain.
edge_cases.outcome: They form the last page.

edge_cases.case: A single line remains.
edge_cases.outcome: It forms a page of its own, on which the cheque amount and the amount in words are replaced by the literal text `VOID`.

worked_examples.description: A stub of twenty lines whose ninth line is an ordinary line
worked_examples.narrative: Three pages are produced, the first carrying the negotiable cheque and the other two showing the literal text VOID in place of the amount.

worked_examples.description: A stub whose ninth line is a bucket header
worked_examples.narrative: The prospective ninth line is a header, so only eight lines are placed on the first page and the refunds bucket opens the second.

records.name: The fields of one printed cheque page
records.purpose: Assembles what each page of the printed cheque carries, and voids every page after the first so that only one negotiable instrument leaves the printer.

operands.name: page index
operands.source: the paging rule, counted from zero
operands.constraints: page zero carries the negotiable cheque

operands.name: stub lines of the page
operands.source: the paging rule
operands.constraints: at most nine

operands.name: payment amount
operands.source: the payment
operands.constraints: printed on page zero only

operands.name: filled amount-in-words line
operands.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a text of two hundred characters
operands.source: the fill rule
operands.constraints: printed on page zero only

preconditions.condition: The pages have been formed by one of the two paging rules.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is printed.

procedure: Carry on every page the cheque number as the sequence number, whether the journal uses manual numbering, the payment date formatted, the payee as partner and partner name, the company name, the payment currency, the payment status, the memo, the cropped flag and the stub lines of that page.
On page zero print the payment amount formatted in the payment currency and the filled amount-in-words line.
On every later page print the literal text `VOID` in place of both the amount and the amount in words.
records.formula:
amount on page i          = the payment amount formatted in the payment currency when i = 0 , the literal text VOID otherwise
amount in words on page i  = the filled amount-in-words line when i = 0 , the literal text VOID otherwise

rounding.what: The printed amount, formatted in the payment currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the payment currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the payment amount was recorded.

result.name: one printed cheque page
result.stored_or_displayed: Printed; only the first page carries a negotiable cheque, the others being explicitly voided.

edge_cases.case: The stub fits on one page.
edge_cases.outcome: Only page zero is produced and nothing is voided.

edge_cases.case: The stub spills over several pages.
edge_cases.outcome: Every page after the first shows the literal text `VOID` in place of the amount and of the amount in words.

edge_cases.case: Lines were dropped in single-page mode.
edge_cases.outcome: The page carries the cropped flag, which is what makes the ellipsis appear.

edge_cases.case: The journal does not use manual numbering.
edge_cases.outcome: The manual sequencing field says so, and the number comes from the pre-printed path.

worked_examples.description: A two-page stub for a cheque of eight hundred euros
worked_examples.narrative: The first page carries the amount of 800.00 and the two-hundred-character amount-in-words line; the second carries the literal text VOID in both places.

records.name: The weighted average price of one row of the invoice analysis report
records.purpose: Expresses what one row of the analysis report paid per reference unit, restating the line's own unit into the product's reference unit and converting the currency.

operands.name: balance of the line
operands.source: the journal item behind the row
operands.constraints: a debit is positive on a vendor bill

operands.name: quantity of the row
operands.source: the line
operands.constraints: zero makes the row's average undefined

operands.name: purchase sign
operands.source: the report's own sign convention for the document type, minus one for a bill
operands.constraints: plus or minus one

operands.name: factor of the line unit
operands.source: the unit of measure of the line
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: factor of the product's reference unit
operands.source: the product's reference unit
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: conversion rate
operands.source: the currency conversion applied by the report
operands.constraints: one when no conversion is needed

preconditions.condition: The quantity of the row is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The division cannot be performed and the row carries no average.

preconditions.condition: The two unit factors are known.
preconditions.otherwise: No restatement between units can be made.

procedure: Divide the balance of the line by its quantity.
Multiply by the purchase sign.
Divide by the factor of the line unit and multiply by the factor of the product's reference unit, which restates the price per reference unit.
Multiply by the conversion rate.
Negate the whole product, the report showing purchases as positive prices.
records.formula: price_average = − ( ( balance ÷ quantity ) × purchase_sign ÷ factor( line_unit ) × factor( template_unit ) ) × conversion_rate

rounding.what: The displayed average.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency the report is expressed in.
rounding.step: At display time; the computation itself is carried at full precision.

result.name: weighted average price of the row
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the report, per reference unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a column of the analysis report; it is not the figure an aggregation shows, the aggregate being computed separately.

edge_cases.case: The line was bought in a multiple of the reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The restatement divides the price accordingly, so a price per dozen becomes a price per unit.

edge_cases.case: The quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The row carries no average.

edge_cases.case: The document is a purchase document.
edge_cases.outcome: The purchase sign is minus one, which together with the leading negation makes the average a positive price.

worked_examples.description: A line of three dozens for three hundred and sixty euros
worked_examples.narrative: Three hundred and sixty divided by three is one hundred and twenty per dozen, restated as ten per unit; the purchase sign of minus one and the leading negation leave a positive price of 10.00 per unit.

records.name: The aggregated average price of a group of the invoice analysis report
records.purpose: Gives the average price of a group of rows as a true weighted average rather than as the mean of the per-row averages, so that large and small purchases carry their proper weight.

operands.name: subtotal of each row
operands.source: the rows of the group
operands.constraints: already signed by the report's conventions

operands.name: quantity of each row
operands.source: the rows of the group, restated into the reference unit
operands.constraints: already signed by the report's conventions

preconditions.condition: The sum of the quantities of the group is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The aggregated average is zero.

procedure: Sum the subtotals of the rows of the group.
Sum the quantities of the rows of the group.
Divide the first sum by the second.
Answer zero when the sum of the quantities is zero.
records.formula: aggregated_average = Σ price_subtotal ÷ Σ quantity        ( 0 when Σ quantity is 0 )

rounding.what: The displayed aggregate.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency the report is expressed in.
rounding.step: At display time; the division itself is carried at full precision.

result.name: aggregated average price
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the report, per reference unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the group row of the analysis report, deliberately computed as a weighted average rather than as the mean of the per-row column.

edge_cases.case: The quantities cancel out.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is zero and the aggregate is zero rather than undefined.

edge_cases.case: The group holds rows of different units.
edge_cases.outcome: Every quantity has already been restated into the product's reference unit, so the division is homogeneous.

edge_cases.case: The group holds a single row.
edge_cases.outcome: The aggregate coincides with the per-row average.

worked_examples.description: Two bill lines of the same product bought by the dozen
worked_examples.narrative: Three dozens restate to thirty-six units and one dozen to twelve, both signed by the purchase sign of minus one; four hundred and ninety divided by forty-eight is 10.2083…, that is 10.21 currency units per unit bought, and not per dozen.

records.name: The converted quantity of a line in the invoice analysis report
records.purpose: Restates the quantity of a line from the unit it was bought or sold in into the product's reference unit, which is the quantity the margin multiplies the cost by.

operands.name: quantity of the line
operands.source: the line
operands.constraints: already signed by the report's conventions

operands.name: factor of the line unit
operands.source: the unit of measure of the line
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: factor of the product's reference unit
operands.source: the product's reference unit
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The line carries a product with a reference unit.
preconditions.otherwise: No restatement is possible and the quantity is used as it stands.

procedure: Multiply the quantity by the factor of the line unit.
Divide by the factor of the product's reference unit.
records.formula: converted_quantity = quantity × factor( line_unit ) ÷ factor( template_unit )

rounding.what: The converted quantity, when it is displayed.
rounding.precision: The decimal precision named for product units.
rounding.step: At display time; the margin uses the unrounded value.

result.name: converted quantity
result.stored_or_displayed: Used by the margin formulas and displayed as the quantity column of the report.

edge_cases.case: The line unit is the reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The two factors are equal and the quantity is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The line unit is a multiple of the reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The quantity is multiplied accordingly, so three dozens become thirty-six units.

edge_cases.case: The line has no product.
edge_cases.outcome: There is no reference unit to restate into.

worked_examples.description: Three dozens restated into units
worked_examples.narrative: Three dozens are thirty-six units, which is the quantity the cost is multiplied by.

records.name: The margin of a purchase row of the invoice analysis report
records.purpose: States that a purchase document never contributes a margin, so that the report's margin column measures selling and not buying.

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the document behind the row
operands.constraints: one of the three purchase types

preconditions.condition: The document type is a purchase type, that is a vendor bill, a vendor credit note or a purchase receipt.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the two sale variants applies.

procedure: Recognise the document as a purchase type.
Answer zero for the margin, whatever the balance, the quantity and the cost.
records.formula: price_margin = 0     for any purchase type

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is exactly zero.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: margin of the row
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as zero in the margin column; bills contribute only to the untaxed amount, the total and the inventory value.

edge_cases.case: The row is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The margin is zero as well, the rule covering every purchase type.

edge_cases.case: The row is a purchase receipt.
edge_cases.outcome: The margin is zero.

worked_examples.description: A bill line of three hundred and sixty euros
worked_examples.narrative: Whatever the cost of the product, a purchase row carries no margin.

records.name: The margin of a customer credit note row of the invoice analysis report
records.purpose: States the margin formula for a customer credit note, recorded here because the payable side shares the analysis report with the receivable side and the sign differs from the invoice case.

operands.name: balance of the line
operands.source: the journal item behind the row
operands.constraints: signed as stored

operands.name: converted quantity
operands.source: the restatement rule
operands.constraints: signed by the report's conventions

operands.name: cost
operands.source: the product's standard price stored for the line's company; an absent value reads as zero
operands.constraints: per reference unit

operands.name: conversion rate
operands.source: the currency conversion applied by the report
operands.constraints: one when no conversion is needed

preconditions.condition: The document type is a customer credit note, stored as `out_refund`.
preconditions.otherwise: The purchase variant or the invoice variant applies.

procedure: Negate the balance of the line.
Multiply the converted quantity by the cost and add the product to the negated balance.
Multiply the sum by the conversion rate.
records.formula: price_margin = conversion_rate × ( − balance + converted_quantity × cost )        for out_refund

rounding.what: The displayed margin.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency the report is expressed in.
rounding.step: At display time; the computation is carried at full precision.

result.name: margin of the row
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the margin column of the analysis report.

edge_cases.case: The product has no standard price for the line's company.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost reads as zero and the margin is the negated balance converted.

edge_cases.case: The line has no product.
edge_cases.outcome: There is no cost and no restatement, so the margin reduces to the converted negated balance.

worked_examples.description: A credit note line of one hundred euros for ten units costing six euros each
worked_examples.narrative: The negated balance is −100.00 and the cost component is +60.00, so the margin is −40.00, that is the margin originally earned on the sale being given back.

records.name: The margin of a customer invoice or sales receipt row of the invoice analysis report
records.purpose: States the margin formula for a sale, recorded here because the payable side shares the analysis report with the receivable side.

operands.name: balance of the line
operands.source: the journal item behind the row
operands.constraints: a credit on a sale, so negative

operands.name: converted quantity
operands.source: the restatement rule
operands.constraints: signed by the report's conventions

operands.name: cost
operands.source: the product's standard price stored for the line's company; an absent value reads as zero
operands.constraints: per reference unit

operands.name: conversion rate
operands.source: the currency conversion applied by the report
operands.constraints: one when no conversion is needed

preconditions.condition: The document type is a customer invoice or a sales receipt, stored as `out_invoice` or `out_receipt`.
preconditions.otherwise: The purchase variant or the credit note variant applies.

procedure: Negate the balance of the line.
Multiply the converted quantity by the cost and subtract the product from the negated balance.
Multiply the difference by the conversion rate.
records.formula: price_margin = conversion_rate × ( − balance − converted_quantity × cost )        for out_invoice and out_receipt

rounding.what: The displayed margin.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the currency the report is expressed in.
rounding.step: At display time; the computation is carried at full precision.

result.name: margin of the row
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the margin column of the analysis report.

edge_cases.case: The product has no standard price for the line's company.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost reads as zero and the margin equals the converted negated balance, that is the whole revenue.

edge_cases.case: The cost exceeds the price.
edge_cases.outcome: The margin is negative.

worked_examples.description: An invoice line of one hundred euros for ten units costing six euros each
worked_examples.narrative: The negated balance is +100.00 and the cost component of 60.00 is subtracted, leaving a margin of 40.00.

records.name: The amounts of the payer's intercompany clearing entry
records.purpose: Computes the two amounts of the entry created in the paying company's books when one company of a group settles a document of another, so that the payment is cleared in the payer's books and a balance towards the other company is recognised.

operands.name: balances of the payment's counterpart lines
operands.source: the lines of the payment's own entry that sit on the receivable or the payable account
operands.constraints: summed and negated

operands.name: amounts in currency of the payment's counterpart lines
operands.source: the same lines
operands.constraints: summed and negated

preconditions.condition: The document is invoice-like, its payment status is not paid, partial or in payment, its company has an intercompany clearing journal, it carries at least one payment transaction with a payment, and the document's company is not the company of that payment.
preconditions.otherwise: No clearing entry is created.

preconditions.condition: The direction and the accounts are complete, an outbound document such as a vendor bill requiring an intercompany payable account in the document's company and an intercompany receivable account in the payer's company.
preconditions.otherwise: No clearing entry is created.

preconditions.condition: At least one such payment is in process or paid, belongs to another company, and that company has an intercompany clearing journal, the transaction itself being authorized or done.
preconditions.otherwise: The payment is not processed.

procedure: Take the counterpart lines of the payment, that is the lines of its own entry on the receivable or the payable account.
Sum their balances and negate the sum to obtain the clearing balance.
Sum their amounts in currency and negate the sum to obtain the clearing amount in currency.
Create the entry in the payer's company, in that company's intercompany clearing journal, with the payment's memo as reference, one entry per settling payment.
Give the first line the payment's own counterpart account, the document's partner, the payment's currency, the clearing amount in currency and the clearing balance.
Give the second line the other company's intercompany payable account for a sale document, its intercompany receivable account otherwise, the document's company partner, and the negated amounts.
Post the entry and reconcile its first line against the payment's counterpart lines, which clears the payment in the payer's books.
records.formula:
clearing_balance          = − Σ balance over the payment's counterpart lines
clearing_amount_currency  = − Σ amount_in_currency over the payment's counterpart lines

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded; the sums are of already rounded balances and amounts in currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the payment's company currency and of the payment currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each line was recorded.

result.name: clearing balance and clearing amount in currency
result.unit_or_currency: the payment's company currency and the payment currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Carried by the two lines of the payer's clearing entry, which is strictly balanced by construction, each line carrying the opposite amount of the other; both lines are labelled with the document partner's display name, a space, an oblique stroke, a space and the document number.

edge_cases.case: The payment settles a vendor bill of another company of the group.
edge_cases.outcome: The payer ends with a receivable from the billing company on its intercompany receivable account.

edge_cases.case: The payment has several counterpart lines.
edge_cases.outcome: Their balances and amounts in currency are summed before the negation.

edge_cases.case: Several payments settle the document.
edge_cases.outcome: One clearing entry is created per settling payment.

edge_cases.case: The transaction is neither authorized nor done.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not processed and no entry is created.

worked_examples.description: A payment of one thousand two hundred euros made by one company for a bill of another
worked_examples.narrative: The payment's payable line is a debit of 1 200.00, so the clearing balance is −1 200.00 on the payment's own counterpart account and +1 200.00 on the intercompany receivable account of the paying company; the entry balances by construction.

records.name: The amounts of the biller's intercompany settlement entry
records.purpose: Computes the amounts of the entry created in the billed company's books when another company of the group pays its document, so that the document is cleared and a balance towards the payer is recognised.

operands.name: balances of the document's receivable and payable lines
operands.source: the term lines of the document
operands.constraints: summed, then negated

preconditions.condition: The same qualifying conditions as for the payer's clearing entry hold.
preconditions.otherwise: No settlement entry is created.

preconditions.condition: The document's company has an intercompany clearing journal.
preconditions.otherwise: No settlement entry is created.

procedure: Sum the balances of the document's receivable and payable lines, that is its term lines, to obtain the total invoice balance.
Negate that total to obtain the clearing counterpart balance.

Create one entry per document in the document's company, in that company's intercompany clearing journal, with a reference naming an intercompany settlement followed by the comma-joined memos of the settling payments.

Give the first line the document company's intercompany receivable account for a sale document or its intercompany payable account otherwise, the payer's company partner, the document company's currency and the negated clearing counterpart balance.
Give the second line the document's own term-line account, the payment's partner, the document company's currency and the clearing counterpart balance.
Post the entry and reconcile its second line against the document's term lines, which clears the document in the biller's books.
records.formula:
total_invoice_balance          = Σ balance over the document's receivable and payable lines
clearing_counterpart_balance   = − total_invoice_balance

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded; the sum is of already rounded balances.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document company's currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each term line was recorded.

result.name: clearing counterpart balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Carried by the two lines of the biller's settlement entry, which is strictly balanced by construction; both lines are labelled with the document partner's display name, a space, an oblique stroke, a space and the document number.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: Its term lines are credits, so the total invoice balance is negative and the clearing counterpart balance is positive, debiting the payable account and clearing the bill.

edge_cases.case: The document has several instalments.
edge_cases.outcome: Every term line is summed, so the entry clears the document as a whole.

edge_cases.case: Several payments settle the document.
edge_cases.outcome: Only one settlement entry is created for the document, its reference naming the comma-joined memos of the settling payments.

edge_cases.case: The net effect over the two entries.
edge_cases.outcome: The bill's payable line is cleared in the billed company and a payable to the paying company remains on the intercompany payable account, mirroring the receivable recognised by the payer, so the two net to zero on consolidation.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill of one thousand two hundred euros paid by another company of the group
worked_examples.narrative: The bill's payable line is a credit of 1 200.00, so the settlement entry debits the payable account with 1 200.00 and credits the intercompany payable account with the same amount, clearing the bill and recognising the debt towards the paying company.

records.name: The precision used for each quantity of the domain
records.purpose: States, quantity by quantity, which precision governs it, so that two independent implementations round the same figure at the same place.

operands.name: kind of quantity
operands.source: the figure being stored or compared
operands.constraints: one of the nine kinds listed

operands.name: decimal precisions of the installation
operands.source: the named decimal precisions for product prices, product units, discounts and payment terms
operands.constraints: configured per installation

operands.name: rounding factors of the currencies
operands.source: the document currency and the company currency
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The quantity being stored is of one of the listed kinds.
preconditions.otherwise: The currency rounding factor governs it, every monetary amount being rounded to its own currency.

procedure: Round a line unit price at the decimal precision named for product prices, respecting a minimum display precision.
Round a line quantity at the decimal precision named for product units.
Round a line discount at the decimal precision named for discounts.
Compare payment term percentages at the decimal precision named for payment terms, which is the precision the constraint that they must sum to one hundred uses.
Round every monetary amount in the document currency at that currency's rounding factor.
Round every monetary amount in the company currency at that currency's rounding factor.
Compare deductibility at two decimal digits.
Apply cash rounding at the rule's own rounding precision and then at the currency's rounding factor.
Perform the currency conversion of a product price without rounding, and round only when the value is stored.
records.formula:
precision( line unit price )                      = the product price decimal precision, with a minimum display precision
precision( line quantity )                        = the product unit decimal precision
precision( line discount )                        = the discount decimal precision
precision( payment term percentage )              = the payment terms decimal precision
precision( monetary amount in document currency ) = the document currency's rounding factor
precision( monetary amount in company currency )  = the company currency's rounding factor
precision( deductibility comparison )             = two decimal digits
precision( cash rounding )                        = the rule's rounding precision, then the currency's rounding factor
precision( currency conversion of a product price ) = none during the conversion, the currency's rounding factor at storage

rounding.what: Every quantity the domain stores or compares.
rounding.precision: As listed above, one precision per kind of quantity.
rounding.method: Half away from zero for monetary amounts and for stored quantities; the cash rounding rule's own method for the cash rounding step.
rounding.step: At storage for computed values, at comparison for the constraints, and never during a currency conversion of a product price.

result.name: the precision governing a quantity
result.unit_or_currency: counts of decimal digits and currency rounding factors
result.stored_or_displayed: Applied wherever the corresponding quantity is stored, compared or displayed.

edge_cases.case: A currency has a rounding factor of five hundredths.
edge_cases.outcome: Every monetary amount in that currency is a multiple of five hundredths, independently of any cash rounding rule.

edge_cases.case: A payment term's percentages sum to one hundred only at a coarser precision.
edge_cases.outcome: The constraint uses the payment terms decimal precision, so the term is accepted or refused at that precision and not at any other.

edge_cases.case: A product price is converted between currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion is not rounded, and only the stored unit price is.

edge_cases.case: A deductibility of 99.995 per cent is entered.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison at two decimal digits treats it as one hundred, so no private-share line is generated.

worked_examples.description: A monetary amount in a currency of two decimal places

inputs.quantity_kind: a monetary amount in the document currency

worked_examples.narrative: The document currency's rounding factor governs, so the value is stored as 82.64.

worked_examples.description: A cash rounding under a rule of five hundredths
worked_examples.narrative: The rule's own precision is applied first and the currency's rounding factor afterwards, giving 23.90.

records.name: The four groups counted on the purchase journal card
records.purpose: Defines which documents each of the four figures of a purchase journal card counts, so that the card's counters can be reproduced exactly.

operands.name: documents of the journal
operands.source: the journal, restricted to the companies the reading user works in
operands.constraints: each group applies its own status, type and date filters

operands.name: payment status
operands.source: each document
operands.constraints: the waiting group keeps the statuses not paid and partial

operands.name: due date
operands.source: each document
operands.constraints: the late group keeps rows whose due date is strictly before today

operands.name: reviewed flag
operands.source: each document
operands.constraints: the review group keeps the documents whose flag is false

preconditions.condition: The journal is a purchase journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The card is built with the same shape but the sale conventions apply to the display.

preconditions.condition: The reading user may read the documents.
preconditions.otherwise: Only the readable documents are counted.

procedure: Count as drafts the documents of the journal, in the user's companies, whose status is draft and whose type is any invoice-like type, receipts included.
Count as waiting the documents of the journal that are posted, whose payment status is not paid or partial, and whose type is one of the three purchase types.
Count as late the rows of that same query whose due date is strictly before today.
Count as to review the documents of the journal that are posted and whose reviewed flag is false, with no type restriction at all, so that a miscellaneous entry of a purchase journal also counts.

Compute the waiting and the late numbers from a single query whose result rows carry a late indicator, the two groups being the rows where that indicator is true and the rows where the indicator saying the document is still to pay is true.
Compute all four groups in one pass over four queries.
records.formula:
drafts    = documents of the journal , in the user's companies , status draft , any invoice-like type
waiting   = documents of the journal , posted , payment status not_paid or partial , type in_invoice, in_refund or in_receipt
late      = the rows of the waiting query whose due date < today
to review = documents of the journal , posted , reviewed flag false , no type restriction

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the four figures are counts of documents.
rounding.precision: One document.

result.name: the four counts of the purchase journal card
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the card under the title that names the bills to pay, each count beside its formatted sum.

edge_cases.case: A miscellaneous entry sits in the purchase journal and has not been reviewed.
edge_cases.outcome: It is counted in the review group, which applies no type restriction.

edge_cases.case: A document is posted, unpaid and due today.
edge_cases.outcome: It is counted as waiting but not as late, the late test being strictly before today.

edge_cases.case: A document's payment status is blocked.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not counted as waiting, only the statuses not paid and partial being kept.

edge_cases.case: The journal holds no document at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The four counts are zero and the card offers the sample bill.

worked_examples.description: A purchase journal with a mixed population
worked_examples.narrative: One draft; two posted unpaid bills are waiting, of which the one due 1 August 2026 is late; the unreviewed miscellaneous entry is counted in the review group even though it is not a purchase type.

records.name: The document-currency amount of a draft row of the dashboard
records.purpose: Signs the total of a draft document so that credit notes reduce the drafts figure instead of inflating it.

operands.name: total of the document
operands.source: the draft document
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the draft document
operands.constraints: the two credit note types take minus one

preconditions.condition: The document is a draft of an invoice-like type.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not part of the drafts query.

procedure: Take the total of the document in its own currency.
Multiply it by minus one when the type is a customer credit note or a vendor credit note, and by plus one otherwise.
Carry the result in the query row, together with the currency, the type, the bill date and the company.
records.formula: row_amount = amount_total × ( −1 when the type is out_refund or in_refund, otherwise +1 )

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded; the total was already rounded to the document currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the total was computed.

result.name: signed document-currency amount of the row
result.stored_or_displayed: Carried in the query row and converted into the target currency when the row's company currency differs from it.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is negated, so it reduces the drafts figure.

edge_cases.case: The document is a purchase receipt.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is plus one, receipts not being credit notes.

edge_cases.case: The draft sum is displayed.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not negated again at display time, because the query has already signed it.

worked_examples.description: A draft bill and a draft vendor credit note
worked_examples.narrative: The credit note is negated, so the drafts figure reads one thousand euros rather than one thousand four hundred.

records.name: The company-currency amount of a draft row of the dashboard
records.purpose: Signs the company-currency total of a draft document so that the figure can be summed directly whenever the row's company currency is the currency the card is shown in.

operands.name: signed total of the document
operands.source: the draft document
operands.constraints: negative on a vendor bill, the ledger seeing a credit on the payable side

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the draft document
operands.constraints: the three purchase types take minus one

preconditions.condition: The document is a draft of an invoice-like type.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not part of the drafts query.

procedure: Take the signed total of the document in the company currency.
Multiply it by minus one when the type is a vendor bill, a vendor credit note or a purchase receipt, and by plus one otherwise.
Carry the result in the query row.
records.formula: row_amount_company = amount_total_signed × ( −1 when the type is in_invoice, in_refund or in_receipt, otherwise +1 )

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded; the signed total was already rounded to the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the signed total was computed.

result.name: signed company-currency amount of the row
result.stored_or_displayed: Carried in the query row and summed directly when the row's company currency equals the target currency.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: Its signed total is negative and the extra minus one makes the row positive, so a draft bill adds to the figure.

edge_cases.case: The document is a sale document in a purchase journal.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is plus one and the signed total is used as it stands.

edge_cases.case: The row's company currency differs from the target currency.
edge_cases.outcome: This figure is not used; the document-currency amount is converted instead.

worked_examples.description: A draft bill of one thousand two hundred euros in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The signed total of a bill is negative, and the extra minus one turns it into the positive figure the card shows.

records.name: The grouped sums of the waiting and late query
records.purpose: Aggregates what is still owed on the posted purchase documents of a journal, in both currencies, split by whether the document is late.

operands.name: signed residual of each document
operands.source: the posted purchase documents of the journal whose payment status is not paid or partial
operands.constraints: negative on an unpaid bill

operands.name: residual of each document
operands.source: the same documents
operands.constraints: positive on an unpaid bill

operands.name: document type
operands.source: each document
operands.constraints: a vendor bill takes minus one in the document-currency sum

operands.name: late indicator
operands.source: the comparison of the due date with today
operands.constraints: true when the due date is before today

preconditions.condition: The documents are posted and their payment status is not paid or partial.
preconditions.otherwise: They are not part of the query.

preconditions.condition: The documents are of one of the three purchase types.
preconditions.otherwise: They are not part of the query.

procedure: Sum the signed residuals of the group in the company currency.
Sum, in the document currency, each residual multiplied by minus one when the type is a vendor bill and by plus one otherwise.
Carry a row count alongside the two sums.
Group by company, journal, currency, the late indicator and the indicator saying the document is still to pay, so that a single query serves both the waiting figure and the late figure.
records.formula:
group_amount_company = Σ amount_residual_signed
group_amount         = Σ ( amount_residual × ( −1 when the type is in_invoice, otherwise +1 ) )

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded; the sums are of already rounded residuals.
rounding.precision: The rounding factors of the company currency and of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each residual was computed.

result.name: grouped residual sums and row count
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Converted into the target currency and displayed as the waiting and late sums of the purchase card, negated at display time.

edge_cases.case: A vendor credit note is unpaid.
edge_cases.outcome: Its residual is added with a sign of plus one in the document-currency sum, so it reduces the negated figure the card shows.

edge_cases.case: A document is due today.
edge_cases.outcome: The late indicator is false and the document contributes to the waiting figure only.

edge_cases.case: The group holds documents in several currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: The grouping includes the currency, so each currency forms its own row and is converted separately.

worked_examples.description: Two unpaid bills and one unpaid vendor credit note in the same currency
worked_examples.narrative: The late row carries one bill; the other row carries a bill of 500.00 and a credit note of 200.00, which nets to −300.00 in both currencies and reads as three hundred euros to pay once the card negates it.

records.name: The grouped sums of the review query
records.purpose: Aggregates the totals of the posted documents of a journal that have not yet been reviewed, in both currencies.

operands.name: signed total of each document
operands.source: the posted documents of the journal whose reviewed flag is false
operands.constraints: negative on a vendor bill

operands.name: total of each document
operands.source: the same documents
operands.constraints: positive on a vendor bill

operands.name: document type
operands.source: each document
operands.constraints: a vendor bill takes minus one in the document-currency sum

preconditions.condition: The documents are posted and their reviewed flag is false.
preconditions.otherwise: They are not part of the query.

procedure: Sum the signed totals of the group in the company currency.
Sum, in the document currency, each total multiplied by minus one when the type is a vendor bill and by plus one otherwise.
Use the same row shape and the same grouping as the waiting query, but over the totals rather than over the residuals.
Apply no type restriction, so that a miscellaneous entry of the journal is included.
records.formula:
group_amount_company = Σ amount_total_signed
group_amount         = Σ ( amount_total × ( −1 when the type is in_invoice, otherwise +1 ) )

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded; the sums are of already rounded totals.
rounding.precision: The rounding factors of the company currency and of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each total was computed.

result.name: grouped total sums and row count
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Converted into the target currency and displayed as the review figure of the purchase card.

edge_cases.case: A miscellaneous entry has not been reviewed.
edge_cases.outcome: It is included, the query applying no type restriction.

edge_cases.case: The reviewed flag is set by a user without the review authority.
edge_cases.outcome: The write is refused with the message that the user does not have the access rights to perform this action.

edge_cases.case: A document is fully paid but unreviewed.
edge_cases.outcome: It still contributes, the review query looking at the totals rather than at the residuals.

worked_examples.description: Two unreviewed posted bills
worked_examples.narrative: Two bills totalling 1 700.00 are awaiting review; both sums are negative and the card negates them for display.

records.name: The counter of a dashboard group
records.purpose: Turns the rows a dashboard query returns into the single count displayed beside a group of the purchase card.

operands.name: rows of the query
operands.source: one of the four dashboard queries
operands.constraints: each row may carry its own count

preconditions.condition: The query has returned rows.
preconditions.otherwise: The count is zero.

procedure: Take each row of the group.
Take the count the row carries, or one when the row carries none.
Sum those counts.
records.formula: count = Σ over rows of the row's count ( 1 when absent )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the counter is a whole number.
rounding.precision: One document.

result.name: counter of the group
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed beside the group's formatted sum on the purchase card.

edge_cases.case: The query returns grouped rows carrying counts.
edge_cases.outcome: Those counts are summed rather than the rows themselves.

edge_cases.case: The query returns one row per document.
edge_cases.outcome: Each row contributes one.

edge_cases.case: No row is returned.
edge_cases.outcome: The counter is zero.

worked_examples.description: A waiting group of two grouped rows
worked_examples.narrative: Five documents are waiting to be paid across the two currency rows.

records.name: The sum of a dashboard group converted into the target currency
records.purpose: Turns rows expressed in several currencies into the single amount displayed for a group of the purchase card, converting only where a conversion is actually needed.

operands.name: target currency
operands.source: the journal's currency when it has one, otherwise the journal's company's currency
operands.constraints: always resolvable

operands.name: company-currency amount of each row
operands.source: the query row
operands.constraints: used as it stands when the row's company currency equals the target currency

operands.name: document-currency amount of each row
operands.source: the query row
operands.constraints: converted when the row's company currency differs from the target currency

operands.name: conversion date
operands.source: the row's bill date, falling back to today
operands.constraints: used to read the rate

preconditions.condition: The journal has a currency, or its company has one.
preconditions.otherwise: No target currency can be resolved and no sum can be shown.

procedure: Resolve the target currency: the journal's currency when it has one, otherwise the journal's company's currency.
For each row, take the company-currency amount as it stands when the row's company currency equals the target currency.
Otherwise convert the row's document-currency amount from the row's currency into the target currency, at the row's bill date or today.
Sum the amounts so obtained.
Round the sum to the target currency.
records.formula:
sum = Σ over rows of:
        row_amount_company                                                              when the row's company currency equals the target currency
        convert( row_amount , row_currency → target , at the row's bill date or today ) otherwise

rounding.what: The converted amounts and the final sum.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the target currency.
rounding.step: At each conversion and once more on the total, before the figure is displayed.

result.name: sum of the group in the target currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Formatted and displayed on the purchase card, negated for the waiting and late groups.

edge_cases.case: Every row is in the target currency.
edge_cases.outcome: No conversion is performed and the company-currency amounts are summed directly.

edge_cases.case: A row has no bill date.
edge_cases.outcome: Today's rate is used for the conversion.

edge_cases.case: The journal carries a currency of its own.
edge_cases.outcome: That currency is the target, so a foreign-currency journal shows its own currency rather than the company's.

worked_examples.description: Two rows, one in the target currency and one to convert
worked_examples.narrative: The first row is already in euros; the second is converted at the rate of its bill date, and the sum of −1 695.00 is negated for display so that the card reads one thousand six hundred and ninety-five euros to pay.

records.name: The display of the purchase journal card
records.purpose: States what the purchase card finally shows, including the negation that makes an amount owed read as a positive figure and the three indicators that flag a journal needing attention.

operands.name: the four counts
operands.source: the counter rule applied to each group
operands.constraints: zero or more

operands.name: the four sums
operands.source: the sum rule applied to each group
operands.constraints: already converted and rounded

operands.name: journal kind
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: the negation applies to a purchase journal and not to a sale journal

operands.name: numbering holes, hashing state and document count
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: drive the three indicators

preconditions.condition: The journal is a purchase journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The waiting and late sums are shown as written, without the negation.

procedure: Show the title naming the bills to pay, the four counts and the four formatted sums.
Negate the waiting sum and the late sum for a purchase journal, so that an amount owed to suppliers reads as a positive figure; show them as written for a sale journal.
Do not negate the draft sum, because the drafts query has already signed it.

Show the irregular-sequences indicator when the journal has at least one numbering hole, with the hint that the irregularities are due to draft, cancelled or deleted bills with a sequence number since the last lock date.
Show the unhashed-entries indicator when the journal secures entries with a hash and at least one posted entry is not yet hashed.
Show the sample-data indicator when the journal has no document at all, the card then offering the sample bill.
records.formula:
displayed waiting sum = − sum( waiting )   for a purchase journal
displayed late sum    = − sum( late )      for a purchase journal
displayed draft sum   = sum( drafts )      unchanged, the query having already signed it

rounding.what: The displayed sums, formatted in the target currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding factor of the target currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the sums were computed.
rounding.step: At display time, after the negation.

result.name: the purchase journal card
result.unit_or_currency: the target currency and counts of documents
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the journal's card, with its four counts, its four sums and its three indicators.

edge_cases.case: The journal is a sale journal.
edge_cases.outcome: The waiting and late sums are shown as written, without the negation.

edge_cases.case: The journal has a numbering hole.
edge_cases.outcome: The irregular-sequences indicator appears with its hint.

edge_cases.case: The journal secures entries with a hash and one posted entry is unhashed.
edge_cases.outcome: The unhashed-entries indicator appears.

edge_cases.case: The journal is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The sample-data indicator appears and the card offers the sample bill.

worked_examples.description: A purchase journal with one thousand seven hundred euros unpaid, of which twelve hundred are late
worked_examples.narrative: The waiting and late sums are negated so that they read as positive amounts owed, while the draft sum is shown as the query produced it.

records.name: The staggered fiscal year test of the numbering pattern
records.purpose: Decides whether the company's financial year ends anywhere other than the last day of December, which is what makes the numbering carry a two-year label instead of a single year.

operands.name: fiscal year end month
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: between one and twelve

operands.name: fiscal year end day
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: between one and thirty-one

preconditions.condition: The company declares a fiscal year end day and month.
preconditions.otherwise: The calendar year is assumed and the test answers false.

procedure: Compare the fiscal year end month with December.
Compare the fiscal year end day with the thirty-first.
Answer true when either of the two differs, and false when both match.
records.formula: staggered = ( M ≠ 12 ) or ( L ≠ 31 )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the answer is a true or false value.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: staggered flag
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it selects which of the two year-part rules builds the numbering pattern, and it also shortens the running number of a sale, bank, cash or credit card journal from five digits to four.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of December.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is false and the year part is the plain four-digit year.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends on the thirtieth of June.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is true and the year part is a two-year label.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends on the thirtieth of December.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is true, because the day differs even though the month does not.

worked_examples.description: A company whose financial year ends on the thirtieth of June
worked_examples.narrative: The month is not December, so the year is staggered and the numbering carries a two-year label.

worked_examples.description: A company on the calendar year
worked_examples.narrative: Both parts match, so the year is not staggered.

records.name: The year part of the numbering pattern for a calendar fiscal year
records.purpose: Supplies the year label of the first number of a journal when the financial year is the calendar year.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the accounting date of the document, falling back to its bill date, falling back to today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

preconditions.condition: The company's fiscal year is not staggered.
preconditions.otherwise: The two-year label applies.

procedure: Take the reference date, that is the accounting date, or the bill date, or today.
Take the four digits of its year as the year part.
records.formula: year_part = the four digits of the year of d

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the year part is a four-character text.
rounding.precision: One year.

result.name: year part of the pattern
result.stored_or_displayed: Inserted into the numbering pattern of the journal.

edge_cases.case: The document has no accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: The bill date is used, and today when it has neither.

edge_cases.case: The accounting date has been shifted by the period rules.
edge_cases.outcome: The shifted date is what fixes the year part, so a bill moved to the last day of the previous month keeps that month's year.

worked_examples.description: A bill dated the fifth of May 2026 in a company on the calendar year
worked_examples.narrative: The year part is the plain four-digit year.

records.name: The year part of the numbering pattern when the date falls after the fiscal year end
records.purpose: Supplies the two-year label of the first number of a journal when the financial year is staggered and the document belongs to the year that has just opened.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the accounting date of the document, falling back to its bill date, falling back to today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

operands.name: fiscal year end month
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: between one and twelve

operands.name: fiscal year end day
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: clamped to the length of that month in the year of the reference date

preconditions.condition: The company's fiscal year is staggered.
preconditions.otherwise: The plain four-digit year applies.

preconditions.condition: The reference date is strictly later than the fiscal year end of its own year, after clamping.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant for a date on or before the fiscal year end applies.

procedure: Clamp the fiscal year end day to the number of days that month has in the year of the reference date.
Form the fiscal year end date from the year of the reference date, the fiscal year end month and the clamped day.
Compare the reference date with that date.
When the reference date is later, build the label from the last two digits of its year, a hyphen, and the last two digits of the following year.
records.formula:
L' = min( L , number_of_days( year of d , M ) )
year_part = "«last two digits of the year of d»-«last two digits of the year of d plus one»"   when d > date( year of d , M , L' )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the fiscal year end day is clamped to the length of its month.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.method: The clamp takes the smaller of the declared day and the length of the month.
rounding.step: Before the comparison with the reference date.

result.name: year part of the pattern
result.stored_or_displayed: Inserted into the numbering pattern of the journal.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year end day is the thirty-first and the month is shorter.
edge_cases.outcome: The clamp reduces it to the length of that month.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year end falls on the twenty-ninth of February in a common year.
edge_cases.outcome: The clamp reduces it to the twenty-eighth.

edge_cases.case: The reference date is exactly the fiscal year end.
edge_cases.outcome: This rule does not apply, the comparison being strict; the other variant does.

worked_examples.description: A bill of the twelfth of September 2026 in a company whose year ends on the thirtieth of June
worked_examples.narrative: The date falls after the close of the financial year, so the label runs from the current year to the next and reads twenty-six hyphen twenty-seven.

records.name: The year part of the numbering pattern when the date falls on or before the fiscal year end
records.purpose: Supplies the two-year label of the first number of a journal when the financial year is staggered and the document still belongs to the year that is closing.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the accounting date of the document, falling back to its bill date, falling back to today
operands.constraints: never empty by construction

operands.name: fiscal year end month
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: between one and twelve

operands.name: fiscal year end day
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: clamped to the length of that month in the year of the reference date

preconditions.condition: The company's fiscal year is staggered.
preconditions.otherwise: The plain four-digit year applies.

preconditions.condition: The reference date is on or before the fiscal year end of its own year, after clamping.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant for a date after the fiscal year end applies.

procedure: Clamp the fiscal year end day to the number of days that month has in the year of the reference date.
Form the fiscal year end date from the year of the reference date, the fiscal year end month and the clamped day.
Compare the reference date with that date.
When the reference date is not later, build the label from the last two digits of the preceding year, a hyphen, and the last two digits of the year of the reference date.
records.formula:
L' = min( L , number_of_days( year of d , M ) )
year_part = "«last two digits of the year of d minus one»-«last two digits of the year of d»"  otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the fiscal year end day is clamped to the length of its month.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.method: The clamp takes the smaller of the declared day and the length of the month.
rounding.step: Before the comparison with the reference date.

result.name: year part of the pattern
result.stored_or_displayed: Inserted into the numbering pattern of the journal.

edge_cases.case: The reference date is exactly the fiscal year end.
edge_cases.outcome: This rule applies, since the comparison that selects the other variant is strict.

edge_cases.case: The reference date is in January of a year whose financial year ends in June.
edge_cases.outcome: The label runs from the previous year to the current one.

worked_examples.description: A bill of the third of March 2026 in a company whose year ends on the thirtieth of June

expected_outputs.comparison: 3 March 2026 is not later than 30 June 2026

worked_examples.narrative: The bill still belongs to the financial year that opened in 2025, so the label reads twenty-five hyphen twenty-six.

records.name: The starting numbering pattern of a purchase journal
records.purpose: Assembles the pattern from which the first number of a purchase journal is derived, which carries the journal code, the year part, the month and a four-digit running number.

operands.name: journal code
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: a short code written as it stands

operands.name: year part
operands.source: one of the three year-part rules
operands.constraints: four characters for a calendar year, five for a staggered one

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the accounting date, falling back to the bill date, falling back to today
operands.constraints: its month supplies the two-digit month of the pattern

preconditions.condition: The journal is of a type other than sale, bank, cash and credit card, which includes every purchase journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The pattern of those four types applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The journal does not use self-billing.
preconditions.otherwise: The self-billing pattern applies.

procedure: Take the journal code.
Append an oblique stroke and the year part.
Append an oblique stroke and the two-digit month of the reference date.
Append an oblique stroke and four zeros, which is the running number at its starting value.

Prefix the whole with the letter that marks a credit note in a journal with a separate refund sequence, the letter that marks a payment's entry in a journal with a separate payment sequence, or the letter that marks a debit note in a journal with a dedicated debit note sequence, when one of those applies.
records.formula: pattern = «code»/«year part»/«two-digit month of d»/0000

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the running number is padded with zeros to four characters.
rounding.precision: One unit.

result.name: starting numbering pattern
result.stored_or_displayed: Used to derive the first number the journal assigns; a number that does not match the journal's numbering override pattern is refused for a user who is not an accounting manager.

edge_cases.case: The company's fiscal year is staggered.
edge_cases.outcome: The year part is the five-character two-year label, the running number staying at four digits for a purchase journal.

edge_cases.case: The document is a credit note in a journal with a separate refund sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: The pattern is prefixed with the letter that marks a refund sequence.

edge_cases.case: The document is a debit note in a journal with a dedicated debit note sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: The pattern is prefixed with the letter that marks a debit note sequence.

worked_examples.description: A purchase journal coded with four letters in a company whose year ends on the thirtieth of June
worked_examples.narrative: The first bill of that month is numbered with the running number one padded to four digits.

worked_examples.description: The same journal for a bill of the third of March 2026
worked_examples.narrative: The earlier date belongs to the financial year that opened in 2025, so the label differs while the shape of the pattern does not.

records.name: The starting numbering pattern of a sale, bank, cash or credit card journal
records.purpose: States the pattern of the four journal types that number by year rather than by month, recorded here because the same assembly rule serves every journal type.

operands.name: journal code
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: a short code written as it stands

operands.name: year part
operands.source: one of the three year-part rules
operands.constraints: four characters for a calendar year, five for a staggered one

operands.name: staggered flag
operands.source: the staggered fiscal year test
operands.constraints: it shortens the running number from five digits to four

preconditions.condition: The journal is of the sale, bank, cash or credit card type.
preconditions.otherwise: The pattern that carries a month applies instead.

procedure: Take the journal code.
Append an oblique stroke and the year part.
Append an oblique stroke and five zeros, or four zeros when the fiscal year is staggered.
Prefix the whole with the appropriate letter when a separate refund, payment or debit note sequence applies.
records.formula:
pattern = «code»/«year part»/00000
pattern = «code»/«year part»/0000     when the year is staggered

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the running number is padded with zeros.
rounding.precision: One unit.

result.name: starting numbering pattern
result.stored_or_displayed: Used to derive the first number the journal assigns.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year is staggered.
edge_cases.outcome: The running number is four digits rather than five, the two extra characters of the year label taking the place of one digit.

edge_cases.case: The journal is a bank journal printing cheques.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry numbering follows this pattern, while the cheque numbers come from the journal's own cheque sequence and are unrelated.

worked_examples.description: A bank journal in a company on the calendar year
worked_examples.narrative: The running number has five digits because the year is not staggered.

worked_examples.description: The same journal in a company whose year ends in June
worked_examples.narrative: The staggered year shortens the running number to four digits.

records.name: The starting numbering pattern of a self-billing purchase journal
records.purpose: Assembles the pattern of a journal in which the company issues the document on the supplier's behalf, so that the numbering carries the supplier's identifier and each supplier keeps its own series.

operands.name: journal code
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: a short code written as it stands

operands.name: commercial partner identifier
operands.source: the commercial partner of the document
operands.constraints: padded to five characters with leading zeros

operands.name: year part
operands.source: one of the three year-part rules
operands.constraints: four characters for a calendar year, five for a staggered one

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the accounting date, falling back to the bill date, falling back to today
operands.constraints: its month supplies the two-digit month

preconditions.condition: The journal uses self-billing.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary pattern of its type applies.

preconditions.condition: The document has a commercial partner with an identifier.
preconditions.otherwise: No supplier-specific series can be formed.

procedure: Take the journal code and append the commercial partner's identifier padded to five characters with leading zeros, with no separator between them.
Append an oblique stroke and the year part.
Append an oblique stroke and the two-digit month of the reference date.
Append an oblique stroke and four zeros.
records.formula: pattern = «code»«partner identifier padded to five with zeros»/«year part»/«two-digit month of d»/0000

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the identifier is padded to five characters and the running number to four.
rounding.precision: One unit.

result.name: starting numbering pattern
result.stored_or_displayed: Used to derive the first number of that supplier's own series in the self-billing journal.

edge_cases.case: The partner identifier has more than five digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The padding adds nothing and the identifier is written in full.

edge_cases.case: Two suppliers are billed in the same self-billing journal.
edge_cases.outcome: Each has its own series, because the identifier is part of the pattern.

worked_examples.description: A self-billing purchase journal in a company on the calendar year
worked_examples.narrative: The identifier four hundred and twelve is padded to five characters and joined directly to the journal code, so this supplier's documents form their own monthly series.

records.name: The prefix letters of a separate numbering sequence
records.purpose: Marks a numbering series that is kept apart from the journal's ordinary one, so that credit notes, payment entries and debit notes can be numbered independently.

operands.name: document kind
operands.source: the document being numbered
operands.constraints: a credit note, a payment's entry or a debit note

operands.name: journal sequence configuration
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: the prefix applies only when the journal keeps a separate sequence for that kind

preconditions.condition: The journal keeps a separate sequence for the kind of document being numbered.
preconditions.otherwise: No prefix is added and the ordinary pattern is used.

procedure: Build the pattern of the journal's type.
Prefix it with the letter that marks a refund sequence when the document is a credit note in a journal with a separate refund sequence.
Prefix it with the letter that marks a payment sequence when the document is a payment's entry in a journal with a separate payment sequence.
Prefix it with the letter that marks a debit note sequence when the document is a debit note in a journal with a dedicated debit note sequence.
records.formula:
pattern = R + pattern     for a credit note in a journal with a separate refund sequence
pattern = P + pattern     for a payment's entry in a journal with a separate payment sequence
pattern = D + pattern     for a debit note in a journal with a dedicated debit note sequence

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the prefix is a single character.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: prefixed numbering pattern
result.stored_or_displayed: Used to derive the first number of the separate series.

edge_cases.case: The journal keeps no separate sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: No prefix is added and credit notes share the ordinary series.

edge_cases.case: A document is both a credit note and a debit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The case does not arise, a debit note against a credit note being created as a bill.

worked_examples.description: A vendor credit note in a purchase journal with a separate refund sequence
worked_examples.narrative: The refund prefix keeps the credit notes in a series of their own.

records.name: The similarity score between two incoming file names
records.purpose: Measures how alike two files delivered in the same message are, so that several representations of one supplier document are gathered onto a single bill.

operands.name: first file name
operands.source: a file attached to the incoming message
operands.constraints: compared character by character

operands.name: second file name
operands.source: another file of the same message
operands.constraints: compared character by character

preconditions.condition: The two files are candidates for the same group, that is their format labels do not clash.
preconditions.otherwise: They cannot be grouped and the score is not consulted.

procedure: Compare the two names character by character.
Find the longest run of characters that appears contiguously in both.
Answer the length of that run, counting every character, with no heuristic that would treat any character as insignificant.
records.formula: similarity( name_1 , name_2 ) = the length of the longest common contiguous substring of the two names

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the score is a count of characters.
rounding.precision: One character.

result.name: similarity score
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides which existing group an incoming file joins.

edge_cases.case: Two files share only their extension.
edge_cases.outcome: The score is the length of that shared run alone, which is small.

edge_cases.case: Two files share their whole name but not their extension.
edge_cases.outcome: The score is the length of the shared prefix including the point.

edge_cases.case: The files have no character in common.
edge_cases.outcome: The score is zero.

edge_cases.case: A character that a similarity heuristic would usually ignore appears in both names.
edge_cases.outcome: It still counts, the score being computed without any such heuristic.

worked_examples.description: Three files delivered in one message
worked_examples.narrative: The first two share fourteen characters, the run ending at the point before the extension; the image shares at most three characters with either, since the underscore run gives three and the point alone gives one.

records.name: Grouping incoming files into bills
records.purpose: Decides how many bills a message with several attachments creates, by letting a file join the most similar existing group unless that group already holds a file of the same format label.

operands.name: files of the message
operands.source: the incoming message
operands.constraints: walked in decreasing decoder priority

operands.name: format label of each file
operands.source: the file, only the Portable Document Format label being recognised by the base implementation
operands.constraints: two files of the same recognised label clash

operands.name: similarity scores
operands.source: the similarity rule applied between the incoming file and the files of each existing group
operands.constraints: the highest score wins

preconditions.condition: The message carries at least one file.
preconditions.otherwise: No bill is created from it.

procedure: Take the files in decreasing decoder priority, so that the file most likely to be decodable anchors each group.
Let the first file start a group.
For each further file, look at the existing groups and discard those that already hold a file of the same recognised format label.
Among the groups that remain, join the one with the highest similarity score.
Start a new group when no group remains.
Create one bill per group, carrying every file of that group.
records.formula:
a file joins the existing group with the highest similarity score among the groups that hold no file of the same recognised format label ; otherwise it starts a group of its own
number of bills = number of groups

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the decision is a comparison of character counts.
rounding.precision: One character.

result.name: the groups of files and the bills created from them
result.stored_or_displayed: Each group becomes one bill carrying every file of the group.

edge_cases.case: Two files carry the Portable Document Format label.
edge_cases.outcome: They clash and cannot share a group, so each anchors a bill of its own.

edge_cases.case: A file carries no recognised format label.
edge_cases.outcome: It never clashes and joins the group it is most similar to.

edge_cases.case: Five files all carry the Portable Document Format label.
edge_cases.outcome: Each starts its own group and five bills are created.

edge_cases.case: One supplier document arrives as a structured file, a printable file and a photograph.
edge_cases.outcome: The three land in one group and one bill is created carrying all three, which is the intended outcome.

worked_examples.description: One document delivered in three representations
worked_examples.narrative: The printable file and the structured file carry different format labels, so they do not clash and their similarity of fourteen puts them together; the image does not clash either and joins the group it is most similar to, which is that same group.

worked_examples.description: Five printable files in one message
worked_examples.narrative: The first file starts a group; the second finds that the only existing group already holds a file of that label, so it starts its own, and so on for the third, the fourth and the fifth, giving five groups and five bills.

records.name: The order in which incoming files are placed into groups
records.purpose: Fixes the order of the grouping walk, so that the file most likely to be decoded anchors each group and a file with no decoder attaches itself rather than creating a bill of its own.

operands.name: files of the message
operands.source: the incoming message
operands.constraints: each carries a decoder priority

operands.name: decoder priority of each file
operands.source: the decoders available for the file's format
operands.constraints: a file with no decoder ranks last

preconditions.condition: The message carries more than one file.
preconditions.otherwise: The single file forms one group and the order is immaterial.

procedure: Sort the files by decreasing decoder priority.
Place files with no decoder last.
Walk the sorted list, applying the grouping rule to each file in turn.
records.formula: order = the files sorted by decreasing decoder priority , files with no decoder last

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the order is a ranking.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.

result.name: the ordered list of files
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the grouping rule; the first file of each group is the one whose content is most likely to fill the bill.

edge_cases.case: A file has no decoder at all.
edge_cases.outcome: It is placed last and therefore attaches itself to an existing group rather than creating one, whenever its format label allows.

edge_cases.case: Two files have the same decoder priority.
edge_cases.outcome: They keep the order in which they arrived, the sort being on the priority alone.

edge_cases.case: Every file has a decoder.
edge_cases.outcome: The order is by priority and each group is anchored by its most decodable file.

worked_examples.description: A structured file, a printable file and a photograph
worked_examples.narrative: The structured file has the highest decoder priority and anchors the group; the photograph, having no decoder, comes last and attaches itself to that group.
